title: Jantar Mantar 2.0 — CJP / anti-SIR protest, Delhi
summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth movement, along with Left groups, student unions and civil-society groups, called a protest at Jantar Mantar, New Delhi, on Sat 10 Oct 2026. They want Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar to resign and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter rolls scrapped. Critics say SIR has removed more than 130 million names (NPR/AP). Delhi Police refused permission and locked down central Delhi: BNSS Sec 163 orders, about 45 metro stations shut until gates reopened around 10:36 PM, trains cancelled, internet cut within 4 km, and roughly 23,000 CAPF personnel deployed. Police detained CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on board their flight. YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was detained at his Gurugram home. Opposition leaders, lawyers and journalists were also detained. INDIA bloc street protests have been running since about 2 Oct, and Rahul Gandhi was detained on 6 and 7 Oct. As of 6:10 PM on 13 Oct 2026, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde were still detained. No release was reported. The Hindu (about 4:48 PM) said CJP accused Delhi Police of illegal detention and of denying lawyers, and called for their release. Times of India (about 5:52 PM), citing ANI, reported Abhijeet Dipke saying police were not letting lawyers meet them and calling that kidnapping. He said Ratna Singh had just told him the three were kept separately. That is his account. Police were not quoted in reply. Dipke himself was in Hingoli, Maharashtra, for his grandmother's last rites. He said he would reach Delhi on Wednesday, and that if Jantar Mantar stays shut, protest sites would come up across the country. His words, via PTI. The INDIA bloc tea at 5 Sunehri Bagh Road was held. Leaders then addressed the media. Rahul Gandhi said they would challenge the removal of Jantar Mantar as a protest site and that they would not stop. The Delhi High Court issued notice on three prayers in the Youth Congress plea and listed the matter for 17 Nov. The government opposed notice and said the plea cannot stand unless the de-notification is challenged. The Hindu headlined that Delhi Police blocked AISF and AIYF from protesting. AISF said the agitation would continue. The Supreme Court protest cluster remains listed for Thursday 15 Oct. That date was not reported as a listing of the Gandhi Special Intensive Revision petition.

stats.label: Detained in Delhi today (media)
stats.note: The Hindu (6:53 PM) restates that over 5,000 protesters were detained in Delhi, including CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, CPI(M) leaders and student activists. Delhi Police said at 6:53 PM they have begun releasing detainees (a senior officer via The Hindu); no count of releases given. NDTV (7:41 PM, with PTI inputs): over 1,500 detained across Delhi; many were released later in the evening. Scroll (8:16 PM): police reportedly detained more than 7,000 protesters in Delhi. NDTV (~10 PM): at least 3,000 detained across Delhi; most released by night. Delhi Police sources via ANI (9:38 PM): all detainees released from detention centres except CJP leaders, for whom due legal process will be followed. As of 10:05 PM. ThePrint (5:28 PM): around 3,500 detained in Delhi; police say detentions could last 'up to 24 hours'. Officials told PTI at 4:53 PM that Delhi Police detained over 3,000 people during the protest (The Hindu's summary says 3,300; The Tribune says 3,000). A Delhi Police officer told The Hindu around 5,000 were detained till 2 PM. TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee claimed (ANI, ~5:07 PM) about 2,500 were detained. A Delhi Police officer told The Hindu around 5,000 protesters were detained across Delhi till 2 PM and taken to temporary detention facilities (The Hindu live blog, 2:57 PM entry; Scroll repeated it at ~4:45 PM). Earlier figures: TOI 1,500+ (midday); PTI citing police sources ~1,000 (3:57 PM). Outside Delhi: Chennai 100+ (NDTV, ~4:22 PM); Bengaluru at least 50 AISA students at Freedom Park (The Hindu, 3:21 PM); Mumbai: over 400 detained so far at August Kranti Maidan (Mumbai Police via ANI, 5:39 PM; PTI had ~200 at 5:18 PM); actor Imran Khan and his relative Zayn Marie Khan were among those detained (NDTV, 8:30 PM); Pune: about 80–100 detained at Lal Mahal Chowk and taken to Lashkar police station (IANS, 8:46 PM); earlier Scroll reported detentions with no number. HT (10:47 PM): police say nearly 4,000 detained. As of 11:10 PM. NDTV (12:12 AM headline): at least 3,000 were detained in Delhi and all of them were released except the CJP leaders and Dhruv Rathee. NDTV also reports at least 25,000 police and paramilitary personnel were deployed. As of 12:15 AM. Over 7,000 released per police sources (DNA, 8:00 AM; ET Now, ~7:19 AM). ET Now says all 7,000 were released except Abhijeet Dipke, Dhruv Rathee and two others. DNA, citing police sources, says Dipke and Das remain in custody. CJP claims more than 15,000 people, including students, civil society members and political leaders, faced detention and police action (Indian Express; CJP claim). Police sources told Indian Express that detainees were kept at around 30 detention centres. As of 8:15 AM. Correction, 10:05 AM: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released at about 10 AM on an Executive Magistrate's order (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). Dhruv Rathee was released at about 3 AM (Hindustan Times, PTI). That corrects the morning reports that still had them in custody. As of 10:05 AM. HT (11:40 AM, 11 Oct): an estimated 7,000 people were detained on Saturday. As of 12:05 PM. 11 Oct: about 60–70 people were detained at Connaught Place (Indian Express, 12:28 PM), and The Hindu reported student activists detained there later. No official count for Sunday. As of 2:05 PM. Police sources, via The Hindu (3:38 PM, 11 Oct), say over 7,000 protesters were detained on Saturday as authorities stopped people reaching Jantar Mantar. Attributed to police sources, not an official figure. Hindustan Times (3:24 PM): about 100 more protesters were packed into two buses and removed from Connaught Place, and detentions there continued despite the Supreme Court order. HT also says more than 26,000 security personnel were deployed alongside Delhi Police. As of 4:05 PM. PTI (4:08 PM): more than 100 people were detained in Delhi on Sunday while marching toward Jantar Mantar. Tribune/PTI (5:46 PM): dozens, including Anjali Damania, were detained at Shivaji Park in Mumbai, and about 600 people had been detained in Mumbai on Saturday. AAP's Sanjay Singh claims more than 6,000 people were detained in Delhi on Saturday (PTI, 4:57 PM). His claim. As of 6:10 PM. Sunday evening: Indian Express reported many fresh detentions at Connaught Place, including women held in large numbers near Rajiv Chowk Metro Gate 7. No official count for Sunday evening. As of 8:10 PM. Goa: Times of India (7:16 PM) and The Hindu/PTI reported dozens detained at Azad Maidan, including CJP leader Amreen Shaikh. The Bombay High Court (Goa bench) later ordered those Panaji detainees released. Times of India and The Goan name seven: Jack Sukhija, Amreen Shaikh (Times of India spells the name Afreen), Aditya Parulekar, Bhupesh Bind, Liston Noronha, Shamiro or Shamino Fernandes, and Milind Rane. PTI and India Today say six. Both counts are kept. The Goan says they were released around 9:40 PM. As of 6:00 AM, 12 Oct.

stats.label: Detained nationwide (CJP claim)
stats.note: Figure from CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka on 8–9 Oct, before the protest. Not verified independently.

stats.label: SFI members detained (SFI claim)
stats.note: SFI national president Adarsh M Saji told PTI more than 400 members were detained after their march began around 10 AM. Not verified independently.

stats.label: Released today
stats.note: A group of lawyers detained near the Supreme Court were released after the CJI stepped in (about 2:30 PM). Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat was released (Bar & Bench, 6:51 PM). Pinarayi Vijayan was released (PTI, ~7:10 PM). ANI reported Ratna Singh's release at about 5:53 PM, but The Hindu says she posted at 7:13 PM that she was still detained; the reports conflict. 6:53 PM: Delhi Police say they have initiated the release of protesters (a senior officer via The Hindu); no count given. 7:11 PM: women released from Maidan Garhi police station (The Wire). 7:38 PM: police sources say women and senior citizens are being released first (The Hindu); many detainees were released in the evening (NDTV). 8:09 PM: Mamata Banerjee released (ANI). 8:13 PM: Arvind Kejriwal released from Jaffarpur police station (PTI). 8:30 PM: Neha Bora and the women detained with her released from Maidan Garhi police station (India Today). No overall release count given. 9:18 PM: police sources say most of those detained today have been released (IANS). 9:38 PM: Delhi Police sources say all detainees were released from detention centres except CJP leaders (ANI). 9:20 PM: Pinarayi Vijayan, John Brittas and K.N. Balagopal released from Mandir Marg police station (IANS). 9:35 PM: Yogendra Yadav says he was released from Maidangarhi police station (his own post). 9:59 PM: about 150 people picked up from Gurudwara Bangla Sahib were released from Chhatrasal Stadium (Scroll). No overall release count given. 11 Oct: Dhruv Rathee released at about 3 AM and handed to his family (Hindustan Times, PTI, citing officials). Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka released at about 10 AM on an Executive Magistrate's order at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, citing Ratna Singh; Bar & Bench).

stats.label: Named key figures still held
stats.note: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released at about 10 AM on 11 Oct on an Executive Magistrate's order at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:58 AM, citing Ratna Singh; Bar & Bench, 10:00 AM). Dhruv Rathee was released at about 3 AM and handed to his family (Hindustan Times and PTI, citing officials). This corrects earlier "still in custody" reports, including ETV Bharat, ET Now and this page's 8:15 AM update. Senior Advocate Dinesh Dwivedi: no new report. Ratna Singh was at the production as CJP's lawyer; an outlet has not confirmed when her own detention ended. Fidal Tom and students Saurabh, Nikhil and Harsh were released overnight (The Wire). The earlier "at least 12" figure counted named people whose individual status was already unconfirmed or likely released. As of 10:05 AM IST. The three were released on a one-year condition that they not breach the peace, with a Rs 50,000 surety, according to LiveLaw citing Ratna Singh, PTI, and Delhi Police via ANI. Dhruv Rathee later said he was kidnapped and gave no undertaking (Hindustan Times, his claim). The Hindu says he was released around 2 AM; HT and PTI say about 3 AM. As of 12:05 PM IST. John Brittas was detained again at about 1 PM on 11 Oct at Connaught Place (Indian Express). Dipke is travelling home to Hingoli; his family says a police delay made him miss his grandmother's funeral, and police dispute that. Das and Ranka were due at a 2 PM press conference. As of 2:05 PM IST. Neha Bora was detained again at about 3:50 PM on 11 Oct while leading a march to Connaught Place (ThePrint, Scroll). John Brittas was later released; CPI(M) alleges police assaulted him and left him injured (ThePrint, India Today). Ratna Singh is now confirmed released; she spoke at the Press Club press conference (The Hindu, 3:38 PM). Three Indian Express Hindi reporters were detained at Connaught Place, and two phones were seized (Indian Express, 3:57 PM). As of 4:05 PM IST. The three Indian Express Hindi reporters were released about 45 minutes later (Indian Express, 4:14 PM). Neha Bora was still reported detained as of 6:10 PM, with no release report. Anjali Damania was detained at about 4:50 PM at Shivaji Park, Mumbai (PTI). As of 6:10 PM IST. As of 8:10 PM, Neha Bora and Anjali Damania were still reported detained, with no release report for either. Dipke missed his grandmother's funeral and flew to Nagpur on the way to Hingoli. His uncle says the release came too late; police deny a delay. As of 10:10 PM, Neha Bora and Anjali Damania were still reported detained. Amreen Shaikh was detained at Azad Maidan and released around 9:40 PM on 11 Oct on a Bombay High Court (Goa bench) order (The Goan; PTI; Times of India). Dipke says he signed no bond against protesting; Ratna Singh's earlier account, via LiveLaw, is a one-year no-breach-of-peace condition. Both are kept. As of 6:00 AM on 12 Oct, Neha Bora's release is still unconfirmed. Sudhir Sangwan and Balakrishnan Shukla: whereabouts unknown per CJP. Dipke is in Hingoli. As of 9:35 PM on 12 Oct, Dhruv Rathee's Monday claim of unofficial house arrest, in an India Today report updated at 12:16 PM from The Lallantop, is his claim. No police confirmation was found. He remains listed as released on 11 Oct.

detainees.name: Dhruv Rathee
detainees.who: YouTuber; flew in from Germany, joined CJP's Bengaluru protest on 8 Oct
detainees.when: 10 Oct, about 7:48 AM IST (police entered the flat, per The Hindu); CJP said about 8 AM
detainees.where: His parents' flat, Sector 56, Gurugram. The Hindu names the society as Central Park Vihar; HT names it Kendriya Vihar. Joint Delhi and Gurugram Police operation
detainees.reason: Police (via HT) say he refused requests not to travel to Delhi for a protest that had no permission
detainees.status: RELEASED (~3 AM, 11 Oct). ThePrint (2:18 PM): "I did not sign any bond, I did not sign any undertaking, I did not sign any condition for release." His words. Hindustan Times (11:47 AM) reports his Instagram caption: "I was not arrested or detained, I was KIDNAPPED." HT says he gave no undertaking to Gurugram Police. His claim. The Hindu (10:53 AM) says the Gurugram Crime Branch released him around 2 AM. HT and PTI, citing officials, say about 3 AM. Both times are kept. HT's 11:47 AM story says he was detained around 9:30 AM on Saturday. HT's earlier story said about 7:30 AM. Both accounts are kept. Hindustan Times, citing officials, says Dhruv Rathee was released at 3 AM on Sunday and handed over to his family. He had been picked up from his residence in Kendriya Vihar society, Gurugram Sector 56, around 7:30 AM on Saturday. An unnamed police officer, quoted by PTI, said: "He can be detained again, or further legal action might be taken if he tries to go to Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders." This corrects earlier reports that he was still in custody, including ETV Bharat (6:48 AM) and ET Now (~7:19 AM). Earlier account: Taken to an undisclosed place in Gurugram. No release reported NDTV (~10 PM) says he remained in custody, with Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Delhi Police sources (ANI, 9:38 PM) said detainees other than CJP leaders had been released. No outlet has reported a release as of 11:10 PM. NDTV (~10 PM) still has him in custody. Social claims of a release are unverified and contradicted by NDTV. Arvind Kejriwal (his own post, 10:03 PM) asked the Prime Minister where Dipke, Ranka, Rathee and Das are being held. HT (11:25 PM) says he is still held, with Dipke, Das and Ranka, while everyone else was released. NDTV says he remained in custody as of 12:15 AM. Social posts claiming he is out are unverified and contradicted by NDTV. LawBeat says a Supreme Court habeas plea also names him; Bar & Bench's report does not mention him (single source). That plea was filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, not by CJP. CJP says it did not file or approve it, and Bharti has sought to withdraw it. On 12 Oct, India Today (updated 12:16 PM), reporting what he told The Lallantop: he wants to join the INDIA bloc march but alleges about 50 police outside his residence, three or four cars following him, and threats that he would be picked up again if he went near a protest. Asked if this was house arrest, he said: "Unofficially, I would say so." His claim. No police confirmation was found as of 9:35 PM. He also said: "I am an Indian citizen, there is no visa issue for me." His words. This does not change the Sunday release.

image.alt: Dhruv Rathee speaking into a microphone.

detainees.name: Abhijeet Dipke
detainees.when: 10 Oct, about 10:30 AM IST (ThePrint live blog)
detainees.where: On board an Air India flight from Mumbai, just after landing at IGI Airport, Delhi. Later moved to Gurugram (TOI)
detainees.reason: Protest was banned / had no permission. No written grounds reported
detainees.status: RELEASED (~10 AM, 11 Oct). On X at 4:26 PM he wrote, "Haven't signed any bond that says we won't protest. We will hit the streets again." That is his statement (Indian Express, 5:11 PM). Separately, LiveLaw (10:20 AM), citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh, says the magistrate released him, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on condition they would not breach the peace for one year. PTI (10:54 AM) says they must "maintain peace" for one year. Delhi Police, via ANI (10:56 AM), say a surety of Rs 50,000 was taken for peace and good behaviour for one year. CJP says that bond only bars a breach of the peace, and that peaceful protest is a constitutional right. Both accounts are kept. He said CJP will hit the streets again. NDTV (5:56 PM): CJP vowed protests across the country. Delhi Police, at a press conference around 5:29 PM, released a video of officers telling him of his grandmother's death. DCP Neha Yadav (ANI, 5:38 PM) said officers offered all possible assistance, including flights and phone calls, and repeatedly asked if he wished to speak to his parents, but he declined. Hindustan Times says the clip shows him declining an offer to return home. That is the police account. CJP's Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das say he was denied permission to speak to his cousin, and they accuse the police of insensitivity. That is CJP's account. Both are kept. Hindustan Times names his grandmother as Savitribai Dipke and says she died on Saturday at the family home in Santuk Pimpri, and that he left for the village on Sunday. The Tribune, with PTI, reports that the last rites were held on Sunday morning and that he missed them. His uncle Vilas Dipke said he pleaded with Delhi Police at least 10 times to release him, and that the release came too late for the funeral. The family says he will be present to collect her ashes. Delhi Police deny any delay. They say he was informed and offered help to travel, and that he declined. Both accounts are kept. He flew to Nagpur and spoke there before going on to Hingoli (Tribune, 7:17 PM; PTI, 6:33 PM): "We will hit the streets again. We are not afraid of PM Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah ... Put me in jail a hundred times." His words. On X at 6:31 PM he said he had asked for his phone for a couple of minutes to get his cousin's number, and had asked to speak to a lawyer, and that both were refused. At 7:24 PM he wrote, "Why did you delete the part where I was asking for my phone ... and where I was asking to let me speak to my lawyers?" He accuses police of editing the clip. His claim. State Mirror, quoting him via Neha Bora's team account, says that at 3:30 AM police told him to call his father and say he was going to jail for a long time. That is his account. PTI (7:52 PM) describes the police video: a woman officer offered transport, and he repeatedly said "I'll stay." An Executive Magistrate ordered the release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:58 AM, citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh; Bar & Bench, 10:00 AM, which reports them released). This corrects earlier reports, including this page's 8:15 AM update, that they were still in custody. LiveLaw (10:20 AM), citing Ratna Singh, says they were released on condition they will not engage in a breach of the peace for one year. PTI (10:54 AM) says the condition is that they "maintain peace" for one year. Delhi Police, via ANI (10:56 AM), say the preventive arrest was under BNSS Sections 126 and 170 on 10 Oct 2026, that all due legal procedures were followed, that they were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate's court at Delhi Cantt, and that a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was taken. That is the police account. CJP counsel Soutik Banerjee said at 10:18 AM that all three had been released (LiveLaw). Indian Express (10:51 AM) says they walked out of Delhi Cantt police station. Delhi Police had placed the three under preventive arrest under BNSS Sections 126 (security for keeping the peace) and 170 (arrest to prevent the commission of cognisable offences) (LiveLaw, 8:23 AM; Bar & Bench, 8:32 AM; PTI, 9:10 AM; Indian Express, 9:34 AM). They were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate, South West District, at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:35 AM; Bar & Bench, 9:39 AM; ANI video, 9:51 AM). India Today (9:00 AM, police sources) had said that no arrests had been made. His mother, Anita Dipke, said he was not allowed to attend his grandmother's funeral (PTI video, 11:12 AM). PTI (12:40 PM) and Indian Express (1:02 PM): his paternal grandmother, Savitribai Shankarrao Dipke, 85, died on Saturday in Hingoli district, Maharashtra, after a prolonged illness, and the last rites were performed on Sunday morning. He missed them. The family says Delhi Police did not release him in time despite repeated pleas. Delhi Police said he was informed and offered help to travel home; his uncle Vilas Dipke disputed that. PTI video (12:46 PM), as he left Kapil Sibal's residence: "I am going home now to be with my family, as my grandmother has passed away. Ashutosh and Saurav will hold a press conference at 2 pm and announce the future course of action... The entire Delhi was brought to a standstill to protect Gyanesh Kumar." His words. Hindustan Times (1:28 PM) says he is heading back to his village and that he says CJP will not back down. The Wire (12:57 PM) quotes him: "October 10 will go down as the beginning of the end of this dictatorship." His words. He was in Delhi until about 10 AM. After release he wrote, as reported by Hindustan Times and The Wire: "Modi, as PM, is an embarrassment to India. Never has this country seen a bigger coward and bully." His words. Hindustan Times says the three were held from inside the plane: flight AI 2428 landed at 10:18 AM on Saturday and was moved to remote bay R12 (people aware of the matter, per HT). Earlier account: CJP alleges he has no access to lawyers. His grandmother died in Hingoli the same day Police sources (PTI, ~4:06 PM) say he was told of his grandmother's death and left to decide whether to stay or go home for her last rites. Delhi Police (via ANI, ~4:26 PM) say he was offered help to travel home on humanitarian grounds for his grandmother's funeral. At 1:08 PM, intelligence sources told The Hindu that Dipke, Das and Ranka were taken to three different locations in Delhi-NCR. CJP said at ~4:45 PM it still has no information on Dipke, Das and Ranka's whereabouts and is concerned for their safety. 5:20 PM: CJP publicly appealed to Delhi Police to release Dipke immediately, saying his whereabouts are still unknown, his lawyers cannot reach him and his family cannot tell him of his grandmother's death (CJP claim). This conflicts with police sources earlier saying he was informed; both accounts are kept, attributed. Delhi Police (via IANS, 7:12 PM) say Dipke's grandmother's death was promptly conveyed to him with due sensitivity, he was told the funeral time, and he was offered all possible assistance to travel home. NDTV (7:41 PM) says that by evening it was not clear whether he would be released. CJP said at a 7:35 PM press conference it still has no information on the whereabouts of Dipke, Das and Ranka (The Hindu). Police sources (The Hindu, 7:38 PM) say due legal process will be followed in the case of CJP leaders. Ajinkya Shinde (CJP, ~8:55 PM) alleges police did not let Dipke speak to his lawyer or family after news of his grandmother's death. CJP says Dipke, Das and Ranka were taken to different locations across Delhi-NCR (The Hindu; IANS, 9:04 PM). SFI joint secretary Aishe Ghosh demanded their release (The Hindu, 8:35 PM). NDTV (~10 PM) says Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remained in custody. Delhi Police sources (ANI, 9:38 PM): all detainees were released from detention centres except CJP leaders, and due legal process will be followed for the CJP leaders. 10:47 PM: Hindustan Times reports Delhi Police posted on X that Dipke was "immediately" told of his grandmother's death and the funeral time and was offered "possible facilitation" to travel home; CJP replied, "Where is Abhijeet? His family wants to talk to him... last rites tomorrow morning." 10:53 PM: CJP posted, "It's been 12 hours. No information. No accountability," and demanded immediate release, disclosure of whereabouts and access to lawyers for Dipke, Das and Ranka. NDTV says police told Dipke he could leave for his grandmother's funeral, but it is unclear whether he will be released. Nothing new was reported on that beyond the earlier police and CJP accounts. HT (11:25 PM) says Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee are still held while everyone else was released. NDTV says the four remained in custody as of 12:15 AM, and that everyone else among at least 3,000 detainees was released. Ajinkya Shinde wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner at 11:29 PM asking where Dipke, Das and Ranka are (IANS). A habeas corpus plea seeking their production and release was filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, not by CJP. CJP legal cell chief Ratna Singh posted at 12:48 AM: "This petition is not filed by @Cockroachisback. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." CJP reposted that and added "Please note." Bar & Bench and LiveLaw report that Bharti has sought to withdraw the plea. Ratna Singh posted at 1:03 AM: "Since morning no one knows where they are, their families don't have any idea, the lawyers have no clue." Says he signed no bond (Tribune, updated 9:57 PM); that conflicts with Ratna Singh's earlier account of a one-year no-breach-of-peace condition. Both are kept. India Today (9:16 PM): he questioned an alleged 3:30 AM call in which officers asked him to tell his parents he could be jailed "for a long time." His account. ThePrint (8:47 PM): he rejected the police claim that they offered help, saying they "wanted to torment my parents." His words. DCP Neha Yadav (Indian Express, 9:19 PM) shared the police video and said permission for the protest was denied because of past non-compliance. That is the police account. IANS (10:31 PM and 11:07 PM), ANI (12:11 AM) and PTI video (12:13 AM): he reached his ancestral village, Santuk Pimpri in Hingoli, late on Sunday night and visited the cremation ground to pay tribute to his grandmother. NDTV (11:07 PM) carries the police video of officers telling him of her death, headlined "We're Sorry." On 12 Oct in Hingoli (PTI video, 10:16 AM; IANS, 10:29–10:32 AM) he said: "Delhi Police, if you have the courage, release the entire video in which I repeatedly asked them to let me speak to my cousin, give me my phone for two minutes and allow me to speak to my lawyer." He also said police may have felt ashamed of alleged molestation by male officers and so used female officers. That is his allegation. On X, via PTI and The Hindu (11:13 AM): "Youth are being assaulted, journalists are being assaulted, even MPs are being assaulted by Delhi Police. What makes Gyanesh Kumar so indispensable to Modi that he is willing to wage war against everyone just to protect him?" His words. The police account remains that he was offered help and declined. On 12 Oct he wrote on X (about 1:46 PM): "They have removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Yes, it's no a longer protest site as anyway it was turned into a war zone by the coward dictator. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!" About 1:59 PM: "Today, Modi denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Tomorrow, he will denotify democracy itself. The dictator's problem was never the protest site. It was the very idea of people protesting." His words. PTI (about 2:24 PM), from Hingoli, reported his allegation that Delhi Police subjected him and his family to "mental torture" and that his relatives and lawyer were unaware of his whereabouts during the 10 Oct detention. His allegation. The police account already on this card is that officers told him of his grandmother's death and offered help. On X at about 5:04 PM on 12 Oct he wrote: "If Modi thinks taking away Jantar Mantar will put an end to protests, he is mistaken. Jantar Mantar is not just a location but a spirit of resistance..." His words. As of 6:15 PM, the 24-hour ultimatum given at Parliament Street around 11:50 AM still had no police response in the reports used here. As of 9:35 PM IST, that 24-hour ultimatum still had no reported police grant of a Jantar Mantar date. On 13 Oct he posted that CJP members carrying the tricolour had entered Jantar Mantar early in the morning before police picked them up, and wrote, tagging the Prime Minister: "You cannot denotify the resistance." His claim (The Hindu / PTI). He was not reported detained in these accounts. Das, Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde were. ETV Bharat (about 3:08 PM, 13 Oct) reported his claim that Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and Saurav Das were held at separate locations, that 11 volunteers were taken elsewhere, and that lawyers were barred and threatened with further detention. He asked, "How can you arrest someone for hoisting the tricolour?" His claim. He was not reported detained. The Hindu and PTI (about 4:31 PM): he was in his village, Santuk Pimpri, in Maharashtra's Hingoli district, for the asthi visarjan of his grandmother, Savitribai Dipke. He warned that if demonstrations are banned at Jantar Mantar, protest sites would emerge across the country. He said that if police stop him on the way to Delhi he would begin the agitation from wherever he is detained, and that he would reach the capital on Wednesday. His words. He was not reported detained. Times of India (about 5:52 PM), citing ANI, reported a later post and interview in which he said Saurav, Ashutosh and Ajinkya were still detained and that police were not letting lawyers meet them. He called it kidnapping. He said Ratna Singh had just told him the three were kept separately. His account.

detainees.name: Saurav Das
detainees.when: 10 Oct, about 10:30 AM IST
detainees.where: Same flight, IGI Airport. Later moved to another location in Delhi (TOI)
detainees.status: Held. Detained again on the morning of 13 Oct at Jantar Mantar, with Ajinkya Shinde (The Hindu, the Economic Times and Times of India; reports from about 9:48 AM). No release was reported as of 12:15 PM. From a detention bus he said: "Jantar Mantar has been breached. We were inside and now they are detaining us and taking us away" (Times of India). The Hindu (about 11:13 AM) reported him saying they had been taken to Jaffarpur police station. Abhijeet Dipke posted that they had entered with the tricolour before police picked them up. His claim. A senior Delhi Police officer told The Hindu (about 10:08 AM) that protesters entered through eateries and food stalls, that a demonstration at Jantar Mantar is illegal because the site has been de-notified, and that they were detained immediately. That is the police account. Earlier account: RELEASED (~10 AM, 11 Oct). An Executive Magistrate ordered the release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:58 AM, citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh; Bar & Bench, 10:00 AM, which reports them released). This corrects earlier reports, including this page's 8:15 AM update, that they were still in custody. LiveLaw (10:20 AM), citing Ratna Singh, says they were released on condition they will not engage in a breach of the peace for one year. PTI (10:54 AM) says the condition is that they "maintain peace" for one year. Delhi Police, via ANI (10:56 AM), say the preventive arrest was under BNSS Sections 126 and 170 on 10 Oct 2026, that all due legal procedures were followed, that they were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate's court at Delhi Cantt, and that a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was taken. That is the police account. CJP counsel Soutik Banerjee said at 10:18 AM that all three had been released (LiveLaw). Indian Express (10:51 AM) says they walked out of Delhi Cantt police station. Delhi Police had placed the three under preventive arrest under BNSS Sections 126 (security for keeping the peace) and 170 (arrest to prevent the commission of cognisable offences) (LiveLaw, 8:23 AM; Bar & Bench, 8:32 AM; PTI, 9:10 AM; Indian Express, 9:34 AM). They were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate, South West District, at Delhi Cantt Police Station (LiveLaw, 9:35 AM; Bar & Bench, 9:39 AM; ANI video, 9:51 AM). India Today (9:00 AM, police sources) had said that no arrests had been made. Earlier account: At 1:08 PM, intelligence sources told The Hindu that Dipke, Das and Ranka were taken to three different locations in Delhi-NCR. CJP said at ~4:45 PM it still has no information on their whereabouts and is concerned for their safety. CJP said at a 7:35 PM press conference it still has no information on the whereabouts of Dipke, Das and Ranka (The Hindu). Police sources (The Hindu, 7:38 PM) say due legal process will be followed in the case of CJP leaders. Ajinkya Shinde (CJP, ~8:55 PM) alleges police did not let Dipke speak to his lawyer or family after news of his grandmother's death. CJP says Dipke, Das and Ranka were taken to different locations across Delhi-NCR (The Hindu; IANS, 9:04 PM). SFI joint secretary Aishe Ghosh demanded their release (The Hindu, 8:35 PM). NDTV (~10 PM) says Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remained in custody. Delhi Police sources (ANI, 9:38 PM): all detainees were released from detention centres except CJP leaders, and due legal process will be followed for the CJP leaders. 10:47 PM: Hindustan Times reports Delhi Police posted on X that Dipke was "immediately" told of his grandmother's death and the funeral time and was offered "possible facilitation" to travel home; CJP replied, "Where is Abhijeet? His family wants to talk to him... last rites tomorrow morning." 10:53 PM: CJP posted, "It's been 12 hours. No information. No accountability," and demanded immediate release, disclosure of whereabouts and access to lawyers for Dipke, Das and Ranka. HT (11:25 PM) says Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee are still held while everyone else was released. NDTV says the four remained in custody as of 12:15 AM, and that everyone else among at least 3,000 detainees was released. Ajinkya Shinde wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner at 11:29 PM asking where Dipke, Das and Ranka are (IANS). A habeas corpus plea seeking their production and release was filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, not by CJP. CJP legal cell chief Ratna Singh posted at 12:48 AM: "This petition is not filed by @Cockroachisback. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." CJP reposted that and added "Please note." Bar & Bench and LiveLaw report that Bharti has sought to withdraw the plea. Ratna Singh posted at 1:03 AM: "Since morning no one knows where they are, their families don't have any idea, the lawyers have no clue." PTI (12:46 PM): Dipke said Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka will hold a press conference at 2 PM at the Press Club of India and announce the next steps. The Wire (2:00 PM) quotes Saurav Das: "We are returning with full strength." His words. A journalist's X post at 1:30 PM described heavy police outside the Press Club; that post is unverified. The press conference was held at the Press Club of India on the afternoon of 11 Oct. Saurav Das (PTI, about 2:50–3:02 PM; Hindustan Times) said Delhi Police "forcefully entered" the airplane and "kidnapped" them, that there was no formal detention notice, that phones were seized with no seizure memo, and that they were not allowed a lawyer. He said he suspects the phones were "hacked or cloned." He said, "We will not go back," and appealed to citizens to take to the streets. On the one-year condition against a breach of the peace, he said the breach was done by PM Modi, Amit Shah and Gyanesh Kumar. He also said Delhi was "like a fort with 40,000 personnel" and that more than 50 metro stations were shut. Those are his figures and his words. Ashutosh Ranka (ThePrint) said, "The fight will continue until every single one of our demands is met." He thanked Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Manik Sarkar and Pinarayi Vijayan. He said several CJP colleagues were detained and assaulted on Sunday and that "the entire SFI team was detained today" (ANI, 3:10 PM). CNN-News18 reported that he said the fight is now also against PM Modi. His words. Ratna Singh spoke at the same briefing. The Hindu (3:38 PM) lists her among those released. ThePrint (3:50 PM) reported Delhi Police at the door of the Press Club while CJP was inside. PTI (4:27 PM) and ThePrint (4:53 PM) reported that the notices were fresh notices in an old case about a woman's allegedly morphed images circulated online, following Delhi High Court directions on her plea. CJP told NDTV (5:31 PM) that wrong tweets were attributed to them and that they will contest the notice. No fresh detention of Das, Ranka or Singh has been reported. Social posts claiming they ran from the Press Club are unverified; no news outlet has reported that. NDTV (5:56 PM): Ashutosh Ranka said, "The fight has just begun," and that it will not stop until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. Saurav Das said the protests would be "not just in Delhi but the whole country." CJP wants Jantar Mantar opened as a venue. Their words. On X at 8:51 PM he accused Delhi Police of "collaborating with these sexual assaulters." His claim. On 12 Oct he and Ashutosh Ranka reached Parliament Street police station around 11:36–11:52 AM (IANS, The Hindu, Hindustan Times, PTI). Das (ANI, 11:31 AM, and Hindustan Times, 11:49 AM): "Police tells everyone to approach them 10 days in advance. We are now saying that they have the choice to tell us the date and time ... We are giving them 24-hour ultimatum." He also said (IANS, 11:40 AM): "Peaceful protest is a right, a constitutional right, and people are already exercising it." His words. No police response was reported as of 12:10 PM. On the de-notification (PTI, about 2:52 PM, and Indian Express) he said: "Unacceptable. Why is Narendra Modi scared of Jantar Mantar? The Jantar Mantar belongs to the people of India. Did the Ministry of Home Affairs consult with the people of India? Were any stakeholders consulted? Were any organisations consulted?" He also said: "We do not accept this arbitrary decision. It is an assault on people's fundamental right to protest and peaceful assembly. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar ban raha he." His words. PTI (about 2:48 PM) shows him and Ashutosh Ranka submitting a letter to the DCP at Parliament Street seeking permission for a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar. No date from police was reported as of 3:06 PM. As of 3:11 PM on 13 Oct, still no release was reported. CJP legal head Ratna Singh alleged that the SHO of Jaffarpur Kalan police station refused to let a lawyer meet Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and others, and that their phones were confiscated (her X post, about 12:39 PM; The Hindu, about 2:20 PM). Her claim. Hindustan Times (published about 12:59 PM, updated about 2:52 PM): CJP legal representative Pushp Sharma told PTI he has not been allowed to meet Das, Ranka and 12 others detained with them. He said the last WhatsApp from Das was that phones were being taken, and that the SHO told him the phones are "kept safe" and that he can call if needed. That is Sharma's account of the SHO. Police were not quoted responding to the lawyer-access or phone claims in these reports. Abhijeet Dipke (ETV Bharat, about 3:08 PM) claimed Ashutosh, Ajinkya and Saurav were held at separate locations, that 11 volunteers were taken elsewhere, and that lawyers were barred and threatened with further detention. He asked, "How can you arrest someone for hoisting the tricolour?" His claim. The Hindu (about 4:48 PM) reported CJP accusing Delhi Police of illegal detention and of denying access to lawyers, and calling for the release of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya and other members. That is CJP's accusation. Times of India (about 5:52 PM), citing ANI: Abhijeet Dipke said they were still in detention. He wrote, "Saurav, Ashu and Ajinkya are still in detention and the police is not allowing the lawyers to meet them," and, "How can police stop lawyers from meeting them? This is kidnapping because the police are certainly not following the rule of law." Speaking to ANI, he said he had just spoken to CJP legal head Ratna Singh, who told him the three had been kept separately, that 11 volunteers had been taken elsewhere, and that police did not let lawyers enter the station and threatened others with detention. That is Dipke's account of what she told him. Police were not quoted responding. No release was reported as of 6:10 PM.

detainees.name: Ratna Singh
detainees.who: Lawyer, head of CJP's legal cell
detainees.when: 10 Oct, morning (reported by about 9:15–10:26 AM IST)
detainees.where: Outside her home in Jangpura, Delhi. Kept inside a car
detainees.reason: She says police had only 'oral orders from above' and showed no notification
detainees.status: RELEASED. The Hindu (3:38 PM, 11 Oct) lists Ratna Singh among those released, and she spoke at the CJP press conference at the Press Club of India. This replaces the earlier conflicting-reports status. Hindustan Times: she alleged that police visited volunteers' homes and intimidated parents from Friday night into Saturday, and that she was followed by the Intelligence Bureau after landing in Delhi. Her allegation. ANI (3:58 PM): she said the release conditions were the standard template, with "no special conditions." Her words. Earlier account: Free — acting as CJP's lawyer at the 11 Oct production; earlier detention reports unconfirmed. ANI reported she was released (~5:53 PM), and Saket court dismissed her plea for an FIR and a release direction (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench, ANI, 5:53 PM). The Hindu live blog (8:13 PM entry) says she posted at 7:13 PM: 'I am still detained. Since 9AM. There are 30 police official for one woman.' The Hindu (8:32 PM) and The Wire (8:54 PM) report a Delhi court dismissed her plea alleging wrongful confinement by police outside her Jangpura home. The Wire quotes her: 'Judge Serving Master' and 'Welcome to new India, where Sarkar can put 30 police personnel confining you...' LiveLaw (9:26 PM): a Delhi court rejected her plea for an FIR against policemen for wrongful confinement and for restraining her from protesting. Neha Bora (AISA) posted at 9:14 PM, 'Why is @whattalawyer still under house arrest?' Attributed as Bora's claim. Status remains conflicting reports as of 10:05 PM. A habeas corpus plea filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity referred to her detention. She posted at 12:48 AM that the petition was not filed by CJP, that CJP is not approaching the Supreme Court, and that CJP's legal team did not approve it. Bharti has sought to withdraw it (Bar & Bench, LiveLaw). She was posting on X between 12:48 AM and 1:46 AM. No outlet has reported her detention status. At 8:02 AM she posted that she will be at Delhi Cantt Police Station at 9 AM, as CJP's legal head, with other advocates, for the production of Dipke, Ranka and Das before an Executive Magistrate. That is consistent with her being free to attend, but no outlet has confirmed her release. On the morning of 11 Oct she was at Delhi Cantt Police Station as CJP's legal head. LiveLaw and Bar & Bench cited her for the Executive Magistrate's release order. No outlet has published a separate confirmation of when her own detention ended. As of 10:05 AM. Her account of the leaders' release, via LiveLaw (10:20 AM), is that the magistrate's condition was no breach of the peace for one year. Dipke later said he had not signed any bond that says they will not protest. Both accounts are kept.

detainees.name: Pinarayi Vijayan, John Brittas MP, K.N. Balagopal
detainees.who: CPI(M): former Kerala CM, Rajya Sabha MP, former Kerala finance minister
detainees.when: 11 Oct: detained about 1 PM at Connaught Place, later released (India Today, 3:46 PM; ThePrint). Earlier: 10 Oct, about 12:15 PM IST
detainees.where: 11 Oct: Connaught Place (Indian Express, about 1 PM). Earlier: Delhi. Driven around the city, taken to Chhatrasal Stadium, then moved again (Brittas) Kerala CM V.D. Satheesan (via UNI, ~5:27 PM) says Vijayan is held at Mandir Marg police station.
detainees.status: RELEASED. CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas was detained again at about 1 PM on 11 Oct from Connaught Place (Indian Express) and was later released. CPI(M), via ThePrint (2:48 PM), alleges Delhi Police brutally attacked him and then dropped him by the roadside, visibly injured and in distress. A video shows him being helped into an autorickshaw. That is the party's allegation. India Today (3:46 PM) says he got into a heated argument with police as they tried to detain him, and repeats the CPI(M) allegation. In a video shared on X at 3:12 PM, which no news outlet has verified, Brittas alleges four CRPF personnel pinned him down in a vehicle until he struggled to breathe, and that he was released only after a DCP threatened suspension. Pinarayi Vijayan and K.N. Balagopal: no new report. Earlier account: RELEASED (PTI video, ~7:10 PM): Pinarayi Vijayan. After his release he accused Delhi Police of behaviour unbecoming of a police force and said he is proud to have been part of the protest against the denial of democracy. RELEASED (IANS, 9:20 PM): John Brittas and K.N. Balagopal were released with him from Mandir Marg police station. Indian Express (posted 3:00 AM, 12 Oct): Brittas said, "CRPF men forcefully detained me and threw me in a bus. They pinned me to a seat after grabbing me by the neck and choked me. It was only after a Delhi Police DCP's intervention that I was allowed to go." Indian Express says RAF and Delhi Police detained him at Connaught Place while he spoke to the media, and that he was taken to RML Hospital. His account.

detainees.name: Tushar Gandhi
detainees.who: Activist, Mahatma Gandhi's great-grandson ('Hum Bharat Ke Log')
detainees.when: 10 Oct, before about 12:15 PM IST
detainees.where: Picked up in Bandra, Mumbai and taken to DN Nagar police station
detainees.reason: Ahead of a solidarity protest at August Kranti Maidan (PTI)
detainees.status: Held at last report. Still held at DN Nagar police station, Mumbai. Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Haroon Khan says he was detained in Bandra and brought to DN Nagar (IANS, 6:15 PM). Aaditya Thackeray sat outside the station demanding his release (IANS, ~5:50 PM); Thackeray and MP Sanjay Raut were there with a large crowd of party workers (IANS, 6:12 PM). Thackeray warned party workers will gather outside if Gandhi is not released (The Hindu, 5:57–5:58 PM). Times Now (7:12 PM): Aaditya Thackeray and Sanjay Raut were still on dharna at DN Nagar police station. No release reported as of 10:05 PM. 11:25 PM: Mumbai's Gamdevi police registered a case against Tushar Gandhi, actor Imran Khan, Ali Bhojani and 300–400 others under BNS sections 223, 126(2) and 189 for protesting without permission (IANS). This is an FIR report, not a reported release.

detainees.name: Neha Bora, Yogendra Yadav, Prashant Bhushan, Dipankar Bhattacharya
detainees.who: Neha Bora, AISA president; Yogendra Yadav, national convenor of Bharat Jodo Abhiyaan; Prashant Bhushan, senior advocate; Dipankar Bhattacharya, CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary. Keep Bora as AISA president (The Sentinel calls her an AAP leader; Deccan Herald does not).
detainees.when: 11 Oct, about 3:50 PM IST (Neha Bora detained again; ThePrint, Scroll). Earlier: 10 Oct, about 2:20 PM IST for Bora and Yadav. Bhushan and Bhattacharya reported ~4:23 PM IST (The Sentinel) and 4:31 PM IST (Deccan Herald); exact detention time not given.
detainees.where: 11 Oct: march from RK Ashram Marg to Connaught Place (ThePrint, Scroll). Earlier: Bora and Yadav: march from Dilli Haat towards Jantar Mantar. Bhushan and Bhattacharya: near INA Market, on the way to the CJP protest (The Sentinel). Dilli Haat is at INA.
detainees.status: RELEASED — exact release time not reported; Neha Bora was seen leading the INDIA bloc march to the Supreme Court on 12 Oct (The Hindu, about 4:03 PM; the lead photo caption by R.V. Moorthy names her with Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra). The Hindu also reported her, Yogendra Yadav and other representatives of Krantikari Yuva Sangathan on the bus toward the Barakhamba junction. She posted on X at about 5:10 PM, "Marching to the Supreme Court...", and at about 5:55 PM, "We're marching to stitch it back." ABP Live says she was among those detained on Sunday and later released. Dipankar Bhattacharya was among the leaders named at the march (Economic Times / PTI). Prashant Bhushan: no new release report on 12 Oct. Earlier account: AISA president Neha Bora was detained again at about 3:50 PM on 11 Oct while leading a march from RK Ashram Marg to Connaught Place, after the Supreme Court's interim order (ThePrint, 3:53 PM; Scroll, 3:25 PM and 3:40 PM). She had called people to assemble at RK Ashram at 2:30 PM (ThePrint, 2:24 PM). Protesters allege police used brute force. AISA alleges protesters were "badly beaten." That is AISA's claim. ANI (3:34 PM) reported AISA workers detained near RK Puram. Yogendra Yadav, Prashant Bhushan and Dipankar Bhattacharya: no new detention report on 11 Oct. Earlier account: RELEASED (India Today, ~8:30 PM): Neha Bora and the other women detained with her, from Maidan Garhi police station. Held at Maidan Garhi detention centre. AISA alleges (4:09 PM) police illegally took the phones of Neha Bora and AISA activist Nirma, kept them in an isolated room and are not letting lawyers meet them. 7:11 PM: women were released from Maidan Garhi police station, and Neha Bora got her phone back (The Wire). India Today later reported that Neha Bora and the women with her were released, which supersedes the earlier line that her own release was not confirmed. RELEASED (his own post, 9:35 PM): Yogendra Yadav. He wrote that he had just been released from Maidangarhi police station and was reaching Sanjay Colony police station. No other outlet had confirmed that release yet. After that release he is sitting at Sanjay Colony police post. At 10:49 PM and 11:07 PM he wrote that four colleagues there were "brutally beaten", including an 18-year-old and a lawyer, that lawyers were not allowed to meet them, and that he will not leave until they are released and get a medical exam (MLC). His claim. Prashant Bhushan and Dipankar Bhattacharya: no individual release reported. Delhi Police sources (ANI, 9:38 PM) said all detainees except CJP leaders were released, so they are likely released; not individually confirmed. At 1:54 AM Yogendra Yadav posted that his colleagues had been released and that at 1 AM they returned to where the day began. He wrote that they set out to stop Jantar Mantar 2.0 and 22 Jantar Mantars sprang up in Delhi, and that the struggle will continue (his own post). No release reported as of 6:10 PM. AISA alleges, via a post carried by The Wire and Indian Express (about 4:49–5:22 PM), that buses were turned into lockups, that protesters were beaten, including in their private parts, and that police used casteist and misogynist slurs. AISA also says detainees were taken beyond barricades where journalists were denied access, phones were snatched, and male protesters were beaten. That is AISA's allegation. ThePrint (4:11 PM) carried a video of Neha Bora from inside a bus: "Are buses the new jails?" Her words. As of 8:10 PM there is still no release report. Indian Express says she was detained on Sunday. Unverified posts said she was at Connaught Place on Sunday evening. Those posts are not confirmed by an outlet. Her team account posted "Connaught Place NOW" at 7:54 PM and, at 7:34 PM, "Which law allows this police brutality against women after 6 PM?" Her side's claim. AISA (7:49 PM) says female detainees are refusing to leave detention centres until all the male protesters are released. That claim is not independently verified. As of 10:10 PM there is still no release report. She stays listed as detained. Her team posted at 9:32 PM that she sent a lookalike friend the other way while police chased her, and that she reached Connaught Place. That is her team's account, and it is unverified. Journalist Alisha Dutta posted at 9:46 PM that outside RK Ashram Metro a hijabi bystander, a woman journalist and "a Neha Bora doppelgänger" were picked up. Her post. Unverified individual posts say Neha Bora was released from Najafgarh. No outlet has confirmed a release. She stays listed as detained. As of 6:00 AM on 12 Oct, no outlet has confirmed a release. As of 12:10 PM on 12 Oct, still no outlet has confirmed a release. As of 3:06 PM on 12 Oct, still no outlet has confirmed a release. India Today (about 5:16 PM, 13 Oct) listed AISA chief Neha Bora and CPI(ML) leader Dipankar Bhattacharya among those present at Rahul Gandhi's tea at 5 Sunehri Bagh Road. That report does not place Yogendra Yadav or Prashant Bhushan at the tea. No new detention of Neha Bora was reported as of 6:10 PM.

The earlier reporter post placed her at Dwarka Sector 17 police station; both accounts are kept, attributed. TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh condemned her detention (IANS, 5:35 PM). PTI (~6:16 PM): she says she has been in a prison van for about two hours — 'We obeyed and accepted whatever they said. Despite that, they picked us up... I have never used this prison van; it is meant for criminals.' Earlier, ~6:01 PM, she said she will join the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court on Monday (PTI). NDTV (7:41 PM): she wore a band-aid over her mouth and called it 'a Super Emergency'. PTI (8:17 PM), after her release: 'Right now we won't say anything because tomorrow the INDIA Alliance has called for a united stand...' Release of the other TMC leaders on this card was not separately confirmed.

detainees.status: RELEASED (The Wire, shortly after midnight; published 1:27 AM). Advocate Fidal Tom (The Wire spells the name Fidel Tom) and students Saurabh, Nikhil and Harsh were released from Sanjay Colony police post (Maidan Garhi). A medico-legal examination was conducted. The Wire's account: he went to the post to seek the students' release, was detained himself, and was allegedly taken to a washroom and beaten by several police personnel, including a plain-clothes man (an account shared with The Wire and student activists). AISA activist Abhigyan told The Wire all four were beaten badly. The SHO told The Wire he would find out and respond. Earlier, the Lawyers' Association for Constitution wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner (10:32–10:37 PM) alleging he was assaulted and illegally detained (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). That earlier allegation is kept, attributed.

Students Saurabh, Nikhil and Harsh were released with advocate Fidal Tom from Sanjay Colony police post. A medico-legal examination was conducted. The Wire's account, from an account shared with The Wire and student activists: Tom was allegedly taken to a washroom and beaten by several police personnel, including a plain-clothes man. AISA activist Abhigyan told The Wire all four were beaten badly. Maktoob (12:22 AM): AISA alleged Saurabh was beaten so badly he could not walk (AISA claim). Earlier, Yogendra Yadav wrote that four colleagues at the post were "brutally beaten", including an 18-year-old and a lawyer, and that he would not leave until they were released (his claim).

Ratna Singh posted at 8:43 PM that CJP national spokesperson Sudhir Sangwan and joint secretary Balakrishnan Shukla were detained by Delhi Police on Sunday evening from Connaught Place and that their whereabouts remain unknown. The name on this card is Balakrishna. Ratna Singh's post names Balakrishnan Shukla. CJP posted at 10:48 PM: "Where is Delhi Police holding CJP Leaders?" and said they were not allowed to contact their lawyers. Saurav Das posted at 1:07 AM: efforts to locate them had been in vain. These are CJP's claims. No police response was found. As of 6:00 AM on 12 Oct. Earlier account: @Cockroachisback posted at 1:55 PM that Ankit Bharadwaj, Anam, Mukesh all-rounder, Balakrishna and Sudhir Sangwan were detained while protesting peacefully. That post was not independently verified. Ankit Bharadwaj, Anam and Mukesh have no new report. As of 9:00 AM on 12 Oct, no further report since the SOS. As of 12:10 PM on 12 Oct, no further report since the SOS. As of 3:06 PM on 12 Oct, no further report since the SOS. As of 6:15 PM on 12 Oct, no further report since the SOS.

detainees.status: RELEASED. Indian Express (3:57 PM): Shashwat, Siya and Vijay were detained at Connaught Place and made to board a police bus despite saying they were on duty. The phones of Shashwat and Siya were seized and had not been returned. Indian Express (4:14 PM): they were released about 45 minutes later near Chhatrasal Stadium, about 12 km from where they were picked up. Indian Express (5:17 AM, 12 Oct): they were picked up at Chelmsford Road and released near Chhatrasal Stadium after about 45 minutes. Vijay's surname is Kumar. Status remains released on 11 Oct.

detainees.reason: Police say legal action is being taken against people assembling without permission.
detainees.status: Held. Detained on 11 Oct at about 4:50 PM at Shivaji Park, Mumbai (PTI). Tribune/PTI (5:46 PM): she was among dozens detained. She told PTI, "I do not know where they are taking me." Scroll (5:07 PM): demonstrators were also picked up at Dadar station, some just for walking in the area. An X post by journalist Ashish Dwivedi (4:59 PM) said she was taken to Tardeo police station. That post is unverified. No release reported as of 6:10 PM. No release reported as of 8:10 PM. No release reported as of 10:10 PM. The Bombay High Court (Goa bench) order that night covers the Panaji detainees, not the Mumbai detentions. No release reported for her as of 6:00 AM on 12 Oct.

detainees.status: RELEASED. The Quint (7:40 PM): Swati Chopra and Mohit Manwani were detained near Shivaji Park, taken to Tardeo police station, and released after more than an hour.

detainees.name: Amreen Shaikh
detainees.when: 11 Oct (Times of India, updated 7:16 PM; The Hindu/PTI, 7:04 PM)
detainees.where: Azad Maidan, Panaji. Dozens were taken into custody on reaching the ground.
detainees.reason: Police stopped a CJP protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar before it began.
detainees.status: RELEASED (~9:40 PM, 11 Oct). The Bombay High Court (Goa bench), Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar, ordered the release at a special Sunday-evening hearing. The Goan says the group was released around 9:40 PM from Panaji police station after being brought back by bus from Pernem. Times of India quotes the court: the detention may not have been authorised because there were no prohibitory orders under BNSS Section 163. The court did not rule on whether the detention was correct. The public prosecutor assured the court they would be released. Norma Alvares undertook that they would not protest at Azad Maidan on Sunday night only. Times of India and The Goan name seven: Jack Sukhija, Amreen Shaikh (Times of India spells the name Afreen), Aditya Parulekar, Bhupesh Bind, Liston Noronha, Shamiro or Shamino Fernandes, and Milind Rane. PTI and India Today say six. Both counts are kept. Alvares argued that Shaikh, a woman, could not be detained after 6 PM (Times of India). Earlier the same evening, Times of India and The Hindu/PTI reported her among dozens detained at Azad Maidan. TOI journalist Bindiya Chari posted the order on X at 9:09 PM. PTI, India Today, New Indian Express, Times of India and The Goan later reported it.

detainees.status: Neha Bora's team on X says he was detained at 8:33 PM and released at about 9:25 PM ("SHYAM MEERA SINGH RELEASED!"). That account is unverified. Her team calls journalist detentions contempt of the Supreme Court's order. Their claim. Inshorts (4:31 PM) reports the detention and a video of him taken into a police van, and does not report a release.

detainees.name: Ajinkya Shinde
detainees.when: Morning of 13 Oct 2026
detainees.where: Jantar Mantar, then Jaffarpur police station, according to Saurav Das (The Hindu, about 11:13 AM)
detainees.reason: Delhi Police say the group entered a de-notified protest site through eateries. CJP says they were inside protesting.
detainees.status: Held. Detained on the morning of 13 Oct at Jantar Mantar with Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka (The Hindu, the Economic Times and Times of India). No release was reported as of 12:15 PM. Dipke posted that they entered with the tricolour before police picked them up. His claim. Das said they had been inside and were being taken away, and later that they were at Jaffarpur police station. Ranka said the protest will take place at Jantar Mantar only. Their words. A senior Delhi Police officer told The Hindu (about 10:08 AM) that they entered through eateries and food stalls and that a demonstration there is illegal because the site has been de-notified. That is the police account. As of 3:11 PM on 13 Oct, still no release was reported. CJP legal head Ratna Singh alleged that the SHO of Jaffarpur Kalan police station refused to let a lawyer meet Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and others, and that their phones were confiscated (her X post, about 12:39 PM; The Hindu, about 2:20 PM). Her claim. Hindustan Times (published about 12:59 PM, updated about 2:52 PM): CJP legal representative Pushp Sharma told PTI he has not been allowed to meet Das, Ranka and 12 others detained with them. He said the last WhatsApp from Das was that phones were being taken, and that the SHO told him the phones are "kept safe" and that he can call if needed. That is Sharma's account of the SHO. Police were not quoted responding to the lawyer-access or phone claims in these reports. Abhijeet Dipke (ETV Bharat, about 3:08 PM) claimed Ashutosh, Ajinkya and Saurav were held at separate locations, that 11 volunteers were taken elsewhere, and that lawyers were barred and threatened with further detention. He asked, "How can you arrest someone for hoisting the tricolour?" His claim. The Hindu (about 4:48 PM) reported CJP accusing Delhi Police of illegal detention and of denying access to lawyers, and calling for the release of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya and other members. That is CJP's accusation. Times of India (about 5:52 PM), citing ANI: Abhijeet Dipke said they were still in detention. He wrote, "Saurav, Ashu and Ajinkya are still in detention and the police is not allowing the lawyers to meet them," and, "How can police stop lawyers from meeting them? This is kidnapping because the police are certainly not following the rule of law." Speaking to ANI, he said he had just spoken to CJP legal head Ratna Singh, who told him the three had been kept separately, that 11 volunteers had been taken elsewhere, and that police did not let lawyers enter the station and threatened others with detention. That is Dipke's account of what she told him. Police were not quoted responding. No release was reported as of 6:10 PM.

timeline.e: INDIA bloc, student unions and other groups begin protests in Delhi against the CEC over SIR.
Rahul Gandhi climbs barricades and leads an 8-hour sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan. About 250 detained, including MPs; all released around 10 PM.
Rahul and Priyanka Gandhi detained a second time near Jantar Mantar. Derek O'Brien and about 90 others also detained.
Dhruv Rathee joins CJP protest in Bengaluru. CJP spokesperson Deepak Baliyan detained in Alwar and released that night.

Supreme Court says there can be no 'complete prohibition' on metro and trains. Delhi HC refuses an urgent hearing for Youth Congress. Delhi Police confirms the protest is denied. Home Secretary tells state police chiefs to stop 'unauthorised entry' into Delhi. INDIA bloc meets the President.
DMRC shuts entry/exit at 45 metro stations until 6 PM on 10 Oct.
Dhruv Rathee detained at his Gurugram home.

image.alt: Dhruv Rathee speaking into a microphone.

timeline.e: Detentions begin at Jantar Mantar. People are put on buses, and stadiums are used as detention centres.
Delhi Police statement: about 500 detained, plus about 50 'with criminal backgrounds'. The district is split into 20 zones, each with its own detention centre.
Dipke, Das and Ranka detained on board their Air India flight at IGI. CJP releases a pre-recorded video handing the lead to Ajinkya Shinde.

image.alt: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka seated in a police bus.

timeline.e: Lawyers marching from the Supreme Court are detained. A contempt plea is filed in the SC over the metro closures.
Pinarayi Vijayan, John Brittas and K.N. Balagopal detained. Tushar Gandhi detained in Mumbai. CPI(M) says 500+ cadres held at HKS Bhawan. About 200 detained at Connaught Place.
Officials say 25–30 protesters jumped barricades on Imtiaz Ali Marg and threw stones; 2 police personnel injured (PTI, citing officials).
CJI Surya Kant and SG Tushar Mehta speak to authorities, and the detained lawyers are released. Hundreds detained outside Bangla Sahib gurdwara.
Ratna Singh moves Saket court. Neha Bora and Yogendra Yadav detained on the Dilli Haat march. Mamata Banerjee and 5 TMC leaders detained outside her residence.

CPI(M) says former Tripura CM Manik Sarkar and CITU's Elamaram Kareem are held at Bawana stadium. At Saket court, LiveLaw says staff told reporters the magistrate was dictating an order in a different case; Ratna Singh's FIR plea was still pending as of 5:27 PM; the court dismissed it at 5:53 PM.
Manish Sisodia and Punjab AAP leaders Baltej Punia and Sonia Mann detained by Chandigarh Police near the Punjab Chief Electoral Officer's office. Punjab FM Harpal Singh Cheema also took part.

image.alt: A crowd at an outdoor protest, many people holding flags.

timeline.e: Arvind Kejriwal detained by Delhi Police while trying to march to Jantar Mantar. TOI says outside his residence; Business Today says outside Lodhi Estate. Gopal Rai also detained. AAP's Atishi alleges Kejriwal was 'brutally taken into custody'.

image.alt: Arvind Kejriwal standing beside a police bus.

timeline.e: CJP's Ajinkya Shinde, in a video, tells people to march on: 'Wherever the Delhi Police try to stop you, make it your Jantar Mantar.' Says the movement continues till the CEC resigns.
More than 50 protesters detained near Dilli Haat at Neha Bora's call; some say they weren't part of the protest.
About 200 students from Punjab reached the Jantar Mantar area after spending the night at Gurdwara Bangla Sahib; several were detained.
PTI, citing police sources, says Delhi Police detained around 1,000 protesters across the city during the anti-CEC stir.

Dipke's father Bhagwan Dipke questions the heavy deployment: 'It is an agitation of students. Have dacoits from Chambal gathered in Delhi?' and says every Indian has a legal right to protest. His mother Anita Dipke asks why he had to be detained from a flight.

Police sources (PTI) say Delhi Police told Abhijeet Dipke of his grandmother's death and left it to him whether to stay in detention and continue the protest or go home for her last rites. Grandmother Savitribai Shankarrao Dipke, 85, died around 11:30 AM in Santuk Pimpri, Hingoli district, Maharashtra; last rites at 10 AM Sunday 11 Oct (family sources).
After his detention, Kejriwal posts a video on X: 'We have been detained by the police... The youth of the country has awakened. We are not going to be intimidated by Modi's tyranny.'

Sanjay Singh, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Durgesh Pathak detained by Delhi Police along with Arvind Kejriwal. Exact time of detention not given; Tribune logged it at 4:18 PM IST. Place in Delhi not specified.
Kejriwal after detention (PTI video): 'Turn the entire country into Jantar Mantar.'
The Hindu reports CJP activists protesting at Chennai's Elliot's Beach; police detained several after a verbal spat.
Mamata Banerjee begins a dharna at Dwarka Sector 17 police station, where she is detained (Derek O'Brien, via Deccan Herald reporter Shemin Joy). Reporter post on X, not yet in a published article.
NDTV: Chennai Police detained 100+ protesters near Elliott's Beach demanding the CEC's resignation; activist Radhika Ganesh among those detained.
NDTV visuals: security forces including Delhi Police and RAF detain protesters at Connaught Place Outer Circle who tried to march past barricades.

Prashant Bhushan (senior advocate) and Dipankar Bhattacharya (CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary) detained near INA Market with Neha Bora (AISA president) and Yogendra Yadav. Exact detention time not given. The Sentinel calls Bora an AAP leader; Deccan Herald and earlier reports say AISA president.

Mamata Banerjee will stay in Delhi for an INDIA bloc march to the Supreme Court on Monday 12 Oct instead of returning to Kolkata; Abhishek Banerjee will also come back for it (Deccan Herald reporter Shemin Joy). Reporter post on X, not yet in a published article.

Delhi Police officials (via ANI): Dipke was detained because the protest call was not permitted; he was told of his grandmother's death 'with due sensitivity', told the funeral time, and offered possible facilitation for his journey to his hometown on humanitarian grounds.

Scroll: a protester detained in Pune says 'We were dragged on the city streets. Multiple women have sustained bruises.' Unverified individual claim on social media; no detention count given. Scroll also reports its journalist Divya Aslesha was detained in Pune.

BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad: 'CJP is doing shadow boxing for the Aam Aadmi Party'; calls the opposition 'defeated, desperate individuals ... weaponizing street protests'; defends SIR as a legal provision conducted 'more than nine times'.
Bengaluru: at least 50 AISA students detained at Freedom Park (The Hindu, 3:21 PM).

AISA's claim: police illegally took the phones of Neha Bora (AISA president) and AISA activist Nirma at the Maidan Garhi detention centre, kept them in an isolated room, and are not letting lawyers meet them (The Hindu, 4:09 PM).
Priyanka Gandhi Vadra: 'India is not a democracy anymore. It is a dictatorship being run by Modi and Shah' (The Hindu).
CJP, SFI and AISF representatives to address a press meet on 'Jantar Mantar 2.0' at HKS Surjeet Bhawan at 5 PM (The Hindu, 4:34 PM).

Yogendra Yadav, in a video shared by The Wire (recorded earlier): 'Protesters succeeded in setting up Jantar Mantar 2.0 at several sites in Delhi.' The video does not indicate that he has been released.
NDTV: BJP attacks Congress and CJP — 'India Is Not A Banana Republic'.
Mumbai: police clash with protesters near August Kranti Marg; protesters detained at August Kranti Maidan (The Hindu). No detention count given.
Scroll: nearly 5,000 protesters detained in Delhi, citing The Hindu.
Sonam Wangchuk says India is in 'a state of undeclared emergency' and he will be compelled to consider an anshan (fast) or padyatra if detained protesters are not released by tomorrow (The Hindu).

CJP says it still has no information on Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka's whereabouts and is concerned for their safety. At 1:08 PM, intelligence sources told The Hindu the three were taken to three different locations in Delhi-NCR. No release reported.
Indian Youth Congress launches a legal helpline (9582223884) for people detained or threatened over the protests (PTI via Tribune).

Hindustan Times: INDIA bloc to hold a mega protest in Delhi on Monday 12 Oct. Mamata Banerjee cancelled her return to Kolkata to join; Abhishek Banerjee will travel back to Delhi for it. This confirms the earlier Deccan Herald reporter post.
The Hindu: a group of individuals threatened, chased and assaulted some protesters in Connaught Place. Perpetrators not identified.
SFI says students and public intellectuals will hold a press conference at HKS Surjeet Bhawan at 5 PM. No reports yet of what was said.

Saket court: the CJM's order on Ratna Singh's FIR plea was under dictation at about 4:58 PM. The court said it would decide on the application as filed, not on changed circumstances (Bar & Bench, LawBeat). The plea was later dismissed at 5:53 PM.
Officials told PTI that Delhi Police detained over 3,000 people during the anti-CEC protest. The Hindu's summary says 3,300; The Tribune says 3,000.
CPI(M) calls on all party units to protest against the day's police repression, the CEC and SIR (The Wire).
Rahul Gandhi releases a video on X telling the youth: 'Keep protesting. We are proud of you' (The Hindu live blog).
SFI leader Aishe Ghosh posts a video alleging police abuse during detention and saying 'Jantar Mantar 2.0 is on' (The Hindu live blog). Attributed as her allegation.
SFI alleges people 'dressed as Delhi police' who attacked protesters and assaulted women students were not wearing name tags (The Hindu live blog). Attributed as SFI's allegation.
TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee (ANI) says about 2,500 people were detained across Delhi.
Hindustan Times: CJP renews its call — 'Wherever Delhi Police stop you, make your own Jantar Mantar'.
PTI, citing officials: police detained around 200 people at Mumbai's August Kranti Maidan. The Hindu (5:19 PM) reports a police clash with protesters there.

Police account (ANI): a police officer was injured after stone pelting during the protest. The officer says a crowd of 100–150 had gathered on the road near the Hanuman temple and protesters twisted his arm while being detained.

The Hindu: hundreds of CJP volunteers and other citizens brought from multiple places across Delhi are being held at Chhatrasal Stadium, Model Town, used as a makeshift holding centre (live blog 4:54 PM entry by Vijaita Singh).

CJP's appeal: it publicly asked Delhi Police to release Abhijeet Dipke immediately, saying his whereabouts are still unknown, his lawyers cannot reach him, and his family cannot tell him of his grandmother's death. This is CJP's claim, and it conflicts with earlier police sources who said he had been informed.
PTI video: police stop protesters marching towards Jantar Mantar on Safdarjung flyover.
NDTV: Delhi Police shares a video explaining why permission for the CJP protest was denied.
Scroll: hundreds raise slogans against CEC Gyanesh Kumar on Aurobindo Marg, South Delhi; police try to break up the crowd using force.

Kerala CM V.D. Satheesan (via UNI) says Pinarayi Vijayan is held at Mandir Marg police station, and that Kerala's Chief Secretary and Resident Commissioner are in contact with Delhi Police to coordinate his immediate release. No release reported.
PTI: 124 former IAS/IFS officers issue an open letter defending the Election Commission and SIR.
ThePrint: around 3,500 people detained in Delhi. Police say the detentions could last up to 24 hours.

Actor Imran Khan detained by Mumbai Police at August Kranti Maidan, the proposed Mumbai venue backing CJP's call. He told IANS he is not part of any organisation and does not speak as a representative.
ThePrint ground report: mini protests spring up at detention centres and on Delhi roads, with people saying they will create their own Jantar Mantar.

The Hindu, citing a senior officer: two Delhi Police personnel, Suman (Pink Force) and Dheeraj Yadav, were injured during the detention of around 1,000 protesters in New Delhi district. Circumstances are being ascertained. Police account.

ANI: Mamata Banerjee alleges Delhi Police 'kidnapped' her and is holding a protest at Dwarka North police station. An earlier reporter post had placed her at Dwarka Sector 17; both accounts are kept, attributed. TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh condemned her detention (IANS, 5:35 PM).
Mumbai Police, via ANI: over 400 people detained so far at August Kranti Maidan. PTI had reported about 200 at 5:18 PM.
CJP's claim: its national spokesperson Siddhant Bharadwaj and his team were detained. Place not stated. Attributed to CJP.
ThePrint ground report: police and RAF detain protesters at Connaught Place, including people who came from Assam and Chhattisgarh.
Police account (ANI): Sub-Inspector Bajrang Yadav says he was injured while stopping people running from the direction of the CPM office.

The Hindu: what happened moments before Dipke, Das and Ranka were detained aboard Air India flight AI 2428. The detention caught even the airline by surprise and raises questions about police access to the aircraft.
DMK chief M.K. Stalin says the BJP government detained former chief ministers Pinarayi Vijayan, Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee and Manik Sarkar, plus M.A. Baby and student leaders (The Hindu).
The Wire: some buses Delhi Police is using to detain protesters are marked 'election duty'.

Saket court dismissed Ratna Singh's plea for an FIR against police over her detention and for a direction to release her (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench, ANI). ANI reported she had been released. The Hindu later said she posted at 7:13 PM that she was still detained. The reports conflict.
Scroll: reporter Divya Aslesha recounts being detained by Pune Police and taken to Lashkar police station. She says a senior officer told her she was detained 'by mistake'.
CPI(ML) holds a road protest in Vannarpettai, Tirunelveli, against the CEC (The Hindu live blog).
Congress MP Pawan Khera (IANS): 'Today, they didn't spare lawyers, they didn't spare journalists... This is an emergency!' Attributed as his statement.

Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Singh: permission was only for the protest, not a march to the CEO's office, so marchers were taken into preventive detention (The Hindu live blog). Police account.

Indian Express live: Rahul Gandhi visited Rashtrapati Bhavan with other Opposition leaders. Exact visit time not given. BJP MP Sambit Patra called him a 'nalayak neta' and accused him of trying to draw the President into a street protest. Both statements attributed.
ThePrint: in a Rohtak village, villagers detained policemen who had come to detain a protester.

Tushar Gandhi is still held at DN Nagar police station, Mumbai. Aaditya Thackeray and MP Sanjay Raut were at the station with party workers demanding his release (IANS, The Hindu, 5:50–6:15 PM). Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Haroon Khan says Gandhi was detained in Bandra and brought there.
DMRC: the 45 Metro stations closed since 9 PM Friday will stay closed till 10 PM tonight (10 Oct). Security agencies will review after that (ANI, PTI).
LiveLaw posts a video it says shows a male CRPF officer manhandling a woman advocate near Mandi House, Delhi. Attributed to LiveLaw's video.

Delhi CM Rekha Gupta (PTI): 'Delhi will not be held hostage.' She calls CJP the 'B-Team' of Rahul Gandhi and Arvind Kejriwal and says the 'politics of spreading anarchy under guise of democracy' will be fought. Attributed as her statement.

Mamata Banerjee, still held, tells PTI she has been in a prison van for about two hours: 'We obeyed and accepted whatever they said. Despite that, they picked us up... I have never used this prison van; it is meant for criminals.' Attributed as her statement. Earlier, ~6:01 PM, she said she will join the INDIA bloc's march to the Supreme Court on Monday. The Hindu live blog also says CJP, SFI and AISF began a joint press conference in New Delhi.
