The Wire: PhD student Mohd Alfauz spent 22 hours in police detention ahead of the 10 Oct protest and describes 'moral lectures, intimidation'. Attributed to his account via The Wire.
PTI video: AAP workers clash with police during a protest in Chandigarh.
Shiv Sena (UBT) MLA Varun Sardesai detained by Mumbai Police during the anti-CEC protest (The Hindu live blog, 6:21 PM). Held at last report.
A rally near Sundarayya Vignana Kendram, Hyderabad, demands that SIR be scrapped and the CEC resign (The Hindu).

Rahul Gandhi (The Wire): 'Arrest All the Leaders. Arrest All the Young People. Arrest Us All.' Attributed as his statement. Union Minister Piyush Goyal responded that Rahul 'has no respect for any constitutional authority' (IANS, 6:23 PM).
INDIA bloc and student groups hold a rally in Visakhapatnam (The Hindu live blog).
A torchlight march in Nashik against the CEC and SIR (IANS).
Police detain a large number of CJP workers at the INA flyover, Delhi (IANS).
AIUDF president Badruddin Ajmal backs the protest and the demand for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation (ANI).
Journalists' bodies condemn the crackdown as an 'assault on press freedom'. The Wire says several journalists were detained despite showing press cards.
Union Minister Ramdas Athawale (ANI): police did not oppose an earlier CJP protest while it was peaceful, but violence and stone-pelting at police followed. Attributed as his statement.
The Wire: women protesters gathered outside Gurudwara Bangla Sahib, and several protesters who had taken shelter inside the gurdwara were detained.

Bar & Bench video: Delhi Police carry Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat away by his arms and legs, his shirt torn, during a detention earlier today. He was later released, and told Bar & Bench he had intervened to stop police manhandling. LiveLaw also posted the detention video (6:46 PM).

Delhi Police have started releasing protesters. A senior officer told The Hindu: 'We have initiated the process to release protesters, who were detained across Delhi during the protest.' The Hindu says over 5,000 were detained, including Abhijeet Dipke, CPI(M) leaders and student activists. No named leader's release was confirmed.
Mumbai: protesters forcibly detained near August Kranti Maidan (The Hindu video).

ANI describes West Bengal ministers Tapas Roy and Bishal Lama criticising the CJP protest. Roy called protesters 'traitors' and 'anti-national'. Lama said they should approach the court. Attributed as their statements.

Sources told The Wire that Trolley Times editor Navkiran and about 20 other women were detained after dark in Delhi. They are in a bus with police who have no name tags and do not know where they are being taken.

AAP workers gherao Jaffarpur Kalan police station in Dwarka, saying Arvind Kejriwal, Sanjay Singh, Anurag Dhanda (AAP national media in-charge) and Saurabh Bharadwaj are held there (PTI video). Attributed as the AAP workers' account. Kejriwal and the AAP leaders are still held; no release reported.
CJP protest leader Ajinkya Shinde (TOI): 'Wherever they stop you, that becomes Jantar Mantar.' He urges supporters to stay peaceful.

Sonam Wangchuk warns of another fast unless detainees are released (Indian Express). Hindustan Times also reports the warning. The Hindu had said he would consider an anshan or padyatra if they are not released by tomorrow.
The Wire: students detained at Bawana police station were denied drinking water.

Pinarayi Vijayan released. In a PTI video after his release, the former Kerala chief minister accuses Delhi Police of behaviour unbecoming of a police force and says he is proud to have been part of the protest. IANS later confirmed (9:20 PM) that Brittas and Balagopal were released with him from Mandir Marg police station.
The Wire: women were released from Maidan Garhi police station, and AISA president Neha Bora got her phone back. The Wire does not say Neha Bora herself was released. Her release is not confirmed.

Delhi Police, via IANS, rebut social-media claims: Dipke's grandmother's death was promptly conveyed to him with due sensitivity, he was told the funeral time, and he was offered all possible assistance to travel home on humanitarian grounds. NDTV (7:41 PM) says that by evening it was not clear whether he would be released. Attributed as the police account.
NDTV video: a clash during the CJP protest in Delhi, with police personnel injured.
CJP press conference: members say they still have no information on the whereabouts of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka (The Hindu live blog).

Delhi Police sources (The Hindu): women protesters and senior citizens are being released from detention centres first, and due legal process will be followed in the case of CJP leaders. Deployment will continue amid expectations of another protest call by CJP, AIYF, AISF and SFI. NDTV (7:41 PM) adds that the heavy deployment will continue on Sunday. Attributed as the police account.

Arvind Kejriwal, in his own video (via IANS; Hindustan Times at 7:57 PM), says he and others were brought to Jafarpur police station and that several hundred people surround it with only 15–20 police: 'this place is also gradually turning into another Jantar Mantar.' Still held. This matches the earlier AAP account of Jaffarpur Kalan police station.

NDTV, with PTI inputs: over 1,500 people were detained across Delhi, including four former chief ministers — Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar. Detainees were held in large stadiums and many were released later in the evening. Mamata wore a band-aid over her mouth and called it 'a Super Emergency'. The INDIA bloc has called a protest on Monday, and its leaders will meet CJI Surya Kant on Monday to submit a memorandum (Rahul Gandhi).

The Supreme Court will hold a special sitting on Sunday 11 Oct on advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi's contempt plea over the blanket closure of metro stations and train cancellations, alleged to violate the court's 9 Oct order. Bench: Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana. IANS (7:57 PM) names the respondents as Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chairperson D. Thara.

Senior advocate and TMC Rajya Sabha MP Menaka Guruswamy has moved the Supreme Court against the preventive detention of opposition leaders, including four former chief ministers, during today's Delhi protests. The plea is listed before the same special Sunday bench (Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana) on 11 Oct. She told Bar & Bench that preventive detention cannot be used to suppress the right to peaceful protest.
The Tribune: Ajinkya Shinde, CJP organisation in-charge from Latur, has taken command of the protest after Dipke picked him to lead it.
ThePrint ground report: police and RAF detain protesters at Connaught Place as the chaos intensifies, including people who came from Assam and Chhattisgarh.

Mamata Banerjee released from Delhi Police detention (ANI video, ~8:09 PM). PTI (8:17 PM), after her release: 'Right now we won't say anything because tomorrow the INDIA Alliance has called for a united stand...' Release of the other TMC leaders with her was not separately confirmed.

The Delhi High Court Bar Association strongly condemns the 'illegal detention' of several advocates and 'disproportionate' force against lawyers, including senior advocates. It calls for an impartial inquiry and accountability (Bar & Bench, LiveLaw, 8:11–8:24 PM).

The Hindu: Ratna Singh posted at 7:13 PM, 'I am still detained. Since 9AM. There are 30 police official for one woman.' This conflicts with ANI's earlier report that she had been released at about 5:53 PM. The Hindu (8:32 PM) and The Wire (8:54 PM) say a Delhi court dismissed her wrongful-confinement plea.
Arvind Kejriwal released from Jaffarpur (Jafarpur Kalan) police station (PTI video, ~8:13 PM). Release of Sanjay Singh, Saurabh Bharadwaj and Durgesh Pathak was not separately confirmed.
Scroll: police reportedly detained more than 7,000 protesters in Delhi today, with smaller protests in Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru. Attributed to Scroll.
Police say the Jantar Mantar area remained clear of protesters. The New Delhi DCP shared a video to counter social-media claims of a large gathering there (The Hindu).
Indian Express: 245 trains cancelled, including Rajdhani and Shatabdi services.
NDTV: actor Imran Khan and his relative Zayn Marie Khan were detained at the CJP protest at August Kranti Maidan, Mumbai. She shared a video from inside the police van.

Menaka Guruswamy's Supreme Court plea is a habeas corpus petition. It challenges the detention of Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar, and other political leaders. It is to be heard on Sunday 11 Oct at the special sitting before Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana (LiveLaw). Bar & Bench says the special Sunday sitting will hear pleas against the detention of opposition leaders.

Neha Bora, AISA national president, and the other women detained with her were released from Maidan Garhi police station (India Today, ~8:30 PM). This supersedes the earlier report that her own release was not confirmed. Yogendra Yadav later wrote at 9:35 PM that he had been released from Maidangarhi police station. Prashant Bhushan and Dipankar Bhattacharya still have no individual release report.

SFI joint secretary Aishe Ghosh demanded the release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka (The Hindu live blog). The Hindu (8:55 PM) confirms Aishe Ghosh and Neha Bora were detained earlier in the day.

UN Human Rights said it was concerned by reports of mass detentions of demonstrators, protest leaders, members of civil society organisations, lawyers and journalists, before and during the day's demonstrations in Delhi, and called on authorities to ensure the right to peaceful assembly is fully respected and fulfilled (via The Hindu live blog).
Pune: police detained about 80–100 CJP protesters at Lal Mahal Chowk, where there was no police permission, and took them to Lashkar police station (IANS).
The Wire quotes Ratna Singh on the court order that dismissed her plea: 'Judge Serving Master' and 'Welcome to new India, where Sarkar can put 30 police personnel confining you...'

CJP's Ajinkya Shinde, at a joint press conference with SFI and AISF: 'We will come back tomorrow and walk towards Jantar Mantar again.' The protest will continue until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. He alleged police did not let Dipke speak to his lawyer or family after news of his grandmother's death. CJP says Dipke, Das and Ranka were taken to different locations across Delhi-NCR (The Hindu; IANS video).
IANS: Pinarayi Vijayan, CPI(M) MP John Brittas and former Kerala minister K.N. Balagopal were released from Mandir Marg police station.

Indian Express: hundreds of people were detained at Nana Chowk, near August Kranti Maidan in Mumbai, at a gathering called by Tushar Gandhi in support of CJP. Existing counts still range from about 200 (NDTV/PTI) to over 400 (Mumbai Police via ANI).
The Hindu video: BSF personnel carried Beretta MX4 submachine guns and INSAS rifles near Jantar Mantar.

Yogendra Yadav says he has been released. In his own post he wrote that he had just been released from Maidangarhi police station and was reaching Sanjay Colony police station. No other outlet had confirmed it yet. Release of Prashant Bhushan and Dipankar Bhattacharya was still not reported.

Delhi Police sources (ANI): all the detainees have been released from the detention centres except CJP leaders, and due legal process will be followed for the CJP leaders. Earlier, at 9:18 PM, police sources told IANS that most of those detained today had been released.
CPI(M): SFI general secretary Srijan Bhattacharya briefed the media at HKS Surjeet Bhawan on the next steps, with CJP, AISF and other student groups. The line was 'Not an inch back'.

CJP and student groups say they will march to Jantar Mantar every day until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns or is removed (NDTV). The Hindu (9:51 PM): CJP has called a march to Jantar Mantar again on Sunday 11 Oct. NDTV says police said heavy security will continue.
NDTV: a BJP leader's daughter was detained during the Delhi protests. She said she had been sitting in a park.
NDTV: the INDIA bloc will hold a mega protest against Gyanesh Kumar on Monday 12 Oct. Rahul Gandhi has already said INDIA bloc leaders will meet CJI Surya Kant on Monday to submit a memorandum.
PTI video: Aligarh Muslim University students were detained in Delhi during the protest. Third-party video.

Scroll: about 150 protesters picked up from Gurudwara Bangla Sahib around 3 PM were taken to Chhatrasal Stadium in north Delhi and kept about five hours. One detainee told Scroll they have now been released.

NDTV: all of about 3,000 detainees were released except Abhijeet Dipke, Dhruv Rathee and two other CJP leaders. The report says Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remained in custody. Police had said Dipke was told he could leave for his grandmother's funeral, but by evening it was not clear if he would be released.

image.alt: Police officers carrying batons move through a crowd.

timeline.e: The Supreme Court special Sunday sitting is still on. LiveLaw says the court will hear on Sunday 11 Oct the contempt petition alleging that metro shutdowns and train cancellations violated the court's 9 Oct order. The Hindu also noted the listing at 9:17 PM.
Arvind Kejriwal (his own post) asked the Prime Minister where Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka, Dhruv Rathee and Saurav Das are being held.
The Hindu: Air India has sought official clarification after police boarded flight AI 2428 and detained Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka from their seats on landing.

The Lawyers' Association for Constitution wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner alleging Supreme Court advocate Fidal Tom, who appeared with Kapil Sibal in the Supreme Court on Friday on the Delhi shutdown, was assaulted by police and is illegally detained at Sanjay Colony police station. The association seeks his release and medical treatment (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). Allegation, not a police finding.
The Hindu: with central Delhi fortified, many groups protested away from Jantar Mantar after learning leaders were detained.
All Delhi Metro station gates reopened and interchanges were restored (DMRC via IANS). Delhi Police reposted DMRC at 11:09 PM. 45 stations had been closed.

PTI (10:38 PM): CJP calls a protest at Jantar Mantar on Sunday at 10 AM, and Delhi Police has issued a traffic advisory. PTI (10:31 PM): CJP says the protest will continue across the country until Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns. IANS (10:46 PM): CJP national organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde says they will return to Jantar Mantar tomorrow; heavy police deployment remains.

NCP(SP) MP Supriya Sule, in a post reposted by CJP: "Deeply concerned by reports that Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka remain in custody, with no warrant shown." TMC MP Derek O'Brien (CJP repost, 10:44 PM): "WHERE IS ABHIJEET? 11 hours and counting."

Hindustan Times: Delhi Police posted on X that Abhijeet Dipke was "immediately" told of his grandmother's death and the funeral time and offered "possible facilitation" to travel home on humanitarian grounds. CJP replied: "Where is Abhijeet? His family wants to talk to him... last rites tomorrow morning." The same report says police say nearly 4,000 people were detained in Delhi today.

Yogendra Yadav (his own posts) says he is staying at Sanjay Colony police post over four colleagues he alleges were "brutally beaten", including an 18-year-old and a lawyer. He says lawyers were not allowed to meet them, demands immediate medical exams (MLC), and says he will not leave until they are released. His claim. He had written at 9:35 PM that he was released from Maidangarhi police station; this is not a new detention of Yadav.

CJP: "It's been 12 hours. No information. No accountability." It demands the immediate release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, disclosure of their whereabouts, and access to lawyers. They remain detained.

LiveLaw: Senior Advocate Dinesh Dwivedi was detained by Delhi Police today. He said he was "simply standing there" and "Do you think what is happening in Delhi is lawful? It is rubbish." No release reported.
Congress leader Bhupesh Baghel (ANI, Raipur) criticises Delhi Police treatment of Rahul Gandhi and the protesters.
Congress leader Udit Raj (IANS): the protest was not CJP alone; SFI, AISA and TMC were involved, and "AAP was leading it" (his claim).
Odisha Congress chief Bhakta Charan Das (ANI): protesters in Delhi were peaceful.

An account named Cockroaches of India (@CJP_for_India), which is not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, asked everyone to reach Jantar Mantar by 10 AM. Treat this as unverified. The Sunday 10 AM march itself was already reported by PTI.
India Today: lawyers detained at Yamuna Sports Complex were seen singing the national anthem, in a video shared by Congress.
DCP New Delhi (ANI) responded to a video of police wearing shoes inside Gurudwara Bangla Sahib, saying the staff were walking in a common passage. Attributed as the police's explanation.
Hindustan Times: 124 former bureaucrats defended the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision.
IANS: Mumbai's Gamdevi police registered a case against Tushar Gandhi, actor Imran Khan, Ali Bhojani and 300–400 others under BNS sections 223, 126(2) and 189 for protesting without permission.

Hindustan Times: Delhi Police posted a video on X, "Broken promises, shattered trust", explaining why they denied permission for the Jantar Mantar protest. Police say CJP broke the signed undertaking it gave during the June–July protests against then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Attributed as the police's claim. The same report says Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee are still held and everyone else was released.
IANS: CJP's Ajinkya Shinde wrote to the Delhi Police Commissioner asking where Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka are.

India Today: the INDIA bloc march in Delhi on Monday 12 Oct demands Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. PTI (12:39 AM) restates the Monday 12 Oct march against CEC Gyanesh Kumar on 'vote chori', and says a senior delegation will submit a memorandum to the Chief Justice seeking intervention.

India rejected the UN Human Rights Office's concerns as "misplaced" and an "unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India", in a statement on the India at UN account. "India is the world's largest democracy, where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by our Constitution." It also said the office "would also do well to devote comparable attention to large-scale protests elsewhere" (NDTV, Hindustan Times, IANS).

image.alt: Security personnel at barricades on Jantar Mantar Road at night

timeline.e: KC Venugopal (ANI) says the INDIA bloc will give a memorandum to the Chief Justice on Monday.

A habeas corpus petition was filed in the Supreme Court by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity (about 11:39 PM to 12:10 AM), not by CJP. It seeks production and release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka and others, their whereabouts, the legal grounds for each detention, and preservation of CCTV, police diaries and movement registers. It asks whether the Section 163 BNSS order for Parliament Street can justify detentions at the airport and in Gurugram, and it asks for the custodial status of Ratna Singh and other advocates. It says it does not seek immunity from lawful action for any separate offence. LawBeat says the plea also names Dhruv Rathee; Bar & Bench's report does not (single source). Correction: CJP later said it did not file or approve the plea, and Bharti sought to withdraw it (see 12:48 AM).

image.alt: Man in a Cockroach Janta Party T-shirt at a protest

timeline.e: The same unofficial account, @CJP_for_India (not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback), posted at 12:11 AM, quoting Neha Bora: "Another part of Delhi will become Jantar Mantar tomorrow! Stay tuned for updates." Treat this as unverified.

NDTV: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remained in custody as of 12:15 AM. The report says at least 3,000 people were detained in Delhi and that all others were released. NDTV says police told Dipke he could leave for his grandmother's funeral, but it is unclear whether he will be released. HT (11:25 PM) says the same four are still held. Social claims that Rathee has been released are unverified.

image.alt: Delhi Police personnel outside Block A, Connaught Place, after the anti-CEC protest

timeline.e: PTI restates that the INDIA bloc will hold a protest march in Delhi on Monday 12 Oct against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on 'vote chori', and that a senior delegation will submit a memorandum to the Chief Justice seeking intervention.

Correction: the Supreme Court habeas corpus plea for Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others was filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, not by CJP. CJP says it did not file it. At 12:48 AM, CJP legal cell chief Ratna Singh posted: "This petition is not filed by @Cockroachisback. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." CJP reposted that and added "Please note" (12:50–12:52 AM). Bar & Bench (12:46 AM and 12:58 AM) and LiveLaw (12:57 AM) report that Bharti has sought to withdraw the plea. Menaka Guruswamy's own habeas plea is a separate case and is unaffected.

PTI: four journalists' organisations, including the Press Club of India and the Indian Women's Press Corps, condemned the detention and harassment of several journalists covering the Delhi protests and demanded an apology and an inquiry.

The Wire: advocate Fidal Tom (spelled Fidel Tom in The Wire) and students Saurabh, Nikhil and Harsh were released by police shortly after midnight from Sanjay Colony police post (Maidan Garhi). A medico-legal examination was conducted. The Wire's account: Tom went to the post to seek the students' release, was detained himself, and was allegedly taken to a washroom and beaten by several police personnel, including a plain-clothes man (an account shared with The Wire and student activists). AISA activist Abhigyan told The Wire all four were beaten badly. The SHO told The Wire he would find out and respond. Maktoob (12:22 AM): AISA alleged Saurabh, its Jamia Millia Islamia secretary, was beaten so badly he could not walk (AISA claim). This updates the earlier report that they were still held.

image.alt: Lawyers gathered outside a police post at night

timeline.e: Yogendra Yadav (his own post) says that at 1 AM, after his colleagues were released, they returned to where the day began. He wrote that they set out to stop Jantar Mantar 2.0 and 22 Jantar Mantars sprang up in Delhi, and that the struggle will continue.

Indian Express: around 30,000 police personnel and 200 companies of paramilitary forces will remain deployed on Sunday, ahead of CJP's 10 AM march to Jantar Mantar. Barricades at Parliament Street and Jantar Mantar stay in place. A police officer said metro and train measures "could be taken depending on the situation". Police will review on Sunday evening before deciding Monday's deployment. AISA's N Sai Balaji alleged some AISA workers were "brutally beaten in detention" and not yet released as of Saturday night (AISA claim). The CJP-SFI-AISF alliance said it would call a protest in the coming days.

image.alt: Security personnel behind chained barricades on Baba Kharak Singh Marg, Saturday

timeline.e: Bar & Bench: the Supreme Court special bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana assembles at 10:30 AM today. Matters: Shailendra Mani Tripathi's contempt plea against Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chair D. Thara; Menaka Guruswamy's plea against preventive detention of opposition leaders, including four former chief ministers; and detention and alleged police excesses against lawyers, including Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat. Advocate Aman Prasad's new contempt petition is likely to be mentioned. RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha has also moved the court the same morning.

A new contempt petition in the Supreme Court against Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar was filed by advocate Aman Prasad (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). He alleges "indiscriminate violence" on 10 Oct: protesters near Jantar Mantar, INA and Dilli Haat assaulted; a protester lifted, thrown down and beaten near INA; a young advocate beaten after intervening when police allegedly pulled at a woman's trousers, with head injuries and a hospital trip in Chhatarpur Enclave; women manhandled by male officers; Scroll's Ayush Tiwari detained despite a press pass; officers without name tags; 45 of 57 metro stations shut. It relies on the court's 28 July, 18 August and 9 Oct orders. Likely to be mentioned at today's 10:30 AM sitting. These are the petitioner's allegations.
ANI video (7:39–7:40 AM) shows heavy security and barricades at Jantar Mantar. PTI video (7:24 AM) shows security beefed up near Janpath.

Police sources, via DNA (8:00 AM): Delhi Police has released over 7,000 people detained during the CJP-led protest, while Abhijeet Dipke and Saurav Das remain in custody. ET Now (~7:19 AM): all 7,000 detainees were released except Dipke, Dhruv Rathee and two others. Indian Express: a CJP statement says more than 15,000 people, including students, civil society members and political leaders, faced detention and police action (CJP claim). Police sources told IE that detainees were kept at around 30 detention centres.

RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha has moved the Supreme Court seeking urgent directions against Delhi Police's alleged illegal detentions, "abduction" and house arrests of "unarmed" protesters, student leaders, advocates, politicians and civilians (LiveLaw). He alleges "disproportionate use of police force" and "sexual harassment of women" protesters, and says the metro shutdown violated court directions. Allegations are his.

CJP legal head Ratna Singh (her own post): "Abhijeet, Ashutosh and Saurav will be produced before the Executive Magistrate at Delhi Cantt Police Station at 9 AM today. A Delhi police official informed me about this in the morning. As CJP's Legal Head, I will be at the police station along with other advocates representing us." This is the first indication of where and when the three will appear. Not yet reported by an outlet. Dhruv Rathee is not mentioned. There is no report yet on whether Dipke can attend his grandmother's funeral at 10 AM in Hingoli.

NDTV: political controversy after opposition leaders alleged police personnel inside Gurudwara Bangla Sahib disrespected the shrine's sanctity. A BJP MP defended the action, saying gurudwaras should not be used for political protests. The post does not name them. Allegation by opposition leaders; the BJP MP's response.
Senior Advocate Kapil Sibal (LiveLaw): "Tired of going to the Supreme Court again and again... I have lost trust."

The account @CJP_for_India, which is not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, posted a statement it attributed to Ratna Singh: "This petition is not filed by @CJP_for_India. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." Treat this as unverified. It is not a post from the official CJP account.
LiveLaw: Delhi Police placed Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka under preventive arrest under BNSS Sections 126 and 170. Bar & Bench reported the same at 8:32 AM.

LiveLaw: a CJP member filed a habeas corpus petition in the Supreme Court seeking production and release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others. CJP's official account has not posted this. A disavowal appeared on @CJP_for_India, which is not the official handle @Cockroachisback, and that post is unverified.
India Today, citing police sources: "No arrests have been made in the case." This was before the reports that Dipke, Das and Ranka had been placed under preventive arrest and then released.
PTI: police confirm that Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were placed under preventive arrest. Indian Express reported the same at 9:34 AM. The sections later cited are BNSS 126 and 170.
PTI: former BJP MP Kirit Somaiya urged Mumbai Police to act against actor Imran Khan for joining a Mumbai protest in support of CJP, and raised his citizenship. Somaiya's demand.
PTI: stringent traffic curbs are in force across Delhi for a second day. India Today (9:25 AM): four pleas over the Delhi shutdown are before the Supreme Court's special bench.

Hindustan Times, citing PTI: the Press Club of India, the Indian Women's Press Corps, the Delhi Union of Journalists and the Kerala Union of Working Journalists (Delhi unit) demand a public apology from Delhi Police. They say journalists from The Quint, The Wire, Scroll, Reporter TV, Navbharat Times and Newslaundry, and senior journalist Paranjoy Guha Thakurta, were detained despite showing press cards, and that some had phones and equipment seized. They called it "reminiscent of a fascist state." HT also reports that men claiming to be from Bajrang Dal threatened journalists near Palika Bazaar at 2:30 PM on Saturday; police chased them away and detained some.

image.alt: Police buses used to detain protesters near Jantar Mantar

timeline.e: Dhruv Rathee was released at about 3 AM on Sunday and handed over to his family, Hindustan Times and PTI report, citing officials. He had been picked up from Kendriya Vihar, Gurugram Sector 56, around 7:30 AM on Saturday. An unnamed police officer, quoted by PTI, said he can be detained again, or further legal action might be taken, if he tries to go to Jantar Mantar despite prohibitory orders. This corrects earlier reports, including ETV Bharat (6:48 AM) and ET Now (~7:19 AM), that he was still in custody.

image.alt: Dhruv Rathee

timeline.e: The Hindu (Vijaita Singh): the Union Home Ministry ordered mobile internet suspended within 500 metres of eight makeshift detention centres in Delhi from noon to 10 PM on 10 Oct. The order, dated 9 Oct, was issued by the Union Home Secretary under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, citing public safety and public order. The venues were Chhatrasal Stadium (Model Town), Rajiv Gandhi Stadium (Bawana), Yamuna Sports Complex, Jasola Sports Complex, Community Centre Daulatpur, Community Centre Pandwala Khurd, Jangli Ram Stadium (Nizampur, Kanjhawala) and Surajmal Stadium (Nangloi). The Hindu says around 2,500 protesters were sent to these centres and released later in the day.

image.alt: Security personnel at Jantar Mantar road

timeline.e: LiveLaw: a prohibitory order under Section 163 BNSS is in force on Bhagwan Das Road in front of the Supreme Court. Police barricades warn that force may be used if people do not disperse peacefully. The INDIA bloc has planned a march to the Supreme Court on Monday.

Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate, South West District, at Delhi Cantt Police Station (ANI video, 9:51 AM; LiveLaw, 9:35 AM; Bar & Bench, 9:39 AM).

Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released at about 10 AM on an Executive Magistrate's order at Delhi Cantt Police Station. LiveLaw (9:58 AM) reported the order as relayed by CJP legal head Ratna Singh. Bar & Bench (10:00 AM) reported the three released from detention. They had been held under preventive arrest under BNSS Sections 126 and 170. This corrects earlier reports that they were still in custody. His mother, Anita Dipke, later said he was not allowed to attend his grandmother's funeral (PTI, 11:12 AM). As of this check, the Supreme Court special bench at 10:30 AM had not started, and there was no report yet from CJP's 10 AM march.

Bar & Bench: the Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association moved the Supreme Court under Article 32 against the 10 Oct police action on lawyers near the court, alleging illegal detention and manhandling, including of women. SCAORA president Devvrat later argued that the internet was shut for 4 km, virtual courts were inaccessible, and lawyers were "lifted." Allegations are SCAORA's.

LiveLaw, citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released on condition they will not engage in a breach of the peace for one year. PTI (10:54 AM) says they must "maintain peace" for one year. Delhi Police, via ANI (10:56 AM), say the preventive arrest was under BNSS Sections 126 and 170, that all due legal procedures were followed, and that a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was taken. Police account. CJP counsel Soutik Banerjee said at 10:18 AM that all three were released. Indian Express (10:51 AM) says they walked out of Delhi Cantt police station.

The Supreme Court special Sunday sitting began before Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana. LiveLaw: the court restrained the virtual-hearing facility; petitioner-side lawyers said they would not proceed unless video conferencing was allowed; the court sat in Court No. 5. LiveLaw also reported the Solicitor General joining with senior Delhi Police officers and a virtual-hearing Webex meeting at full capacity, so the virtual-hearing position is unclear. ANI (11:06 AM) said the hearing on the detention pleas had commenced. Bar & Bench named Kapil Sibal, Gopal Sankaranarayanan, Menaka Guruswamy, Arundhati Katju, Sanjay Hegde and Anas Tanwir for the petitioners, and SG Tushar Mehta for the respondents. At 11:10 AM Justice Bagchi said the court would either pass an order that day or post the pleas to Monday. On K.K. Venugopal's contempt plea, the court indicated it would be posted to Monday. Sibal said people were picked up from trains and from outside the 4 km radius, and that the internet was suspended. Gopal Sankaranarayanan handed over video stills of action against lawyers, including Shadan Farasat, and flagged the Section 163 order outside the court.

India Today: CJP will hold a press briefing at 2 PM. Hindustan Times later said the press conference was still set for 2 PM. A post on @CJP_for_India at 11:20 AM, which is not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, attributed the 2 PM conference to Ashutosh Ranka. That post is unverified.
Indian Express: four right-wing men were arrested over a viral video showing students and women being assaulted.
PTI: security was increased in Connaught Place and police held a flag march. Hindustan Times' e-paper (10:57 AM) says CJP has called a fresh march to Jantar Mantar today.
LiveLaw: a PIL in the Supreme Court seeks scrutiny of the central Delhi internet shutdown.
PTI video: Abhijeet Dipke's mother, Anita Dipke, said, "Have they achieved anything by not allowing him to attend his grandmother's funeral." He did not attend. He was in Delhi until about 10 AM.
India Today: Delhi Police filed 20 FIRs over the 10 Oct protest, for obstructing official work and assaulting police.

CPI(M) MP John Brittas (PTI, ANI): the protest will continue "without a break" whether or not they are allowed into Jantar Mantar. He says he and Kerala's former chief minister were detained on Saturday.

Ashutosh Ranka wrote on X, in Hindi. The Wire's translation: Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar is a "traitor", and Ranka is ready to stay in jail for his entire life to get him removed. His words, after his release.

Hindustan Times: hundreds of people sheltered in Gurdwara Bangla Sahib on Saturday while police waited outside. HT also says AISA president Neha Bora regrouped protesters at Dilli Haat around 1 PM on Saturday before she and others were detained on Sri Aurobindo Marg.

Menaka Guruswamy in the Supreme Court (Bar & Bench): what is at stake is "the suspension of citizens' peacefully exercised constitutional rights." She said the last time the court had to consider such challenges was during the Emergency. Her comparison. Kapil Sibal asked for an interim order against Section 163 orders, detentions and barricades outside the 4 km zone, and said trains that were supposed to run from their origin did not (LiveLaw). K.K. Venugopal (12:01–12:02 PM) said a former junior of his was lifted into a police van, taken nine kilometres away and dropped 11 kilometres away, and could not reach the court, and that police had no badges (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). Sibal said journalists were being impeded inside and outside. These are the lawyers' accounts.

Hindustan Times: police are keeping central Delhi sealed on Sunday. Jantar Mantar is shut, borders are barricaded, and traffic is diverted at 30 points, while CJP says it will march again. CJP's Ajinkya Shinde: "We will continue our agitation till Gyanesh Kumar resigns." HT estimates about 7,000 people were detained on Saturday. That figure sits alongside the other attributed counts.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta (Bar & Bench): on the habeas pleas, "a statutory regime was followed", and "Most of these people mentioned here were picked up at 2 p.m. and they were released at around 6 o'clock." He also said there was no curtailment of Metro service on 10 Oct and no reduction in the volume of operations, with 4,157 train trips across a 303-station network. An affidavit is to follow. His submissions.

Shiv Sena's Shaina NC (ANI): "No arrest has been made; rather, preventive action has been taken." She said removing the Chief Election Commissioner is a matter for Parliament, not the streets, referring to the INDIA bloc's 12 Oct protest. Her statement. A woman lawyer fainted in the courtroom around 11:54 AM; the Solicitor General attributed it to the air circulation (Bar & Bench).

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the Supreme Court that 47 Metro stations were closed or restricted, "only 15%" (LiveLaw). Justice Bagchi noted that the authorities first proposed closing 57 and that 45 were closed after the court's 9 Oct order (Bar & Bench; LiveLaw's quote of the closed figure is 47). The bench asked for a map of the stations in the affidavit, and for the state to explain the circumstances, manner and justification of the detentions. On the Section 163 board on Bhagwan Das Road, the Solicitor General said he had just been informed of it. Justice Bagchi said that if people were not aware of the order, that was a good ground to quash it (LiveLaw).

Hindustan Times: Dhruv Rathee wrote, "I was not arrested or detained, I was KIDNAPPED." HT says he gave no undertaking to Gurugram Police. His claim. HT now says he was detained around 9:30 AM on Saturday; its earlier story said about 7:30 AM. The Hindu (10:53 AM) says he was released around 2 AM; HT and PTI, citing officials, say about 3 AM. The official account of a release at about 3 AM is unchanged. Both the release times and the pickup times are kept.

image.alt: Dhruv Rathee at Freedom Park, Bengaluru

timeline.e: After his release, Abhijeet Dipke wrote: "Modi, as PM, is an embarrassment to India. Never has this country seen a bigger coward and bully." Hindustan Times and The Wire reported the post. His words. HT says the three were detained from their seats on flight AI 2428, which landed at 10:18 AM on Saturday and was moved to remote bay R12.

image.alt: Abhijeet Dipke

timeline.e: The Supreme Court special bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana said it will pass an interim order. LiveLaw: the Metro should function normally unless a law-and-order situation arises, the public should have free movement, the internet should be restored, and lawyers should not be impeded in their professional duties. Bar & Bench quotes Justice Bagchi that no advocate should be hindered in discharging their professional duties, and that the Solicitor General's position is that Metro services are already normal unless a public-order situation arises and that the internet is already restored. SG Tushar Mehta said all Metro stations are open today. India Today's headline said barricades should be removed and the internet cannot be shut down. LiveLaw's wording is the more precise account. The full text was not out yet. The written interim order was reported by Bar & Bench at 12:51 PM.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, in Bengaluru (PTI video), criticised the arrests: "We never arrested people unnecessarily." The Wire published an explainer tracking five sets of pleas in the Supreme Court.

Bar & Bench: Justice Joymalya Bagchi began dictating the Supreme Court's interim order. The order records that the special bench assembled on urgent applications alleging violation of the 9 Oct order and illegal detention of a large number of people on 10 Oct. It records Dr Menaka Guruswamy's statement that GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya Metro stations, and others, were completely shut, which she called a deliberate and wilful violation. That is her allegation, as recorded. The state was asked to explain the detentions and to put station-wise Metro details on a map in its affidavit. At 12:03 PM the full text was still awaited. During the hearing, the court had spoken of posting K.K. Venugopal's contempt plea to Monday. Bar & Bench's report of the written order, at 12:51 PM, sets the next hearing for Tuesday 13 Oct. New detentions at Connaught Place were reported after 12:28 PM.

image.alt: Protesters, some holding Cockroach Janta Party signs, gathered outdoors.

timeline.e: Indian Express: around 60–70 protesters were detained after marching from Gate No. 6 of Palika Bazaar towards Connaught Place. This was after the Supreme Court had begun dictating its interim order.

Abhijeet Dipke missed his grandmother's funeral. PTI (12:40 PM) and Indian Express (1:02 PM): Savitribai Shankarrao Dipke, 85, died on Saturday in Hingoli district, Maharashtra, after a prolonged illness, and the last rites were performed on Sunday morning. The family says Delhi Police did not release him in time despite repeated pleas. Delhi Police said he was informed and offered help to travel home. His uncle Vilas Dipke disputed that. Both accounts are kept.

The NLSIU Alumni Association condemned the police action and the detention and manhandling of Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat, and said "over 10,000 people have reportedly been detained across the country" (their figure). It asked for an impartial inquiry (Bar & Bench, LiveLaw).

Hindustan Times: senior police officers said more than 20 FIRs were registered over attempts to protest at Jantar Mantar, including over alleged attacks on police. That adds detail to India Today's 11:14 AM report of 20 FIRs. Police cite the July CJP NEET protest, in which they say more than 200 officers were injured, a safe capacity of about 1,000 at Jantar Mantar, and notice only on 7 Oct against a 10-day requirement. That is the police account.

image.alt: Security personnel standing guard near a metro station.

timeline.e: PTI video: leaving Kapil Sibal's residence, Abhijeet Dipke said, "I am going home now to be with my family, as my grandmother has passed away. Ashutosh and Saurav will hold a press conference at 2 pm and announce the future course of action... The entire Delhi was brought to a standstill to protect Gyanesh Kumar." His words. Hindustan Times (1:28 PM) says he is heading back to his village and that CJP will not back down. The Wire (12:57 PM) quotes him: "October 10 will go down as the beginning of the end of this dictatorship." Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka's 2 PM press conference at the Press Club of India had not been reported as held as of 2:05 PM. It was later held at the Press Club; see the afternoon update. A journalist's X post at 1:30 PM described heavy police outside the club; that post is unverified.

Indian Express, updated 12:48 PM: Northern Railway restored 214 passenger trains. Thirty remain cancelled today. Friday's cancellation total was 245 trains, of which 75 were mail or express and 170 were passenger.

image.alt: A red passenger train on the tracks.

timeline.e: The Supreme Court special bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana passed its interim order. The court rose about 12:36 PM. Bar & Bench (12:51 PM): no illegal detention except by procedure established by law; Metro and trains to run normally unless regulation is needed for public order; free movement, subject to traffic rules, with barricades to be reviewed forthwith; the internet shall remain undisturbed, as per law; peaceful assembly is allowed, particularly outside the Section 163 BNSS zone; the Section 163 notice board near the Supreme Court is to come down. The court recorded an assurance that lawyers, journalists and other professionals will not be obstructed. A contempt notice was issued. A short affidavit to show cause, and a compliance report including Metro restrictions and railway advisories, are due Tuesday 13 Oct, when the habeas pleas and connected matters will also be heard. The principal contempt petition is advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi's, against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chair D. Thara. This is the written order. It replaces the earlier report that the order was still being dictated and that the full text was awaited. The signed order, uploaded at about 5:25 PM, finds a prima facie case of contempt. See that update.
Raijor Dal MLA Akhil Gogoi (ANI) welcomed the release of the CJP leaders.

Barricades outside the Supreme Court were being removed. LiveLaw (12:56 PM): lawyers asked police to remove barricades around Patiala House Courts, citing the court's directions. Bar & Bench (1:07 PM): senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan and dozens of lawyers asked police to remove barricades at Tilak Marg, and lawyers said police refused. At 1:08 PM Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said, "The barricades are now being removed." LiveLaw (1:07 PM): Delhi Police were removing barricades outside the Supreme Court premises following the judicial directions and the lawyers' requests.

Detentions continued after the Supreme Court's interim order. Indian Express (12:28 PM): around 60–70 protesters were detained after marching from Palika Bazaar's Gate No. 6 towards Connaught Place. Indian Express (1:08 PM): CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas was detained from Connaught Place; around 60 people were detained at CP's N Block; security was tightened again around Jantar Mantar, and entry into Sansad Marg was blocked again. He was later released. CPI(M) alleges he was assaulted; see the 3:46 PM update.

Kapil Sibal, after meeting Abhijeet Dipke (PTI): "deeply grateful to the Supreme Court... an order that restores the faith of the Indian people." AAP's Saurabh Bharadwaj (PTI): police "acted brutally at the government's behest... Several of them have been detained for two days." His allegation.
AAP's Gopal Rai (PTI) called the police action a "black emergency." His words.

Advocate Barun Kumar Sinha (ANI) said the Supreme Court passed only three interim orders, on the Metro, the internet and lawyers, deferred the rest to Tuesday, and did not pass a contempt order beyond seeking a response. His reading. Bar & Bench's report of the order is broader: it includes free movement, a review of barricades, peaceful assembly outside the Section 163 zone, and a contempt notice with an affidavit due on Tuesday.
Bar & Bench: Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat told the Supreme Court that the authorities' actions amounted to a "police state." His submission.

The Hindu (1:32 PM): police detained activists from various student bodies in Connaught Place. The Hindu (1:51 PM): SFI activists detained there said they were being taken to an unknown location. That is their account, from an SFI video. The Wire (2:00 PM): SFI alleges continuing police brutality against hundreds of its student activists. That is SFI's allegation.
PTI: INDIA bloc activists marched towards the Odisha Assembly in Bhubaneswar demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.

CJP's account @Cockroachisback said its leaders Ankit Bharadwaj, Anam, Mukesh all-rounder, Balakrishna and Sudhir Sangwan "got detained while protesting peacefully Today." Party claim. Not independently verified.

The Wire: CJP alleges the unlawful detention of its South India lead, Vijay Mallangi. Not independently verified. Saurav Das, via The Wire: "We are returning with full strength." His words. SFI alleges continuing police brutality against hundreds of its student activists. That is SFI's allegation.
Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar (ANI): "There was no permission for the program." His statement.

ThePrint, citing SFI: SFI president Adarsh M Saji, Delhi state secretary Sooraj Elamon, CEC member Abhijith Manilal and "hundreds" of others were detained at Rajiv Chowk while marching toward Jantar Mantar. SFI's claim. Not independently verified.
Actor Prakash Raj, in a video carried by ThePrint, criticised the Prime Minister.
Arvind Kejriwal (ThePrint) said the Prime Minister had "left Hitler behind." His words.
Dhruv Rathee (ThePrint): "I did not sign any bond, I did not sign any undertaking, I did not sign any condition for release." His words. His status is unchanged: released.

PTI, also carried by ThePrint at 3:13 PM: among more than 20 FIRs is a Kamla Market case in which four men who claimed links to the Hindu Raksha Dal were arrested for allegedly assaulting students and manhandling women during Saturday's protest. This is further detail on the four right-wing arrests Indian Express reported at 10:54 AM, not a separate set of arrests. Hindustan Times (Jignasa Sinha, posted 8:22 AM on 12 Oct): Delhi Police on Sunday apprehended four men allegedly linked to the Hindu Raksha Dal for assaulting a minor near Civic Centre during Saturday's protest. Police named Raman Saini, 50, and Vivekanand, 32, of Delhi, and Kapil Kumar, 27, and Ravinder Singh, 35, of Ghaziabad. A case of causing hurt and illegal restraint was registered suo motu from a social-media video showing a minor dragged on a road, assaulted and threatened. The men also threatened journalists. Police say no one, including the minor, complained. The accused told police they attacked because protesters had confronted them earlier. Police say the initial probe found no evidence for that claim. Both accounts are kept. Outfit chief Pinky Chaudhary, also known as Bhupender Tomar, posted support for the accused and a threat: "These are my warriors. Wherever cockroaches are found, we will fix their minds." His words. Hindustan Times got no police comment on his posts.

image.alt: Police officers escorting several men outdoors, one officer holding a man by the arm.

timeline.e: ThePrint: people who were detained described being driven around Delhi on police buses, which the report calls a "merry-go-round." Hindustan Times also reported a CJP claim that police entered Gurdwara Bangla Sahib "with shoes, weapons," and that CJP urged Sikhs to join. That is CJP's claim.

Hindustan Times: detentions continued around Connaught Place despite the Supreme Court order. About 100 protesters were packed into two buses and removed. HT also says more than 26,000 security personnel were deployed alongside Delhi Police.

image.alt: Security personnel in camouflage standing in a line at Connaught Place.

timeline.e: At the Press Club of India, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ratna Singh spoke for CJP. Das (PTI; Hindustan Times) said Delhi Police "forcefully entered" the airplane and "kidnapped" them, that there was no detention notice, that phones were seized with no seizure memo, and that they were not allowed a lawyer. He said he suspects the phones were "hacked or cloned," and that "We will not go back." On the one-year peace condition, he said the breach was done by PM Modi, Amit Shah and Gyanesh Kumar. He put the deployment at 40,000 and said more than 50 metro stations were shut. Those are his figures. Ranka (ThePrint): "The fight will continue until every single one of our demands is met." He said several CJP colleagues were detained and assaulted today and that "the entire SFI team was detained today" (ANI, 3:10 PM). CNN-News18: he said the fight is now also against PM Modi. An SFI leader at the briefing (ThePrint, 2:59 PM): "Wherever you are stopped, turn that exact place into Jantar Mantar." Ratna Singh (Hindustan Times) alleged police visited volunteers' homes and intimidated parents, and that the Intelligence Bureau followed her after she landed in Delhi. ANI (3:58 PM): she said the release conditions were the standard template, "no special conditions."

image.alt: Saurav Das speaking at a press conference, with microphones in front of him.

timeline.e: The Hindu, citing police sources: over 7,000 protesters were detained on Saturday as authorities stopped people from reaching Jantar Mantar. Attributed to police sources, not an official figure. It sits alongside the other counts, including HT's earlier estimate of about 7,000. The same report lists Ratna Singh among those released.
BJP MP Tarun Chugh (ANI): "The mood of the country is against the protesters." His statement.

John Brittas was released after being detained at Connaught Place. CPI(M), via ThePrint (2:48 PM), alleges Delhi Police brutally attacked him and later dropped him by the roadside, visibly injured. A video shows him being helped into an autorickshaw. India Today (3:46 PM) says he argued with police as they tried to detain him, and repeats the CPI(M) allegation. In a video shared on X at 3:12 PM, which no outlet has verified, Brittas says four CRPF personnel pinned him down until he struggled to breathe, and that he was released only after a DCP threatened suspension. The assault account is attributed.

ThePrint: "Dramatic scenes at Press Club of India; CJP inside, Delhi Police at door." PTI (4:27 PM) and ThePrint (4:53 PM) reported that Delhi Police issued fresh notices to the CJP leaders in an old case about a woman's allegedly morphed images circulated online, following Delhi High Court directions on her plea. CJP told NDTV (5:31 PM): "Wrong tweets attributed to us; will fight court notice legally." No fresh detention of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka or Ratna Singh has been reported. Social posts claiming Das and Ranka ran from the club are unverified; no news outlet has reported that.

AISA president Neha Bora was detained again at about 3:50 PM while leading a march from RK Ashram Marg to Connaught Place, after the Supreme Court's interim order (ThePrint, 3:53 PM; Scroll, 3:25 PM and 3:40 PM, citing videos). She had called an assembly at RK Ashram at 2:30 PM (ThePrint, 2:24 PM). Protesters allege police used brute force. AISA alleges protesters were "badly beaten." That is AISA's claim. ANI (3:34 PM) reported AISA workers detained near RK Puram. Scroll (3:34 PM) reported more journalists and bystanders being detained at RK Ashram metro station, citing reporter @knowleena.

Indian Express: three of its Hindi reporters, Shashwat, Siya and Vijay, were detained at Connaught Place and made to board a police bus despite saying they were on duty. The phones of Shashwat and Siya were seized and had not been returned. No surnames were given. This was after the Supreme Court recorded an assurance that journalists would not be obstructed. Indian Express (4:14 PM): they were released about 45 minutes later near Chhatrasal Stadium, about 12 km from Connaught Place.
Union Minister Pralhad Joshi (ANI): "They were detained because there was no permission for where they planned the protests." His statement.
PTI: more than 100 people were detained in Delhi on Sunday while marching toward Jantar Mantar. Several were dragged into buses.

Union Minister Ramdas Athawale (PTI) backed Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, said there is no need for him to resign, and accused CJP of inviting chaos. NDTV quoted Defence Minister Rajnath Singh: dissent is a right, but "spreading anarchy is not anyone's right." Their statements.

Indian Express: its three Hindi reporters, Shashwat, Siya and Vijay, were released about 45 minutes after they were detained. They were freed near Chhatrasal Stadium, about 12 km from Connaught Place, where they had been picked up. Indian Express (5:17 AM, 12 Oct) says they were picked up at Chelmsford Road, and gives Vijay's surname as Kumar.
Indian Express: two CJP members from Jharkhand dropped their plans to come to Delhi. They allege plainclothes men followed them and filmed them at Ranchi station. Their allegation.
LiveLaw: the lawyers' body Lawyers' Voice moved the Supreme Court to intervene in the contempt case. It says the CJP protests paralyse Delhi and hurt lawyers' livelihoods.

Two accounts of the release condition are kept, and they are not collapsed. Abhijeet Dipke on X at 4:26 PM, as carried by Indian Express at 5:11 PM: "Haven't signed any bond that says we won't protest. We will hit the streets again." That is his statement. Earlier, LiveLaw (10:20 AM), citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh, said an Executive Magistrate released Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on condition they would not engage in a breach of the peace for one year. PTI (10:54 AM) says the condition is that they "maintain peace" for one year. Delhi Police, via ANI (10:56 AM), say a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was taken for peace and good behaviour for one year. CJP says that bond only bars a breach of the peace, and that peaceful protest is a constitutional right. NDTV (5:56 PM): CJP vowed protests nationwide. Ashutosh Ranka: "The fight has just begun" and will not stop until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. Saurav Das: the protests will be "not just in Delhi but the whole country." CJP wants Jantar Mantar opened as a venue. SFI's Aishe Ghosh: "Jantar Mantar 2.0 is on." Their words.

PTI: Delhi Police issued fresh notices to CJP leaders in an old case about a woman's allegedly morphed images circulated online, following Delhi High Court directions on her plea. ThePrint carried the same account at 4:53 PM. This replaces the earlier line that a Press Club notice had been served but that its contents were unverified. CJP told NDTV (5:31 PM): "Wrong tweets attributed to us; will fight court notice legally."
India Today: NSUI workers were detained in Delhi while protesting against the Chief Election Commissioner.

AISA alleges that buses were turned into lockups, with cage-like doors and no air, and that protesters were beaten in their private parts and abused with casteist and misogynist slurs. A later AISA post, carried at 5:22 PM, says detainees were taken beyond barricades where journalists were denied access, phones were snatched, and male protesters were beaten. That is AISA's allegation. ThePrint (4:11 PM) carried Neha Bora from inside a bus: "Are buses the new jails?" Her words. No release report for her as of 6:10 PM.

PTI: activist Anjali Damania was detained after she reached Shivaji Park in Mumbai for a CJP solidarity protest that Ajinkya Shinde had called for 4 PM. The fuller account, including dozens of others and pickups at Dadar station, is in the 5:46 PM update.
Scroll: Mumbai demonstrators were not allowed to assemble at Shivaji Park. People were detained from Dadar station itself, and some were detained just for walking in the area.

AAP's Sanjay Singh, at a press conference (PTI, 4:57 PM; ThePrint, 5:16 PM), alleged that more than 6,000 people were detained in Delhi on Saturday and that force was used on women, lawyers and journalists. AAP's claim.

The Supreme Court's written order is out. LiveLaw and Bar & Bench: the court finds a prima facie case of contempt over the Metro and train shutdown, treated as a violation of its 9 Oct order. Notice went to the alleged contemnors. LiveLaw names Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, the Delhi Police Commissioner and the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation. Counter-affidavits and a compliance report are due on 13 Oct. Personal appearance is dispensed with for now. Notice was also issued on the habeas corpus petition. Menaka Guruswamy argued that it covers the illegal detention of about 7,000 people, not only named leaders. The order says lawyers, journalists and other professionals shall not be hindered in any manner whatsoever. Metro and trains are to run normally, subject to Article 19(2). People may move freely, and barricades are to be reviewed forthwith. The internet is not to be hindered. There is to be no illegal detention of peaceful unarmed assemblies beyond the Section 163 BNSS area, and the Section 163 board at the court is to come down. The case is listed again on 13 Oct with the other tagged petitions. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta denied any violation. He said 45 of 303 Metro stations were closed for law and order, denied that anyone was illegally detained, and called the habeas plea infructuous because detainees had been released. That is his submission, as recorded in the order.

The Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee filed a police complaint against Arvind Kejriwal and AAP MLAs and workers over the incident at Gurdwara Bangla Sahib during the protests (PTI; Indian Express, 5:30 PM). CJP's separate allegation, that police entered the gurdwara with shoes and weapons, remains CJP's claim.

NDTV: CJP said wrong tweets were attributed to it and that it will fight the court notice legally. The notice, PTI reported at 4:27 PM, is in an old case about allegedly morphed photos and follows Delhi High Court directions.

Delhi Police held a press conference and released a video of officers telling Abhijeet Dipke of his grandmother's death. DCP Neha Yadav (ANI, 5:38 PM) said they offered all possible assistance, including flights and phone calls, and that he repeatedly declined to speak to his parents. Hindustan Times: the clip shows him declining an offer to return home. That is the police account. CJP's Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das say he was denied permission to speak to his cousin and accuse the police of insensitivity. That is CJP's account. Both are kept. ANI listed the briefing as also covering alleged attacks on police; no details of that part were reported. The Tribune, with PTI, later reported that he missed the Sunday morning funeral. His uncle Vilas Dipke says the release came too late. Delhi Police deny a delay. He flew to Nagpur. See the evening update.

The protest reached Mumbai. Activist Anjali Damania and dozens of others were detained at Shivaji Park at about 4:50 PM (PTI; Tribune, 5:46 PM). She told PTI, "I do not know where they are taking me," as plainclothes police took her away in a private vehicle. Most of those detained were shifted to Shivaji Park police station. Police say they will take legal action against people assembling without permission. Scroll (5:07 PM): people were picked up at Dadar station itself, and some were detained just for walking in the area. The Tribune report also says about 600 people were detained in Mumbai on Saturday in solidarity with CJP. CJP's Ajinkya Shinde had called the Shivaji Park protest for 4 PM (mid-day). An X post by journalist Ashish Dwivedi (4:59 PM) said Damania was taken to Tardeo police station. That post is unverified.

NDTV: CJP vowed a nationwide protest after the Delhi crackdown. Ashutosh Ranka: "The fight has just begun" and will not stop until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. Saurav Das said the protests would be held not just in Delhi but across the country. Their words. Abhijeet Dipke had written at 4:26 PM that he had not signed a bond against protesting and that they will hit the streets again.

Scroll: Aaditya Thackeray climbed onto a police van outside Shiv Sena Bhavan to stop it taking protesters away. Indian Express (7:06 PM): he and Anil Parab formed a human chain near the building. The protest at the police station is in the later update.
Hindustan Times: central Delhi Metro stations, including Janpath, Rajiv Chowk and Mandi House, reopened on Sunday.

The Wire live blog, quoting Delhi Police: permission for the CJP protest was denied because of a failure to follow procedures and a history of non-compliance with the laws. That is the police account.

Indian Express: protesters gathering at Connaught Place were being detained, a second day of protests there. NDTV (6:51 PM) reported an RAF and Delhi Police flag march at Connaught Place. India Today (7:13 PM and 7:28 PM) reported a fresh anti-CEC protest at Connaught Place, several people detained, and heavy security.

ANI: senior Congress leaders are to meet on Monday. Chhattisgarh Congress chief Deepak Baij said further instructions will be issued. This is separate from Rahul Gandhi's announcement of the march to the Supreme Court.
NDTV: the Rapid Action Force and Delhi Police held a flag march at Connaught Place.
Ramdas Athawale again criticised CJP (ANI).

Rahul Gandhi announced that opposition parties, youth, civil-society groups and citizens will march to the Supreme Court on Monday 12 Oct and submit a memorandum to the Chief Justice of India (Indian Express, 6:59 PM; PTI, 7:07 PM). He says the memorandum demands an end to what he calls "vote chori", a halt to the Special Intensive Revision, and Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. He alleged that young protesters on Saturday "were beaten, both by cops and BJP goons." That is his allegation. He wrote "Daro mat" and used the hashtag #chalodilli. Separately, ANI reported a meeting of senior Congress leaders on Monday.

At a CJP press conference (The Tribune, 7:05 PM), Ashutosh Ranka said "PM Modi will save Gyanesh Kumar at any cost" and claimed the past 72 hours had "surpassed the Emergency." His words. CJP's north coordinator, Shreshth Singh Khera, told India Today (7:31 PM) that only four slogans were allowed at the Jantar Mantar demonstration.

The Hindu: actor Prakash Raj, addressing the Prime Minister, asked, "Friend, whom are you trying to save — Gyanesh Kumar or yourself?" Hindustan Times (7:36 PM) reported Bollywood celebrities voicing support for the CJP protests. K.C. Venugopal (The Hindu, 7:13 PM) accused the Prime Minister, the Home Minister and the Chief Election Commissioner of undermining democracy. His allegation.

A second evening of protests at Connaught Place brought many more detentions. Indian Express (6:32 PM) reported protesters there being detained. At 7:14 PM it reported women protesters detained in large numbers near Rajiv Chowk Metro Gate 7, with police forming a human chain around the bus they were put in. India Today reported several detentions and heavy security. No official count for Sunday evening was given. PTI had earlier put Sunday's detentions above 100. AISA (7:49 PM) says female detainees are refusing to leave until all male protesters are released. That is AISA's claim, and it is not independently verified. Neha Bora's team account posted from the protest. Unverified posts said she herself was detained again at Connaught Place. No outlet has confirmed a new detention, and there is still no release report. She stays listed as detained from the afternoon.

Abhijeet Dipke missed his grandmother's funeral. The Tribune, with PTI: Savitribai Shankarrao Dipke, 85, died on Saturday in Hingoli district, Maharashtra, and the last rites were held on Sunday morning. His uncle Vilas Dipke said, "I pleaded with the Delhi police with folded hands at least 10 times to release Abhijeet ... Though he was eventually released today, it was too late for him to attend." The family says Dipke will be present to collect her ashes. Delhi Police deny any delay. They say he was informed and offered help to travel, and that he declined. Both accounts are kept. He flew to Nagpur. At the airport, before going on to Hingoli, he said, "We will hit the streets again. We are not afraid of PM Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah ... Put me in jail a hundred times." His words. Indian Express says he had earlier left Kapil Sibal's residence saying he was going home.

image.alt: Abhijeet Dipke speaking to reporters, a bag over his shoulder, at an airport.

timeline.e: Abhijeet Dipke disputed the police video. On X at 6:31 PM he said he had asked for his phone for a couple of minutes to get his cousin's number and had asked to speak to a lawyer, and that both were refused. At 7:24 PM he wrote, "Why did you delete the part where I was asking for my phone ... and where I was asking to let me speak to my lawyers?" He accuses the police of editing the clip. His claim. State Mirror, quoting him via Neha Bora's team account, says police told him at 3:30 AM to call his father and say he was going to jail for a long time. PTI (7:52 PM), describing the video the police released: a woman officer offered him transport, and he repeatedly said "I'll stay."
The Hindu: the BJP Mahila Morcha announced a protest march on Monday 12 Oct against the Congress. It says the opposition is giving these protests political patronage.

The Quint: its journalists Swati Chopra and Mohit Manwani were detained near Shivaji Park in Mumbai, taken to Tardeo police station, and released after more than an hour. FPJ reported that student leaders from PSU and Chhatrabharati were also held. No names or release time were given for them.
BJP's Sudhanshu Trivedi (Indian Express) said CJP had "suddenly" shifted from students' issues to electoral politics, calling it a "fast mutation" and "radioactive decay." His words.

Aaditya Thackeray of Shiv Sena (UBT) and Amit Thackeray of the MNS protested outside Shivaji Park police station against the detentions (ANI, 7:29 PM; Times of India, 7:54 PM). Earlier, Scroll reported Aaditya Thackeray climbing onto a police van outside Shiv Sena Bhavan, and Indian Express reported him and Anil Parab forming a human chain there. Anjali Damania was still reported detained, with no release report.

Inshorts: YouTuber and journalist Shyam Meera Singh was detained by Delhi Police during the CJP protest, and a video showed him taken into a police van. Inshorts does not report a release. Neha Bora's team says he was detained and later released. That release is unverified and is not treated as confirmed. He is not listed as released.

Times of India (updated 7:16 PM) and The Hindu/PTI (7:04 PM): Goa Police stopped a CJP protest at Azad Maidan in Panaji before it began. Dozens were taken into custody on reaching the ground, including CJP leader Amreen Shaikh. No count was given. Former Allahabad High Court Chief Justice Ferdin Rebello, who heads Enough Is Enough, lawyers Claud and Norma Alvares, and activists Swapnesh Sherlekar and Govind Shirodkar were stopped from entering. They are not all described as detained. A protester said, "We don't know how many of them are detained because they were lifting everyone who was heading to Azad Maidan." Rebello, via PTI: "Entering Azad Maidan is not an offence." Superintendent of Police (North) Harish Madkaikar was present. Protesters then gathered outside the Goa Police headquarters. At 9:09 PM, TOI journalist Bindiya Chari posted that the Bombay High Court had ordered the detainees released. PTI, India Today, Times of India and The Goan later confirmed a Goa-bench release order. The Goan says they were released around 9:40 PM. Amreen Shaikh is listed as released.

image.alt: A crowd of protesters outdoors in Goa, many holding placards.

timeline.e: Navbharat Times: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav left Patna airport on Sunday evening for Delhi and said he was going to join the protest there. The report is of his departure from Patna, not of his arrival in Delhi. Before he left, he alleged that Delhi Police had not been enough and that BJP and RSS workers were sent against protesters, and that Delhi had been turned into a cantonment to protect one person. His allegation.

Indian Express (9:41 PM): the INDIA bloc march on Monday 12 Oct will start at 1:30 PM from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba junction and go to the Supreme Court. Rahul Gandhi confirmed the time and the place. At 9:32 PM he posted on X: "Tomorrow, 12th October, India marches peacefully as one to the Supreme Court. Students, civil society organisations, Opposition parties: Please join us to defend our democracy." Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge are seeking to give Chief Justice Surya Kant a memorandum. Kharge told reporters that he and Rahul had written to the Chief Justice and had been given a slot between 4 PM and 5 PM on Monday (PTI via ThePrint). Kharge said, "We cannot demand anything before him (Surya Kant). We will request him with folded hands." That slot is Kharge's account. The court has not published a confirmation.

Indian Express live blog, updated 10:01 PM, citing PTI: CJP's Jharkhand coordinator Khusboo Choudhary said she boarded a Ranchi–Delhi train on the night of 8 Oct, noticed about eight people following her and filming her, and was warned by a ticket examiner that she could be detained once the train entered Uttar Pradesh. She said she got off at Bokaro at about 3:30 AM and returned to Ranchi. Her allegation. She said it strengthened her resolve, and that CJP would also protest in Jharkhand. This is her named account. It is separate from the earlier report of two unnamed Jharkhand members who dropped their Delhi plans. Indian Express says railway security said they had no information.
Indian Express: Pinarayi Vijayan, in a Facebook post, called the force used against protesters in Delhi "brutal state terrorism." His words.
Scroll: a protest near Shivajinagar police station in Pune on Sunday evening, with Marathi chants calling for Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
The Hindu: DYFI and SFI protested outside the BSNL office near the Collectorate in Coimbatore.
The Wire: CPI(M) general secretary M.A. Baby said, "Modi and Amit Shah are trying to protect Gyanesh Kumar, but they will find that they won't be able to protect themselves." His words.

TOI journalist Bindiya Chari posted on X that the Bombay High Court, at an urgent Sunday-night hearing on a Goa Foundation habeas corpus plea about 7 protesters, directed that all detained protesters be released immediately. PTI (11:22 PM), India Today (10:50 PM), New Indian Express (11:16 PM), Times of India and The Goan later confirmed the Goa-bench order. The Goan says the group was released around 9:40 PM from Panaji police station. Amreen Shaikh is listed as released.

ANI: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav arrived in Delhi. He alleged "dictatorship" and "desperate attempts to shield CEC Gyanesh Kumar." His claim. Navbharat Times had earlier reported him leaving Patna airport for Delhi.

Neha Bora's team posted "SHYAM MEERA SINGH RELEASED!" and said journalist Shyam Meera Singh, detained earlier in the evening, had been released. The same account had posted at 8:33 PM that he was detained, and called journalist detentions contempt of the Supreme Court's order. Their claim. The account is partisan, and the release is unverified. Inshorts reported the detention and did not report a release. He is not listed as released.

Neha Bora's team says she sent a lookalike friend the other way while police chased her, and that she reached Connaught Place. That is her team's account, and it is unverified. Journalist Alisha Dutta posted at 9:46 PM that outside RK Ashram Metro a hijabi bystander, a woman journalist and "a Neha Bora doppelgänger" were picked up. Her post. Unverified individual posts say Neha Bora was released from Najafgarh. No outlet has confirmed a release. She stays listed as detained.
PTI: BJP MP Hemang Joshi said the so-called "Protest 2.0" had "failed miserably." His words. That is the BJP view.

PTI: Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, Leaders of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, have both written to Chief Justice Surya Kant seeking a meeting between 4 PM and 5 PM on Monday to hand over a memorandum. The demands they describe are an end to what they call "vote chori", Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, a halt to the Special Intensive Revision, and a return to paper ballots. Kharge, speaking in Bengaluru, said: "We cannot demand. Only with folded hands, we can request him ... everywhere an undeclared emergency is imposed." His words. An earlier PTI report carried by ThePrint quoted him saying they had been given the 4–5 PM slot. Both wordings are his account. The court has not published a confirmation.

The Tribune, updated 9:57 PM, with PTI: at Nagpur airport, on his way to Hingoli for his grandmother's last rites, Abhijeet Dipke said he has not signed any bond that he and other CJP leaders will not protest again. "We will hit the streets again." His words. That conflicts with CJP legal head Ratna Singh's earlier account, via LiveLaw and Indian Express, that the magistrate released Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka on condition they do not breach the peace for one year. Both accounts are kept.

image.alt: Abhijeet Dipke speaking to reporters at an airport, a bag over his shoulder.

timeline.e: Ashutosh Ranka on X: "Unbelievable stories of police brutality coming out against CJP leaders. From tomorrow, not a single CJP leader will leave detention centres without proper MLC [medico-legal certificate]." His allegation. Saurav Das at 8:51 PM accused Delhi Police of "collaborating with these sexual assaulters." His claim. India Today (9:16 PM): Abhijeet Dipke questioned an alleged 3:30 AM call in which officers asked him to tell his parents he could be jailed "for a long time." His account. ThePrint (8:47 PM): he rejected the police claim that they offered help, saying they "wanted to torment my parents." His words. DCP Neha Yadav (Indian Express, 9:19 PM) shared the police video and reiterated that permission was denied because of past non-compliance. That is the police account. Both sides are kept.

Ashutosh Ranka on X: he, Saurav Das, Ratna Singh and other CJP leaders will go to Parliament Street police station at 10 AM on Monday to get a date for a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar. "@DelhiPolice can give us a date for Jantar Mantar in 24 hours, or we will give another protest call." CJP's account repeated it at 10:21 PM. PTI (11:14 PM and 11:21 PM), Hindustan Times (11:16 PM) and Indian Express (1:00 AM) report the ultimatum. That is CJP's account.
ANI: Jan Suraaj's Prashant Kishor said, "this protest, this agitation, will continue." His words.

Abhijeet Dipke reached his ancestral village, Santuk Pimpri in Hingoli, late on Sunday night and visited the cremation ground to pay tribute to his grandmother (IANS, 10:31 PM and 11:07 PM; ANI, 12:11 AM; PTI video, 12:13 AM). NDTV (11:07 PM) carries the police video of officers telling him of her death, under the headline "We're Sorry." That video is the police account, already disputed by Dipke.

News9, updated 11:09 PM, citing people aware of the matter: Chief Justice Surya Kant declined Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge's request for a 4–5 PM meeting on Monday to hand over a memorandum. In an email reply he reportedly said the issues are already before the court, the court cannot meet political delegations at an administrative level, and they should file a petition. He stressed that the court's doors are open to everyone. This is sourced to people aware of it, not to an official statement. K.C. Venugopal told ANI, via webindia123: "The CJI has declined to meet us, provided that open avenue for giving a petition to the Supreme Court by hand or a general legal way. We respect that decision, but we are very much for marching to the Supreme Court tomorrow." His words. The 1:30 PM march from Connaught Place–Barakhamba is still on. Indian Express (12:25 AM), reporting what it learnt: the Chief Justice's reply made four points. The grievances about the Special Intensive Revision and the Chief Election Commissioner are already pending before the court. Under the constitutional scheme the court cannot take cognisance of such grievances on the administrative side.
