The court has judicial review powers under Article 32, and if a petition is filed on Monday it will be taken up the following day, Tuesday 13 Oct, when the already pending matters are listed. The court is committed to fundamental rights and its doors are always open. The march is still set for 1:30 PM from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba Road junction to the Supreme Court, about 2 km.

The Bombay High Court (Goa bench) ordered the release of CJP activists detained at Azad Maidan in Panaji. Justices Valmiki Menezes and Amit Jamsandekar held a special Sunday-evening hearing on habeas corpus pleas by Melisa Simoes and Rui Gomes Pereira. Senior Advocate Norma Alvares appeared with Om D'Costa. Alvares, via PTI, said the hearing ran from about 7:30 PM to 8:45 PM. Times of India quotes the court: "Considering that there are no prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the BNSS, we are of the opinion that the detention may not have been authorised." The bench was told an executive magistrate gave oral instructions to detain them because they "barged into" Azad Maidan. The court did not rule on whether the detention was correct. The public prosecutor assured the court they would be released. Alvares gave an undertaking that they would not protest at Azad Maidan on Sunday night only. The Goan: they were released around 9:40 PM from Panaji police station after a bus brought them back from Pernem police station. Times of India and The Goan name seven: Jack Sukhija, Amreen Shaikh (Times of India spells the name Afreen), Aditya Parulekar, Bhupesh Bind, Liston Noronha, Shamiro or Shamino Fernandes, and Milind Rane. PTI and India Today say six. Both counts are kept. The court ordered the Panaji and Pernem station in-charges to file affidavits on the reasons for the detention and on why the peaceful protest was not allowed. Further hearing Monday 12 Oct at noon (The Goan). A medical exam at Goa Medical College was offered because two were reportedly injured (Alvares). Alvares also argued that Shaikh, a woman, could not be detained after 6 PM (Times of India). Jack Sukhija, after release, told PTI that phones were taken away and they were not allowed to contact anyone. His claim. This confirms the 9:09 PM post by TOI journalist Bindiya Chari. PTI reported it at 11:22 PM, India Today at 10:50 PM, and New Indian Express at 11:16 PM.

Saurav Das posted an SOS: the whereabouts of CJP national spokesperson Sudhir Sangwan and joint secretary Balakrishnan Shukla are unknown, and efforts to locate them have failed. Ratna Singh had said at 8:43 PM that Delhi Police detained them from Connaught Place on Sunday evening. CJP asked at 10:48 PM where they were being held and said they could not contact their lawyers. CJP's claims. No police response found. As of 6:00 AM they are listed as whereabouts unknown per CJP.
IANS: CJP state spokesperson Konda Garry Matthews says CJP is protesting at Dharna Chowk, Indira Park, in Hyderabad. His account.
ANI: rain in parts of Delhi. Its visuals are from Jantar Mantar.

The Hindu, citing PTI, at 4:56 AM: DMRC said that for security reasons, entry and exit will be closed from 6 AM to 4 PM on 12 Oct at Patel Chowk, Janpath, Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House, Central Secretariat and Barakhamba Road. Trains will run, and interchange will be available. Security agencies will review the closure. DMRC posted this at about 2:11 AM. Delhi Traffic Police, in a Sunday-night advisory carried by ANI via Lokmat Times and by LatestLY, said diversions from 6 AM Monday, depending on the situation, at about 30 points in New and Central Delhi. Those points include Mandi House, Patel Chowk, Ashoka Road–Jantar Mantar Road, Tolstoy–Janpath, the Outer Circle Connaught Place–Barakhamba Road and Sansad Marg crossings, RML Hospital and the Dhaula Kuan flyover. Commuters were asked to avoid non-essential travel and to allow extra time for stations, ISBTs and the airport.

Today's schedule, as of 6:00 AM. CJP leaders say they will be at Parliament Street police station at 10 AM for a Jantar Mantar date. The Bombay High Court (Goa bench) hearing continues at noon, with police affidavits due. The INDIA bloc march is still set for 1:30 PM from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba junction to the Supreme Court. The 4–5 PM meeting with the Chief Justice was declined, according to News9, citing people aware of the matter. The Delhi High Court Youth Congress plea and the Madhya Pradesh High Court hearing on the Itarsi detentions are also listed for today. No news on either yet.

Indian Express: Delhi Traffic Police advised restrictions and diversions around Deen Dayal Upadhyay Marg, ITO and adjoining areas from 10 AM to 2 PM on 12 Oct "due to a scheduled demonstration." The organiser is not named. This is separate from the overnight advisory on about 30 points in New and Central Delhi.

John Brittas told Indian Express: "CRPF men forcefully detained me and threw me in a bus. They pinned me to a seat after grabbing me by the neck and choked me. It was only after a Delhi Police DCP's intervention that I was allowed to go." Indian Express says RAF and Delhi Police detained him at Connaught Place while he spoke to the media, and that he was taken to RML Hospital for treatment. His account.

Indian Express: Kerala's Congress government will move a resolution in the state Assembly on Monday 12 Oct urging the Union government to remove Gyanesh Kumar as Chief Election Commissioner. Indian Express says the Assembly bulletin lists it to be moved by V.D. Satheesan, and that Kerala will be the first Assembly to seek the CEC's removal. In September last year the then LDF government passed a resolution against rolling out the Special Intensive Revision. Times of India, the Economic Times and Indian Express: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan is to move it under Rule 118 on the opening day of the Assembly's second session. Besides removal of the Chief Election Commissioner, it seeks reinstatement of eligible voters struck off during the Special Intensive Revision and changes to the selection panel for Election Commissioners, including restoring the Chief Justice of India, per India Today. The Economic Times says the opposition LDF has decided to back it, so passage is expected, and gives the House as UDF 102, LDF 35 and BJP 3 in a 140-member Assembly. The Economic Times notes a state Assembly resolution is not binding. Under Article 324(5) a Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner of a Supreme Court judge, by a special-majority motion in Parliament. It was not reported as passed as of 12:10 PM. Update, about 12:52–1:29 PM: The Hindu (updated 2:14 PM), Hindustan Times and ThePrint report that the Keralam Legislative Assembly passed the resolution. UDF and LDF supported it. The BJP objected and proposed amendments that were rejected. Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan accepted Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan's amendment changing "lakhs" of excluded voters to "crores". The resolution also seeks steps to improve the Election Commission's transparency and a selection panel that includes the Chief Justice of India alongside the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition, citing an earlier Supreme Court order. A state Assembly resolution is still not binding. Under Article 324(5) a Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner of a Supreme Court judge, by a special-majority motion in Parliament. Separately, PTI (about 2:49 PM) reported Satheesan denying political vendetta in a Vigilance probe into allegations linked to a road project involving Gyanesh Kumar when he was Kerala PWD secretary: "It is not political. There is no political vendetta." His words.
ANI: Haryana Congress MLAs and MPs gathered at Bhupinder Singh Hooda's residence to join the INDIA bloc march.
Security was tightened at Jantar Mantar and Sansad Marg, with a heavy police deployment (PTI video, 8:38 AM; ANI, 8:50 AM; IANS, 8:56 AM).

As of 9:00 AM. Still due today: CJP leaders at Parliament Street police station at 10 AM; the Bombay High Court (Goa bench) hearing at noon; the INDIA bloc march at 1:30 PM from Connaught Place–Barakhamba; the Kerala Assembly resolution on removing the Chief Election Commissioner; and the Delhi High Court Youth Congress plea. Metro entry and exit at six stations stay closed until 4 PM. Sudhir Sangwan and Balakrishnan Shukla: no update since CJP's SOS. They stay listed as whereabouts unknown per CJP.

The Hindu's live blog (8:03 AM), citing The Hindu of 11 Oct: DYFI president A.A. Rahim MP says the Democratic Youth Federation of India will move the Supreme Court over alleged illegal detention and custodial torture of its activists. That is DYFI's allegation. Update, about 1:49 PM: The Hindu's live blog says Rajya Sabha MP A.A. Rahim has moved the Supreme Court. The plea alleges illegal detention, "secret transportation" in specialised compartmentalised vehicles, and custodial torture of DYFI office-bearers and activists by police on 11 Oct at Connaught Place. That is DYFI's allegation.

PTI, via The Hindu (9:41 AM), citing police sources: Delhi Police filed an FIR against Arvind Kejriwal and other AAP leaders on the Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee's complaint over the alleged ruckus at Gurdwara Bangla Sahib on 11 Oct. The committee alleges AAP workers protested inside and misused the gurdwara for politics, and that AAP leaders circulated a distorted version on social media. Police say footage is being examined. That is the police and committee account. No AAP response was found in this report.

ANI, via The Hindu: the Himachal Pradesh Congress held a protest march at Himachal Bhawan in Delhi against the Chief Election Commissioner. Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu (ANI, 11:05 AM; IANS, 11:30 AM) says Congress will give memoranda to constitutional bodies. His words.

Bar & Bench (10:12 AM) and LiveLaw (10:32 AM): the Karnataka State Youth Lawyers Forum and others called a protest near the Karnataka High Court's Golden Gate on Tuesday 13 Oct, in solidarity with lawyers and students detained in Delhi.

In Hingoli, Abhijeet Dipke (PTI video, 10:16 AM; IANS, 10:29–10:32 AM) said: "Delhi Police, if you have the courage, release the entire video in which I repeatedly asked them to let me speak to my cousin, give me my phone for two minutes and allow me to speak to my lawyer." He also said police may have felt ashamed of alleged molestation by male officers and so used female officers. That is his allegation. On X, via PTI and The Hindu (11:13 AM), he wrote: "Youth are being assaulted, journalists are being assaulted, even MPs are being assaulted by Delhi Police. What makes Gyanesh Kumar so indispensable to Modi that he is willing to wage war against everyone just to protect him?" His words. The police account, already on his card, is that he was offered help and declined.

Chief Justice Surya Kant, speaking to reporters after the National Human Rights Commission's 33rd Foundation Day (New Indian Express; Indian Express, 10:47 AM): "I received a letter yesterday regarding a meeting request, and I responded to it last night, outlining the reasons why I will be unable to meet." He also said: "The Supreme Court's doors are open to everyone. Any petition from any common citizen or member of an elected body is welcome. Every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court, and we will hear their concerns and grant whatever is due under the law." This is the first on-record confirmation by the Chief Justice himself. Earlier reports were attributed to people aware of the matter. In open court, The Hindu's Krishnadas Rajagopal (11:36 AM) reported him saying that democratic and political protests need to take place, but the "Supreme Court should not be dragged into it" and "There should not be any inconvenience caused to litigants, lawyers, court staff." The 1:30 PM march is still on. The 4–5 PM meeting remains declined.

The Supreme Court Bar Association mentioned before Chief Justice Surya Kant's bench its petition on the detention of lawyers and the internet suspension during the anti-CEC protests (LiveLaw, about 11:01 AM). Senior Advocate Nadkarni said a lawyer he represents has also filed (LiveLaw). IANS (11:18 AM): the Bar Association filed the petition, and the hearing is tomorrow. PTI, via The Hindu (11:52 AM): a bench of Chief Justice Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana agreed to hear tomorrow petitions including the Bar Association's, after its president, Senior Advocate Pradeep Rai, raised issues including internet restrictions. The Chief Justice said: "Democratic activities must take place smoothly, but there should be no obstruction to the functioning of the Supreme Court or movement of lawyers, court staff and litigants." PTI, via The Hindu (about 1:54 PM): the Chief Justice also said every lawyer has the right to participate in peaceful protests at designated locations, and the bench agreed to hear pleas against alleged police excesses tomorrow.

Government and party responses, their words. Shiv Sena's Shaina NC (ANI, 10:54 AM): "The Chief Justice of India, Surya Kant has already said that the matter is sub judice, so Rahul Gandhi, stop your drama." BJP's Ram Kadam (PTI, 11:06 AM) said opposition leaders "do not understand the difference between the judiciary and the executive." Bihar BJP chief Sanjay Saraogi (IANS, 10:01 AM) called it a "cheap spectacle of creating chaos on the streets and putting pressure on the Election Commission." West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh (Mint): "Are they now going to try to intimidate the Supreme Court too? No one is above the law."

Three Delhi High Court matters were listed for Tuesday 13 Oct. Justice Amit Mahajan began hearing the Youth Congress plea for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar around 11:35–11:39 AM. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, for Delhi Police, sought time until tomorrow for instructions, and the plea was adjourned to 13 Oct (Bar & Bench, 11:40–11:41 AM; LiveLaw, 11:40 AM and 11:48 AM). A plea challenging the closure of Jantar Mantar, saying no alternative site has been earmarked, was mentioned before the Acting Chief Justice's bench around 11:03 AM and listed for 13 Oct (LiveLaw, 11:03 AM; PTI, 11:21 AM; ANI, 11:35 AM). The Hindu (11:19 AM) says the High Court declined to hear it today because the Supreme Court is already seized of the matter. A separate plea alleging harassment of protesters by outsiders on 10 and 11 Oct will also be heard tomorrow (The Hindu). Acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambre agreed to list tomorrow an NSUI plea seeking a special investigation team into violence against protesters on 10 Oct (Bar & Bench, 11:12 AM).

Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das reached Parliament Street police station (IANS, 11:36 AM; Hindustan Times, 11:47 AM; The Hindu, 11:49 AM; PTI, 11:52 AM). The Hindu (published 10:48 AM) reported that security was tightened outside the station, and that a public-address system warned of prohibitory orders and told people to avoid unauthorised gatherings. The Hindu restates Delhi Police's 9 Oct reasons for denying permission: non-compliance with an earlier undertaking, short notice, the 10-day advance-application rule, and law-and-order and traffic concerns. That is the police position. Ranka (IANS and PTI): "We are going to ask Delhi Police for a date to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar. We hope the police will give us a date. If they do not, we will make another call within 24 hours." Saurav Das (ANI, 11:31 AM, and Hindustan Times, 11:49 AM): "Police tells everyone to approach them 10 days in advance. We are now saying that they have the choice to tell us the date and time ... We are giving them 24-hour ultimatum." Das (IANS, 11:40 AM): "Peaceful protest is a right, a constitutional right, and people are already exercising it." Their words. No police response or outcome was reported as of 12:10 PM.

image.alt: Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das standing outside a police station, speaking to reporters.

timeline.e: Rahul Gandhi left his residence around 11:49 AM for a press conference at Indira Bhawan (ANI; IANS, 12:03 PM). The press conference itself was not yet reported. NDTV's live coverage says Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav are expected to join the march. Sanjay Raut (IANS, 10:09 AM) said all INDIA bloc parties will walk. Congress MP Praveen Chakravarty (IANS, 11:12 AM): "CJP is welcome to protest ... all of us are fighting for the same issue." His words. The march is still set for 1:30 PM from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba junction. Update: the press conference was held at Indira Bhawan from about 12:17 PM to 1:30 PM. Rahul Gandhi said the Chief Justice had instructed them to file a petition, and that he and INDIA bloc leaders would go to the Supreme Court to file one, instead of submitting a memorandum. As of 3:06 PM the filing itself was not confirmed in the wire copy used here.

As of 12:10 PM. CJP's 24-hour ultimatum to Delhi Police for a Jantar Mantar date began around 11:50 AM, with no police outcome yet. Rahul Gandhi's press conference at Indira Bhawan was imminent. The INDIA bloc march is still set for 1:30 PM. The Kerala Assembly resolution is pending and not reported as passed. The Bombay High Court (Goa bench) noon hearing and the Madhya Pradesh High Court hearing on the Itarsi detentions have no outcome yet. Tomorrow, 13 Oct: the Supreme Court hears the Supreme Court Bar Association plea and related petitions; the Delhi High Court hears the Youth Congress plea, the Jantar Mantar closure plea, the outsiders-harassment plea and the NSUI special-investigation plea; and Bengaluru lawyers have called a protest. Neha Bora: still no outlet-confirmed release. Sudhir Sangwan and Balakrishnan Shukla: no update since CJP's SOS. They stay listed as whereabouts unknown per CJP. Metro entry and exit at six stations stay closed until 4 PM.

The Keralam Legislative Assembly passed a resolution seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar (The Hindu, updated 2:14 PM; Hindustan Times; ThePrint). Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan moved it. The House took it up from about 12:52 PM and it had passed by about 1:29 PM. UDF and LDF supported it. The BJP objected and proposed amendments that were rejected. The resolution seeks Kumar's removal, steps to improve the Election Commission's transparency, action by the Centre and the Commission on defects in the Special Intensive Revision, restoration of voting rights to eligible voters wrongly excluded, and a selection panel that again includes the Chief Justice of India alongside the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition, citing an earlier Supreme Court order. Satheesan accepted Opposition Leader Pinarayi Vijayan's amendment changing "lakhs" of excluded voters to "crores". A state Assembly resolution is not binding. Under Article 324(5) a Chief Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner of a Supreme Court judge, by a special-majority motion in Parliament. Separately, PTI (about 2:49 PM) reported Satheesan denying political vendetta in a Vigilance probe into allegations linked to a road project involving Kumar when he was Kerala PWD secretary: "It is not political. There is no political vendetta." His words.

At a press conference at Indira Bhawan, about 12:17–1:30 PM, Rahul Gandhi said the INDIA bloc will file a Supreme Court petition against the Chief Election Commissioner and alleged "vote chori", instead of submitting a memorandum to the Chief Justice. New Indian Express, NewsDrum, India Today and The Hindu quote him: "The Honourable CJI has instructed us to file a petition and INDIA bloc leaders and I will go to the Supreme Court to file this petition." He asked Gyanesh Kumar to "Resign, turn approver; you have made a mistake but you are not the mind behind the mistake." He claimed about 200 government officers are "in touch" and providing information. That is his claim. He also described Delhi as a "fortress" and asked, "Why is capital city of India in jail?" India Today said the petition was planned for around 3 PM, with the march from Connaught Place–Barakhamba at 1:30 PM. As of 3:06 PM the filing itself was not confirmed in the wire copy used here.

The Hindu's live blog (about 1:49 PM): Rajya Sabha MP A.A. Rahim has moved the Supreme Court over alleged illegal detention, "secret transportation" in specialised compartmentalised vehicles, and custodial torture of DYFI office-bearers and activists by police on 11 Oct at Connaught Place. That is DYFI's allegation. This is the filing he had said DYFI would make.

Delhi Police have de-notified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Commissioner Anurag Kumar's order is dated 11 Oct 2026 and was made public on 12 Oct between about 1:47 and 2:01 PM. It partially modifies Standing Order No. L&O/48/22 of 28 Apr 2022. The police and Home Ministry account, via PTI, Indian Express, India Today, The Hindu and News On AIR: the Ministry of Home Affairs set up a committee to examine other venues for protests, and on that committee's recommendation Jantar Mantar has been de-notified. Three sites are designated instead: Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground, and CBD Ground, East Delhi. A detailed revised procedure for the three venues is to be issued separately. Indian Express and India Today both describe the new sites as farther from the central administrative area and Parliament. They agree Ramlila Ground is about 3 km from Jantar Mantar. They differ on the other two: Indian Express puts CBD Ground more than 26 km to the northeast and Burari about 16 km to the northwest; India Today puts CBD Ground at 13.5 km and Burari at 44 km. Both distance sets are kept. The announcement came hours after CJP leaders asked Parliament Street police for a Jantar Mantar date and gave a 24-hour ultimatum around 11:50 AM. The order itself is dated the day before.

PTI (about 2:48 PM) shows Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka submitting a letter to the DCP at Parliament Street police station, seeking permission for a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar. This follows the 24-hour ultimatum they gave at the station around 11:50 AM. No date from police was reported as of 3:06 PM.

PTI, via The Hindu (about 2:50 PM): the Delhi High Court asked city police to file a status report on civil rights activist Mohammad Wasiq Nadeem Khan's allegation that he was illegally detained to stop him attending a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar, and that he was under constant surveillance and phone calls. A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma issued notice. Orally, the court acknowledged that police may refuse permission for a protest, and questioned entering his house and confining him: "How can you enter the house of this man? ... Where is your cause to confine him?"

Reactions to the de-notification, their words. Saurav Das (PTI, about 2:52 PM, and Indian Express): "Unacceptable. Why is Narendra Modi scared of Jantar Mantar? The Jantar Mantar belongs to the people of India. Did the Ministry of Home Affairs consult with the people of India? Were any stakeholders consulted? Were any organisations consulted?" He also said: "We do not accept this arbitrary decision. It is an assault on people's fundamental right to protest and peaceful assembly. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar ban raha he." Abhijeet Dipke on X (about 1:46 PM): "They have removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Yes, it's no a longer protest site as anyway it was turned into a war zone by the coward dictator. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!" About 1:59 PM: "Today, Modi denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Tomorrow, he will denotify democracy itself. The dictator's problem was never the protest site. It was the very idea of people protesting." PTI (about 2:24 PM), from Hingoli, carried his separate allegation that Delhi Police subjected him and his family to "mental torture" and that his relatives and lawyer did not know where he was during the 10 Oct detention. The police account already on his card is that officers told him of his grandmother's death and offered help. Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi (PTI): "They are scared and are aware that they are not going to remain in power for long." Prashant Bhushan wrote that the government wants to push protests to the outskirts. His comment. Some BJP-aligned commentary calls the change a law-and-order and traffic measure. That is commentary, not the text of the order.

Government responses, their words, via PTI and The Hindu. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis (about 1:42 PM) accused the Opposition of trying to "demonise" judicial institutions after the Chief Justice declined a meeting, and called the march "anti-constitutional." Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi (about 1:51 PM) defended the Special Intensive Revision as necessary for electoral integrity and clean rolls. Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan (about 3:00 PM) called Rahul Gandhi's march to the Supreme Court "drama" and said Congress is trying to create anarchy by spreading falsehoods.

The INDIA bloc march toward the Supreme Court was underway as of about 3:05 PM. From about 2:30 PM, opposition MPs gathered at the Constitution Club. A bus carrying Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and others went to the Barakhamba Road junction (PTI video, about 3:03 PM). ANI reported the march getting underway and leaders heading to the Supreme Court. The Hindu's photograph, about 2:45 PM, shows lawyers in the crowd. Around 2:25 PM The Hindu reported police forming a row before Congress protesters at Barakhamba. CPI's D. Raja (ANI): "MPs will be marching. But inside the Supreme Court, 10 leaders will sign the petition and submit it on behalf of the INDIA bloc. I am one of the signatories." That is his account of the plan. The filing itself was not confirmed in the wire copy used here as of 3:06 PM. Hindustan Times (about 12:01 PM) quoted CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka saying the CJP team "will be there" in solidarity. March coverage as of this check is INDIA-bloc-led.

image.alt: A dense crowd of protesters marching on a city street, many in white shirts and caps, with placards and a large Indian flag.

timeline.e: As of 3:06 PM. Jantar Mantar has been de-notified as a designated protest site. The named alternatives are Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground, East Delhi. CJP rejects that decision. The 24-hour ultimatum given at Parliament Street around 11:50 AM is still running, and police had not given a date. The Keralam Assembly resolution seeking removal of the Chief Election Commissioner has passed. It is not binding. The INDIA bloc march from the Constitution Club and Barakhamba Road toward the Supreme Court was underway, to file a petition. The filing was not confirmed in the wire copy used here. Tomorrow, 13 Oct: the Supreme Court hears the Bar Association plea and related lawyer and internet pleas; the Delhi High Court hears the Youth Congress plea, the Jantar Mantar closure plea, the outsiders-harassment plea and the NSUI special-investigation plea; Bengaluru lawyers have called a protest. Neha Bora: still no outlet-confirmed release. Sudhir Sangwan and Balakrishnan Shukla: no update since CJP's SOS. They stay listed as whereabouts unknown per CJP. Metro entry and exit at six stations stay closed until 4 PM.
ANI (about 2:30 PM): students of New College in Chennai protested inside the campus, seeking the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.

Congress's Jairam Ramesh (PTI, via The Hindu, about 3:38 PM) called the de-notification of Jantar Mantar a sign of "extreme panic" by "the PM-HM duo", and said: "Democracy no longer matters for them. It is all a matter of Demokursi." His words.

PTI (about 3:46 PM), via The Hindu: the CPI(M) Central Committee says it will intensify the struggle against the Special Intensive Revision, condemns Delhi Police action, and demands that the Chief Election Commissioner resign, that the revision be withdrawn, and that the law on appointing Election Commissioners be repealed. It alleges bulk Form-7 filings by BJP workers to delete genuine voters. That is CPI(M)'s allegation.
The Telegraph (about 3:47 PM): Indians abroad held protests seeking Gyanesh Kumar's resignation in London, Berlin and Amsterdam.

LiveLaw (about 4:31 PM): 100 Harvard University alumni issued a statement condemning "police brutality, unlawful detention, and violations of constitutional rights of all peaceful protestors" in Delhi on 10 Oct. Their statement.

Police stopped the INDIA bloc "March for Democracy" at barricades on Bhagwan Dass Road, metres short of the Supreme Court. The Hindu says the march began from Barakhamba Road at about 4:04 PM. PTI, via The Hindu, the Economic Times and Zee News, say police stopped it at about 4:37 PM. About 5:22 PM, The Hindu reported more barricades on Bhagwan Das Road. About 5:34 PM, police started pushing protesters back near Barakhamba Road. Zee News says thousands joined and that stretches of Mandi House and Barakhamba Road were brought to a standstill. Economic Times and PTI name Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, D. Raja of the CPI, M.A. Baby of the CPI(M), Tejashwi Yadav of the RJD, Supriya Sule of the NCP-SP, Sanjay Raut of Shiv Sena (UBT), Dipankar Bhattacharya of the CPI(ML), E.T. Mohammed Basheer of the IUML, and Akhilesh Yadav of the Samajwadi Party. The Hindu also reported lawyers joining at about 4:25 PM, Congress MLA Vinesh Phogat at about 4:47 PM, and Shashi Tharoor at about 5:33 PM. No report of detentions of these leaders at the march was found as of 6:15 PM. PTI lists the bloc's demands as removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, an immediate halt to the Special Intensive Revision, and an end to police repression against democratic voices. Their words: K.C. Venugopal (IANS, about 6:15 PM), "this is only the beginning... this type of agitation will be repeated across the country until Gyanesh Kumar goes." Akhilesh Yadav (about 4:34 PM): "Democracy will be saved if the BJP is removed." Shashi Tharoor: "Protecting democracy is above any politics." Charanjit Singh Channi (ANI, about 6:02 PM) alleged that voter lists were rigged in Haryana, Assam and Bihar. That is his allegation.

image.alt: Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra walking at the front of a street march, with police and a crowd behind them.

timeline.e: Delhi Police posted a video at about 4:46 PM, captioned "Beyond the chaos & hate you see online, the reality speaks for itself." India.com describes it as officers distributing food and water and assisting detained demonstrators, prompting "Delhi Police Zindabad" chants. That is the account attached to the police video.

Abhijeet Dipke wrote on X at about 5:04 PM: "If Modi thinks taking away Jantar Mantar will put an end to protests, he is mistaken. Jantar Mantar is not just a location but a spirit of resistance..." His words. Indian Express published the text of CJP's letter to Delhi Police. CJP asks police to de-escalate the deployment, which CJP puts at more than 55,000 police and paramilitary, to stop what it calls illegal detentions and harassment of journalists, and to choose a date for a protest at Jantar Mantar. CJP says that if there is no response within 24 hours it will announce a new date for a mass protest. That is CJP's letter. The ultimatum was given at Parliament Street around 11:50 AM. As of 6:15 PM, no police response was reported.

Delhi Metro (5:04 PM): "entry and exit gates of all Metro Stations of the Delhi Metro network are now open. The interchange facility at all the concerned Metro stations is also available." The Hindu's live blog carried that at 5:07 PM. India Today also says the six stations that had been closed reopened.

Delhi Police issued a "FACT CHECK" at about 5:05 PM, calling a viral claim that police fired on Rahul Gandhi's rally and killed five workers a rumour and fake news, and warning of legal action. No news outlet reported any firing. The police account is that the claim is false.

Rahul Gandhi's lawyer, Advocate S. Prasanna, filed the INDIA bloc petition in the Supreme Court on his behalf, because Gandhi could not reach the court by the 4:30 PM physical-filing cut-off (IANS; Prasanna confirmed this to ANI, via the Economic Times, updated 4:56 PM). The legal team had first asked the Supreme Court registry to extend that deadline (India Today, Zee News). India Today's live coverage says the petition is officially registered on the Supreme Court website. The Hindu (Krishnadas Rajagopal, about 5:07 PM; also the paper's top-news item, published 6:08 PM) says the plea seeks an independent committee to inquire into the Special Intensive Revision and the Election Commission's decision-making on it, a re-look at online voter registration and services such as the ECINet portal, and an order calling for the Commission's records and official notings on the revision. The Hindu says it is also filed by Mallikarjun Kharge, Trinamool Congress MP Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and RJD's Tejashwi Prasad Yadav. Earlier, IANS via DNA, citing sources, said the court had agreed to let Gandhi and five to ten leaders, with lawyers, submit the petition at the filing counter outside the high-security area, and that the Chief Justice had agreed to that arrangement. That is a sources account. No hearing date was confirmed in the reports used here.

BJP spokesperson Harsh Singh Dahiya (News18, about 6:15 PM), on the de-notification: "The venue has changed but the right to protest remains - the new sites will be convenient for protestors as well." His words. Punjab Assembly Speaker Kultar Singh Sandhwan (IANS, about 6:15 PM), on Delhi Police entering Gurdwara Bangla Sahib: "they are deliberately trying to intimidate people." His words.

As of 6:15 PM. The INDIA bloc petition has been filed in the Supreme Court. No hearing date was confirmed. Police stopped the march at Bhagwan Dass Road. No detention of the leaders there was reported. Delhi Metro reopened entry and exit at all stations at 5:04 PM. Jantar Mantar stays de-notified. CJP's 24-hour ultimatum, from about 11:50 AM, still has no police response. The Keralam resolution has passed and is not binding. Neha Bora was seen leading the march. Her exact release time was not reported. Sudhir Sangwan and Balakrishnan Shukla: no update since CJP's SOS. They stay listed as whereabouts unknown per CJP. Tomorrow, 13 Oct, remains as already listed: the Supreme Court hears the Bar Association plea and related lawyer and internet pleas, and the Delhi High Court hears the Youth Congress plea, the Jantar Mantar closure plea, the outsiders-harassment plea and the NSUI special-investigation plea. Bengaluru lawyers have called a protest.

Dhruv Rathee told The Lallantop, reported by India Today (updated 12:16 PM), that he wants to join the INDIA bloc march to the Supreme Court but alleges about 50 police outside his residence. He said: "I want to join the protest but they (police) have stationed around 50 people outside my house. Wherever I go, they follow me and threaten me, saying that if I go anywhere near a protest, they would pick me up immediately again." He also said three or four cars follow him. Asked if this was house arrest, he replied: "Unofficially, I would say so." His claim. No police confirmation was found in this check. He dismissed visa-investigation talk: "I am an Indian citizen, there is no visa issue for me." His words. This is separate from his Saturday detention and his release early on Sunday. India Today credits the photograph to PTI.

image.alt: Dhruv Rathee speaking into a megaphone, with a crowd behind him.

timeline.e: Supreme Court Observer (3:11 PM): the Supreme Court Bar Association notified one minute of silence on 13 Oct at 1:15 PM before the Gandhi statue, in solidarity with advocates it says were mistreated and manhandled by police. Participants were asked to wear a white ribbon.

NDTV (published 4:52 PM, updated 6:06 PM): the Supreme Court registry "has been directed to process the petition today" and "to rectify any defects so that the matter can be listed for hearing on Tuesday." NDTV says a bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant "will likely hear" Rahul Gandhi's petition on Tuesday, and ties that to the Chief Justice's earlier response that a Monday filing would be heard the next day. NDTV's copy does not name who directed the registry. This is a media report. It is not a cause-list confirmation. The 6:15 PM check on this page had not treated any hearing date as confirmed.

After Advocate S. Prasanna filed the petition earlier in the afternoon, Rahul Gandhi entered the Supreme Court premises. Supreme Court Observer (6:30 PM): he arrived shortly after the filing was reported, and a crowd near the gates chanted "Rahul Gandhi Zindabad" as he entered. Bar & Bench (posts at about 7:08 PM, 7:38 PM and 7:55 PM): he and other INDIA bloc leaders entered from Gate B. Delhi Police increased security and attempted to stop leaders. The registry was shut at first. Later scenes inside the registry showed a crowd of lawyers and leaders, including Akhilesh Yadav and Supriya Sule, jostling toward filing of the petition on alleged voter deletions. LiveLaw (about 7:24 PM) showed senior leaders entering Gate B and noted the writ had already been filed. India Today's video headline: Rahul Gandhi enters the Supreme Court with top Congress leaders after the Delhi protests. This physical entry is later than the 4:37 PM filing and the stop at Bhagwan Dass Road.

India Today (published 8:04 PM, updated 8:29 PM), Bar & Bench (about 8:20 PM) and NDTV published the petition's ten prayers. In paraphrase of that prayer block: (1) the Election Commission to produce the complete files, agendas, minutes, notings and objections of the Election Commissioners on disputed SIR decisions, plus ECINET and ERONET access logs and the complete file for the 24 June 2025 decision to begin nationwide SIR; (2) examine whether those decisions complied with Article 324, Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023, and T.N. Seshan v. Union of India, and quash and set aside any decision taken without lawful authority; (3) action against persons responsible for breaches, including under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, where warranted; (4) pending adjudication, every SIR-related Commission decision to be taken and minuted under Section 18; (5) online Form 6 to conform to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, unless those Rules are lawfully amended; (6) an independent committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge, with technical experts, to audit SIR deletions and database access, including ECINET and ERONET, and to review EVM policies, procedures and technical design against global best practices; (7) booth-wise publication of deleted electors with reasons and a gender and age breakdown, and a working way to restore eligible names; (8) no deletion without notice and a hearing, and eligible persons in Punjab and other poll-bound States allowed to seek inclusion until the last date the law allows; (9) an interim direction suspending the ongoing SIR across States pending adjudication; (10) other orders the court finds fit. The published prayer block does not ask for the Chief Election Commissioner's removal. India Today's introduction describes the plea as challenging the validity of SIR. The petition text in the same story says it does not seek to reopen the validity of SIR after the court's 27 May 2026 judgment in ADR v ECI. It challenges implementation and whether the Commission acted as a collective institution. The petition cites an Indian Express report of 23 September 2026 that the two Election Commissioners had recorded objections. It notes that the Commission says differences are normal and that decisions were unanimous. Both accounts are kept.

image.alt: Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra at the front of a street march, with police alongside and other marchers behind them.

timeline.e: Rahul Gandhi, answering a question on CJP (Indian Express, about 8:21 PM): "All protests are one, to remove Gyanesh Kumar." His words. That is his comment on the protests. It is not one of the ten prayers in the petition.

The Hindu (updated 8:52 PM) and Supreme Court Observer: the petition is on the Supreme Court website as filed at 4:37 p.m., Diary No. 64196/2026, through Advocate Prasanna S. (the same counsel earlier reports call Advocate S. Prasanna). Petitioners: Rahul Gandhi; Mallikarjun Kharge; Saugata Roy (TMC); Akhilesh Yadav (SP); Tejashwi Prasad Yadav (RJD); Supriya Sule (NCP-SP); Sanjay Raut (Shiv Sena UBT); D. Raja (CPI); Mahua Majhi (JMM); M.A. Baby (CPI-M); E.T. Mohammed Basheer (IUML). The Hindu's list matches Supreme Court Observer. Respondents: the Election Commission of India; Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar; Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. The 5:07 PM report had named Kharge, Saugata Roy, Akhilesh Yadav and Tejashwi Yadav as co-filers. Mahua Majhi is additional in this list. Supriya Sule, Sanjay Raut, D. Raja, M.A. Baby and Basheer are named here as co-petitioners, not only as people on the march. NDTV's list of the ten leaders besides Gandhi is the same set.

image.alt: A crowd of men in white clothes gathered at a gate.

timeline.e: Evening reactions, their words. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi (PTI video, about 9:20 PM), as captioned by PTI: "Cong protest against EC, SIR conspiracy funded by foreign organisations." His allegation. Himanta Biswa Sarma (ANI, about 8:39 PM): "Ask your Govts to resign first," a challenge to Rahul Gandhi over the Chief Election Commissioner and the electoral roll. Jyotiraditya Scindia (ANI, about 9:12 PM): "Decisions are made in court of people, not on streets," hitting the Opposition protest. DK Shivakumar (ANI, about 9:01 PM): "Everyone wants SIR scrapped," backing the INDIA bloc petition. Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy (ANI, about 9:16 PM) alleged that the Modi government "conspired to delete voters' names" under SIR "in collusion with" Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. His allegation.

As of 9:35 PM. After the 4:37 PM filing, Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders later entered the Supreme Court, with Gate B and registry scenes between about 6:30 PM and 7:55 PM. Diary No. 64196/2026. The fuller co-petitioner and respondent lists are published. Ten prayers are detailed, including an interim suspension of the ongoing SIR and a retired-judge audit. The published prayers do not ask for the Chief Election Commissioner's removal. NDTV reports registry processing aimed at a Tuesday listing. That is not confirmed on a cause list. Evening BJP and NDA quotes, and INDIA bloc quotes, are above. Dhruv Rathee's morning claim of "unofficial house arrest" is his claim. No police confirmation was found. CJP's 24-hour ultimatum for a Jantar Mantar date, given around 11:50 AM, still has no reported police grant. The window runs toward late Tuesday morning. Tuesday 13 Oct stays as already listed: the Supreme Court hears the Bar Association plea and related lawyer and internet pleas, and the Delhi High Court hears the Youth Congress plea, the Jantar Mantar closure plea, the outsiders-harassment plea and the NSUI special-investigation plea. A listing of the Gandhi petition that day is only the media expectation above, if defects are cleared. The Bar Association has also called one minute of silence at 1:15 PM before the Gandhi statue.

Bar & Bench (9:57 PM): the Network of Women in Media, India has moved the Supreme Court over the alleged detention, dragging and manhandling of journalists, including women reporters, who were covering the anti-CEC protests. The petitioners say the police action continued despite the court's direction that journalists not be hindered, and they seek binding safeguards and an independent inquiry. That is their allegation. No police response was found. No hearing date was reported.

The Supreme Court registry flagged 14 defects on 12 Oct in the INDIA bloc petition, Diary No. 64196/2026 (IANS, about 11:04 PM; News18 and India TV, 11:07 PM; India TV updated 11:47 PM). Named defects, as IANS, India TV and DNA report them: private individuals named as respondents without explanation, and discrepancies in respondent names; no copy of an earlier judgment annexed; vakalatnamas missing for nine petitioners, everyone except Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge; an illegible copy of Kharge's identity card; a Rs 220 shortfall in the court fee; and small type, legibility and printing problems. DNA adds that the registry asked for clear copies of the Election Commission's 24 June 2025 Special Intensive Revision decision and related records, plus digital copies on a pen drive. Under the Supreme Court Rules 2013 the defects must be cured before the matter can be listed. India TV says curing them all on Monday is likely to be difficult. This sits beside NDTV's earlier report that the registry was processing the petition for a likely Tuesday hearing. That remains NDTV's report, not a cause-list confirmation. PTI (7:50 AM, 13 Oct) describes the registry note as more than 10 defects. IANS, News18 and India TV said 14. Both counts are kept.

image.alt: Rahul Gandhi speaking into a microphone at a podium.

timeline.e: PTI video (11:25 PM): Khan Market Traders Association president Sanjiv Mehra said "CJP indulging in vandalism and spreading anarchy", that road closures had caused "huge business losses", and that the association will move the Supreme Court "seeking a ban on protests here." His claims. Update, ANI (8:04 AM, 13 Oct): the association's president, whom ANI spells Sanjeev Mehra, said business has been hit and that the police perimeter starts 1 km out. The 11:25 PM PTI video spelled the name Sanjiv Mehra. Both spellings are kept. His claims.

Bar & Bench (11:43 PM): "Rahul Gandhi's petition does not figure in the Supreme Court's supplementary cause list for October 13, released late tonight (11:25 pm)." Listed before Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana are CPI(M)'s M.A. Baby PIL, with a tagged contempt plea by Shailendra Mani Tripathi against Govind Mohan and Apoorvanand's plea; Menaka Guruswamy; RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha; the Association for Democratic Reforms; the Supreme Court Bar Association; SCAORA; the Youth Bar Association of India; and pleas by Priya Mishra, Samriddhi Das, who has sought an ex-parte stay, Bhanu Sanoriya, Mukesh Kumar Pandey, Aman Prasad and Anand Kumar Pandey. The Gandhi petition could still be mentioned, or listed later, if the registry defects are cured. No report of that yet. NDTV's earlier report of a likely Tuesday hearing stays NDTV's report. Update, 13 Oct morning: LiveLaw (8:01 AM and 9:05 AM) says this bench will hear today the petitions on police and paramilitary action against the Delhi protesters. Its list matches the matters already named here. No outcome yet. The Gandhi petition is still not on the list.

The account @CJP_for_India, which is not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, posted at 11:47 PM that people are seeking money in CJP's name and claiming to provide legal help to detainees, that those people are not affiliated with CJP, and that no one should pay them, and should verify through official channels. Treat this post as unverified. It is not from the official CJP account.

PTI (12:41 AM), citing sources: Rahul Gandhi will host a high tea for INDIA bloc MPs at his residence on Tuesday. The discussion is expected to cover strategy for joint protests against what they call "vote chori" and for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. ANI had reported the plan at 10:37 PM on Monday. PTI attributes the detail to sources. Update, PTI (8:26 AM), citing sources: INDIA bloc leaders will hold a joint press conference. Rahul Gandhi's invitation now also covers members of civil society and student organisations, not only INDIA bloc MPs. A PTI video at 8:37 AM shows the outside of his residence. ETV Bharat (about 1:44 PM, 13 Oct), quoting Rahul Gandhi: he invited INDIA alliance leaders, opposition MPs, student organisations and civil society to his home for tea, and said that after tea they will put their case to the media, and that "All protests are one." The tea and joint appearance were set for about 4 PM at 5 Sunehri Bagh Road. As of 3:11 PM they had not been reported as held. Update: the tea was held. India Today (about 5:16 PM) reported leaders, students and civil society at 5 Sunehri Bagh Road, and named among those present Tejashwi Yadav, Manoj Jha, Mahua Maji, Harender Malik, Anand Bhadauria, Mohibullah Nadvi, M.A. Baby, D. Raja, P. Sandosh Kumar, Neha Bora, Dipankar Bhattacharya, Mahua Moitra, Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, K.C. Venugopal, Jairam Ramesh, Shashi Tharoor and Pawan Khera. The Hindu reported arrivals including Shashi Tharoor (about 4:42 PM) and D.K. Shiva Kumar, described in that update as Karnataka Chief Minister (about 5:37 PM). India TV reported Sonia Gandhi and Kharge arriving at about 4:38–4:39 PM, and a press conference afterwards. India TV (about 3:51 PM) quoted Congress MP Manickam Tagore, before the meeting, saying they would sit together and decide. As of 6:10 PM the tea and the press conference had been reported as held.

BJP leaders allege that Rahul Gandhi pushed a woman journalist near the Supreme Court on Monday evening. The clips they cite are from about 9 PM. Pradeep Bhandari (ANI, 2:41 AM; IANS, 3:05 AM) alleges Gandhi "grabbed a female journalist, hit her with the elbow and made her fall" and says she is hospitalised. Rajesh Bhatia (ANI, 2:43 AM) says her sister told him the journalist, who is pregnant, was pushed by Gandhi and admitted for observation. Umang Bajaj (ANI, 2:47 AM) names her as Richa Parashar. Those are their allegations. Gandhi supporters on X argue the clip shows her own camera person, not Gandhi, pushing her. No official Congress response was found. No police complaint or FIR was reported.

As of 6:10 AM Tuesday. The Supreme Court registry flagged 14 defects in the INDIA bloc petition, including a Rs 220 fee shortfall and nine missing vakalatnamas, and Bar & Bench reports it is not on the 13 Oct supplementary cause list released at 11:25 PM. NDTV's earlier "likely Tuesday" report stays NDTV's report. The Chief Justice-led bench is listed to hear the M.A. Baby PIL, the Tripathi contempt plea and other related pleas today. The Network of Women in Media, India has filed a Supreme Court plea over alleged manhandling of journalists. That is the petitioners' allegation. BJP leaders allege Gandhi pushed a woman journalist. That is disputed, and no Congress response was found. Gandhi hosts INDIA bloc MPs this evening, according to PTI, citing sources. CJP's ultimatum for a Jantar Mantar date is still unanswered. The 24 hours from about 11:50 AM on Monday run out late this morning. Today: the Supreme Court hearings already on the list, the Delhi High Court pleas already listed, and the Bar Association's one minute of silence at 1:15 PM. No new detention or release of a named key person was found overnight.

Indian Express, from a Jaipur press meet on Monday: CJP national spokesperson Deepak Baliyan said, "We want to warn the government that you can't stop us from going to Delhi and if you try, we will make a Jantar Mantar in every city." He said CJP will protest in Rajasthan in the next few days. The date and venue are not announced. He says police told him there were "instructions from above" to stop him going to Delhi. Activists Geegraj Jodli and Shashikant also described detentions by Rajasthan Police. Those are their claims. Sri Ganganagar police had said workers were only counselled, not detained.

image.alt: Deepak Baliyan speaking into a microphone at a press meet.

timeline.e: LiveLaw (published 7:40 AM) and Bar & Bench (9:04 AM): the Lawyers' Association for Constitution and advocates Fidel Tom, Sumita Hazarika, Anna Oommen and Anne Mathew have moved the Supreme Court over alleged police excesses. The association's convenor is Senior Advocate Anjana Prakash. The petition is filed through advocate-on-record Pyoli. LiveLaw spells the name Fidel Tom. This page's earlier card uses Fidal Tom. They allege they were manhandled and illegally detained by Delhi Police on 10 and 11 Oct, and that Tom was assaulted at Sanjay Colony police station and denied timely legal and medical help. They seek a court-monitored inquiry, which Bar & Bench says would be headed by a retired judge, along with preservation of CCTV, detention records, police name tags, compensation, and binding rules for policing peaceful assemblies. Those are the petitioners' allegations. No police response was found.

image.alt: Police officers facing a crowd of protesters on a city street.

timeline.e: Hindustan Times (published 7:41 AM): Delhi Police constable Amit Yadav, 33, of Kalyan Puri police station, was killed in a road accident. He had been deployed at Jantar Mantar for security around the CJP protest and was riding home when a truck coming from the wrong direction hit his motorcycle in Farrukhnagar, Gurugram, at about 9:30 AM on Monday. Gurugram Police registered an FIR against the truck driver, who fled. This is a traffic death. It is not reported as protest violence.

On 12 Oct, asked about the anti-CEC protests and the restrictions in Delhi at a National Human Rights Commission anniversary event at Vigyan Bhawan, Chief Justice Surya Kant said: "Ye law and order ka mudda hai. Ye mera vishay nahin hai" ("This is a matter of law and order; it doesn't pertain to my domain"). News18 and The Telegraph, via PTI, carry that remark. The official Congress Keralam account then posted: "Dear Surya Kant, if law and order is not your domain, resign now. We will find your replacement who can handle it." The post was deleted. KPCC president Sunny Joseph said the person responsible was removed, that the post was made without the leadership's knowledge or consent, and that Congress has no disagreement with the judiciary's impartiality. Union minister Kiren Rijiju shared a screenshot and accused Congress of targeting constitutional institutions. BJP spokesperson C.R. Kesavan (PTI video, 7:21 AM, 13 Oct) called it "uncouth language... to openly threaten and abuse the high office of Chief Justice of India." Their words. NDTV (8:12 AM) reported that a Keralam minister questioned the Chief Justice and asked Gyanesh Kumar to examine his own duties. The minister is not named in that post.

LiveLaw (8:36 AM): Moliticis India journalist Amaan Rastogi has filed a contempt petition in the Supreme Court. He alleges Delhi Police detained him repeatedly on 10 and 11 Oct despite the court's order that journalists not be hindered, and alleges he was manhandled, his phone was damaged and his press identity card was destroyed. Those are his allegations. No police response was found.

IANS (8:57 AM), quoting Delhi Police sources: "Police registered multiple FIRs in connection with yesterday's protest march to the Supreme Court by Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders." No details yet on who is named or under which sections. No official statement was found. This is attributed to police sources. Update: The Hindu and PTI (about 9:46–11:32 AM) report two FIRs, at Barakhamba Road and Tilak Marg police stations. ANI and ABP Live (about 10:42 AM) also report FIRs at Connaught Place and Mandir Marg for alleged violation of BNSS Section 163. Both accounts are kept.

Other responses, their words. NDMC vice-chairman Kuljeet Singh Chahal (PTI, 8:51 AM; IANS, 9:03 AM), at a cleanliness drive near Mandi House: "The Aam Aadmi Party, Rahul Gandhi and the CJP have made it a daily agenda to harass New Delhi and its people. This is not a case of vote theft." Telangana BJP president Ramchandra Rao (IANS, 9:02 AM) said Rahul Gandhi "is dragging the Supreme Court and the judiciary into a political controversy." BJP MP Jagdambika Pal (IANS, 9:07 AM) said the INDIA bloc has every right to petition, and asked whether any Leader of the Opposition has ever marched against the judiciary.

As of 9:15 AM Tuesday. The Supreme Court is set to hear today the petitions on police action against protesters, before the Chief Justice-led bench. No outcome yet. New pleas: the Lawyers' Association for Constitution seeks a court-monitored inquiry into alleged police excesses on 10 and 11 Oct, and journalist Amaan Rastogi has filed a contempt plea. Those are the petitioners' allegations. Delhi Police sources say multiple FIRs were registered over Monday's INDIA bloc march. No names or sections were given. The INDIA bloc plans a joint press conference, and Gandhi's tea now includes civil society and student groups. PTI cites sources. CJP says it will protest in Rajasthan in the next few days. The date and venue are not announced. The registry defects remain as reported: 14 in the IANS, News18 and India TV accounts, and more than 10 in PTI's. The Gandhi petition is still not on the supplementary cause list. NDTV's likely-Tuesday report stays NDTV's report. The ultimatum for a Jantar Mantar date is still unanswered. PTI and IANS visuals around 7:44 AM showed heavy security on Jantar Mantar Road. The official CJP account posted at 8:34 AM that leaders had visited Parliament Street police station to demand a date and that the government then de-notified the site. That is their framing of the de-notification already recorded. No new detention or release of a named key person was reported this morning.

PTI, via The Hindu (about 9:11 AM): Delhi Police have asked the Home Ministry to extend the deployment of 273 companies of central armed police in Delhi until 20 Oct, citing possible protests by CJP and others. The deployment had been due to end on Monday. Sources said 301 companies had been approved, 221 on 6 Oct and 80 on 8 Oct, and that 28 of the extra 80 had not reported as of Monday. Police flagged possible demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, the Election Commission, Parliament House and India Gate. That is the police request.

Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut (ANI, via The Hindu, about 10:39 AM), on the defects in Rahul Gandhi's Supreme Court petition: "There might be errors, but we will correct them…" He again called for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation and raised the Special Intensive Revision. His words.

The Hindu (Soibam Rocky Singh, about 11:10 AM): the Delhi High Court is to hear petitions seeking standard procedures for protests so that businesses and lawyers are not disrupted. Senior Advocate Sachin Puri said recent protests caused traders losses of more than Rs 2,000 crore. That is his claim. The matter was to be heard at the end of the board. The court was awaiting Supreme Court directions on related issues. No order was reported as of 12:15 PM.

Delhi Police detained CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde at Jantar Mantar on Tuesday morning, a day after the site was de-notified as a protest venue (The Hindu, the Economic Times and Times of India; reports from about 9:48 AM). No release was reported as of 12:15 PM. Abhijeet Dipke posted that "Cockroaches with the Tiranga sneaked into Jantar Mantar early this morning" before police picked them up, and wrote to the Prime Minister: "You cannot denotify the resistance." His claim. The Hindu credits a still from his video to X/@abhijeet_dipke via PTI. From a detention bus, Das said: "Jantar Mantar has been breached. We were inside and now they are detaining us and taking us away." Ranka said: "Today 5 people entered… tomorrow 50,000 would enter until Gyanesh Kumar resigns. Protest will take place at Jantar Mantar only." Their words. A senior Delhi Police officer told The Hindu (about 10:08 AM) that the protesters entered through eateries and food stalls, that a demonstration at the de-notified site is illegal, and that they were detained immediately, with further action underway. That is the police account. The Hindu (about 11:13 AM): Das said they had been taken to Jaffarpur police station.

image.alt: Three men seated in a police vehicle, one holding up a phone.

timeline.e: Station detail on Monday's INDIA bloc march, beyond the earlier "multiple FIRs" line. The Hindu and PTI (about 9:46–11:32 AM) and India Today (about 9:33 AM) report two FIRs, at Barakhamba Road and Tilak Marg, over the march to the Supreme Court without permission. Police accounts in those reports allege a barricade was breached with the help of a mini-truck. Moneycontrol, citing police, also mentions graffiti. India Today says the accused column in the initial complaints was blank and that police are examining CCTV and video. ANI and ABP Live (about 10:42 AM) report FIRs as well at Connaught Place and Mandir Marg for alleged violation of BNSS Section 163. The two-station account and the wider station list are both kept. No official statement naming the accused was found.

The Supreme Court did not complete a hearing on the merits of the Delhi-protest pleas this morning, and it did not dispose of them. Indian Express (about 10:56–10:59 AM): senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan mentioned a journalist's contempt plea. These reports tie that mention to Amaan Rastogi and the 11 Oct order. Chief Justice Surya Kant, sitting with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana, said matters can be listed once defects are cured, and "We will take up the matter tomorrow." PTI and The Hindu (about 11:51 AM) and New Indian Express: he assured petitioners that all pleas related to the Delhi protests will be listed, and that they may be listed on Wednesday or Thursday. He said, "Make sure that the defects are cured." Indian Express (about 12:04–12:05 PM): the hearing was adjourned. The Chief Justice said Justice V. Mohana is unwell. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said the affidavit and compliance report on the contempt notice are ready and that he wants to make them more comprehensive. The court extended the time to file that reply. The Chief Justice said listing will happen and that he would like some senior officer to remain present. Senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia, also a BJP leader, mentioned the previous day's scene of opposition leaders at the court. The court asked him to mention it tomorrow. The Gandhi petition's absence from today's supplementary cause list is unchanged. NDTV's earlier likely-Tuesday report stays NDTV's report. Update, afternoon: The Hindu and PTI (about 12:48 PM) say the protest-related hearing was deferred to Thursday 15 Oct because Justice V. Mohana was indisposed. The Hindu (about 1:36 PM) says the Centre's reply, described as ready but still to be fine-tuned, is now due Thursday. That date is for the detention and protest-curbs cluster. It is not a report that the Gandhi Special Intensive Revision petition was listed for 15 Oct.

As of 12:15 PM. Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde are detained again after trying to protest at Jantar Mantar. Das said they were at Jaffarpur police station. No release was reported. Police say they entered through eateries and that a protest at the de-notified site is illegal. CJP says they were inside. Both accounts are kept. The morning Supreme Court hearing was adjourned. Justice V. Mohana was reported unwell. The Chief Justice said the protest pleas will be listed, possibly on Wednesday or Thursday, once defects are cured, and the court extended the time to reply to the contempt notice. No merits order was reported. FIR reports now name Barakhamba Road and Tilak Marg, and ANI also names Connaught Place and Mandir Marg. Still ahead today, with no outcome yet: the INDIA bloc joint press conference and the tea at Rahul Gandhi's residence. Delhi Police have asked for central armed police to stay until 20 Oct. That request was not reported as granted.

Indian Express (about 12:36 PM): before Justice Amit Mahajan, Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma said the Indian Youth Congress plea for a Jantar Mantar protest, for president Uday Bhanu Chib, had become "infructuous" because the site was de-notified. Senior advocate Siddharth Luthra, for Chib, said the plea was not infructuous, alleged "subterfuge", and said notice must issue and that the plea would be amended. The court passed the matter over and was to take it up later on Tuesday, with Luthra to appear in person. No final order was reported as of 3:11 PM.

The hearing on the Delhi-protest pleas, covering alleged illegal detentions and the metro and train curbs, was deferred to Thursday 15 Oct 2026 because Justice V. Mohana was indisposed (The Hindu and PTI, about 12:48 PM; ETV Bharat). The Hindu (about 1:36 PM): the Centre told the Supreme Court its response is ready but needs fine-tuning. The bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant extended the filing to Thursday 15 Oct. ETV Bharat paraphrased the Chief Justice as saying democratic activities must proceed smoothly, without obstructing the court or lawyers, staff and litigants. This date is for that protest-curbs and detention cluster. It is not a report that Rahul Gandhi's Special Intensive Revision petition, which still has registry defects to cure, was listed for 15 Oct.

ETV Bharat (about 1:38 PM), citing officials: Delhi Police say four FIRs have been registered since 10 Oct over fake online posts, and that they are looking at Pakistani social media handles. That is the officials' claim. It is separate from the FIRs over Monday's march.

The Hindu (about 2:30 PM): Ramlila Maidan, one of the three sites designated after Jantar Mantar was de-notified, has no free dates for about the next two and a half months. Officials said only 29, 30 and 31 Dec 2026 are open for booking. They put capacity at about 50,000, and the charge at about Rs 50,000 a day plus a refundable deposit of about Rs 55,000, roughly Rs 1.21 lakh with taxes for a day. That is the officials' account. Protesters have said the alternative sites are impractical.

The Hindu (about 1:48–2:56 PM): the Disha Students Organisation, with speakers from Naujawan Bharat Sabha and Revolutionary Workers' Party of India, protested at Connaught Place against the de-notification of Jantar Mantar and for scrapping the Special Intensive Revision, and demanded the release of Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Naureen of Disha said, "Jantar Mantar is ours… Throwing us to far off places like Burari is not going to help." Chiranshu of Naujawan Bharat Sabha demanded the release of Das and Ranka. Their words. ETV Bharat (about 2:43 PM) also reported a Disha march from Connaught Place. The Hindu (about 2:56 PM): NSUI workers who staged a flash protest at Connaught Place metro station were all detained. ETV Bharat also reported an AISA protest at Gandhi Maidan in Patna (about 2:26 PM) and a Trinamool Congress protest in Kolkata demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation (about 2:50 PM).

image.alt: Young protesters with placards gathered on a city pavement beside a bus.

timeline.e: ETV Bharat (about 3:01 PM): journalist Parashar alleged that Rahul Gandhi and his security manhandled and shoved her during the chaotic exit from the Supreme Court protest, and that she is pregnant. That is her allegation. It sits beside the earlier BJP account, from about 2:41–3:05 AM, that Gandhi pushed a woman journalist, which supporters disputed. Neither account is treated here as established. No police complaint was reported in the morning check.

CJP alleges that detained leaders were denied their lawyer and that their phones were taken. No release of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka or Ajinkya Shinde was reported as of 3:11 PM. Ratna Singh wrote at about 12:39 PM, and The Hindu carried it at about 2:20 PM, that the SHO of Jaffarpur Kalan police station refused to let the lawyer meet them and that their phones were confiscated. Her claim. Hindustan Times (updated about 2:52 PM): Pushp Sharma told PTI he has not been allowed to meet Das, Ranka and 12 others detained with them. He said Das's last WhatsApp message was that phones were being taken, and that the SHO told him the phones are "kept safe" and that Sharma can call if needed. That is Sharma's account of what the SHO said. Police were not quoted responding to these claims. Abhijeet Dipke (ETV Bharat, about 3:08 PM) claimed the three leaders were held at separate locations, that 11 volunteers were taken elsewhere, and that lawyers were barred and threatened with further detention. He asked, "How can you arrest someone for hoisting the tricolour?" His claim.

As of 3:11 PM. Das, Ranka and Shinde were still detained. CJP's account places them at Jaffarpur Kalan. Dipke says the leaders were split and volunteers were taken elsewhere. His claim. The legal team alleges a lawyer was denied and phones were taken. No police rebuttal was found in the reports used here. The Supreme Court protest-related cluster was deferred to Thursday 15 Oct. The Centre's reply, which it called ready but still to be fine-tuned, is due Thursday. Ramlila Maidan is booked through December except 29, 30 and 31 Dec, officials told The Hindu. Disha protested at Connaught Place. NSUI's flash protest at the Connaught Place metro station ended in detention, The Hindu reported. The Youth Congress plea in the Delhi High Court was passed over after the Centre called it infructuous. No final order yet. The INDIA bloc tea and press conference at 5 Sunehri Bagh Road were still ahead, around 4 PM. Kiran Bedi, on ETV Bharat, said Jantar Mantar is the least suitable protest site because of narrow lanes and nearby sensitive buildings, that every city needs an open ground, and that Ramlila Maidan needs a clear security and functioning plan. Her words. John Brittas, on the petition defects, said small defects are normal, the registry has a way to correct them, and the focus should be the content. His words. No confirmed release of the three CJP leaders.

The Hindu (about 4:27 PM) headlined that Delhi Police blocked the All India Students' Federation and the All India Youth Federation from protesting. The live post quotes AISF: "We will continue our democratic struggle demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Detentions, police barricades and repression will not silence students or stop us from exercising our democratic rights." That is AISF's post. A separate police statement spelling out an allegation against the groups was not in the text of that update.

The Hindu and PTI (about 4:31 PM): Abhijeet Dipke, speaking in Santuk Pimpri in Maharashtra's Hingoli district during the asthi visarjan of his grandmother, Savitribai Dipke, warned that if demonstrations are banned at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, protest sites would emerge across the country. He said that if police stop him on the way to Delhi he would start the agitation from wherever he is detained, and that he would reach the capital on Wednesday for the protest demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. His words. He was not reported detained.

Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde were still detained as of about 5:52 PM. No release was reported. The Hindu (about 4:48 PM): CJP accused Delhi Police of illegal detention and of denying lawyers access, and called for the release of Das, Ranka, Ajinkya and other members. That is CJP's accusation. Times of India, citing ANI: Abhijeet Dipke wrote that police were "not allowing the lawyers to meet them" and asked, "How can police stop lawyers from meeting them? This is kidnapping because the police are certainly not following the rule of law." He said Ratna Singh had just told him the three were kept separately, that 11 volunteers were taken elsewhere, and that police did not let lawyers enter and threatened others with detention. That is his account of what she told him. Police were not quoted in reply. This follows the afternoon claims that a lawyer was refused and phones were taken. It does not independently confirm those claims.

LiveLaw (6:08 PM): Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice on three prayers in the Indian Youth Congress plea, (c), (d) and (f), and listed the matter for 17 Nov. Prayer (c) seeks a declaration that the 2022 standing order cannot automatically prohibit a peaceful assembly. Prayer (d) seeks a fresh, reasoned reconsideration of the protest request. Prayer (f) seeks a declaration that the 10-day notice rule is not an absolute bar. Senior advocate Siddharth Luthra, for president Uday Bhanu Chib, said he would amend the prayers after Monday's de-notification and called conditions in the 2022 order "Completely non speaking" and "bad in law." Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma opposed notice. He said the petition is about holding a demonstration at Jantar Mantar, that the site was de-notified pursuant to Supreme Court orders, and that the petition cannot stand unless the de-notification is challenged. Notice on those three prayers is not an order granting permission to protest, and it is not a ruling on the de-notification itself.

After the high tea at 5 Sunehri Bagh Road, INDIA bloc leaders addressed the media (India TV, about 5:48–6:08 PM; The Hindu, about 5:40 PM and a 5:53 PM caption). Rahul Gandhi said, "We will not stop," and that removing Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site would be challenged: "The one method of expression of democracy was Jantar Mantar and now the government has decided that Jantar Mantar can no longer be used to express democratic feelings. We are going to challenge that idea." He named Narendra Modi as "the main architect," Amit Shah as "the implementer," and Gyanesh Kumar "and others," and said there is "one singular protest" to restore democracy. His words. Mallikarjun Kharge called the recent protests a tremendous success and said everyone was prepared to "fully expose PM Modi's plan to steal votes." His words. D. Raja condemned the de-notification and said they would fight to regain Jantar Mantar. Sanjay Raut called Gyanesh Kumar a "mafia." Supriya Sule said the Constitution had been undermined. Those are their words, as India TV reported them. India TV's quote of Tejashwi Yadav renders the Chief Election Commissioner's name as "Gyanesh Kumar Gupta" and "Gyanesh Gupta"; other reports in this file name him Gyanesh Kumar. India Today (about 5:16 PM) had reported the tea as held. The Hindu's photograph caption names Rahul Gandhi, Kharge, Tejashwi Yadav and D. Raja at the microphones, and credits the picture to X/@RahulGandhi.

image.alt: Opposition leaders seated at a table during a press conference, with microphones in front of them.

timeline.e: As of 6:10 PM. Das, Ranka and Shinde were still detained. CJP calls the detention illegal and says lawyers were denied. Dipke, citing Ratna Singh, says the three were split and calls the lawyer bar kidnapping. No police rebuttal was in the reports used here. Dipke was in Hingoli and said he would reach Delhi on Wednesday. The INDIA bloc tea and press conference at 5 Sunehri Bagh Road were held. Rahul Gandhi said the removal of Jantar Mantar would be challenged and that the protest would not stop. The Delhi High Court issued notice on three Youth Congress prayers and listed 17 Nov. The government said the plea cannot stand unless the de-notification is challenged. The Hindu headlined that police blocked AISF and AIYF. The Supreme Court protest cluster is still down for Thursday 15 Oct, not as a listing of the Gandhi Special Intensive Revision petition.

joined.name: Ajinkya Shinde
joined.role: CJP organisation in-charge; now leading the protest while the top leaders are held On the morning of 13 Oct he was detained at Jantar Mantar with Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka. Das said they were taken to Jaffarpur police station. No release was reported as of 12:15 PM. Police say they entered through eateries at a de-notified site. CJP says they were inside protesting. As of 3:11 PM he was still detained. Ratna Singh alleges a lawyer was refused and phones were taken. That is CJP's claim. No police reply was quoted. No release was reported. As of 6:10 PM he was still detained, on Dipke's account to ANI (Times of India, about 5:52 PM) and on CJP's call for release (The Hindu, about 4:48 PM). No release was reported.

joined.name: Dhruv Rathee
joined.role: YouTuber; called people to Jantar Mantar and joined the 8 Oct Bengaluru protest On 12 Oct he told The Lallantop, reported by India Today (updated 12:16 PM), that about 50 police were outside his residence and that he was "unofficially" under house arrest. His claim. No police confirmation was found as of 9:35 PM.

joined.name: Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Mallikarjun Kharge, KC Venugopal
joined.role: Congress / INDIA bloc street protests, 6–9 Oct. 4:57 PM video: 'Keep protesting. We are proud of you' (The Hindu). NDTV (7:41 PM), quoting his X post: 'Arrest all the leaders... Arrest us all... Youth of India, I am proud of you. Keep protesting.' INDIA bloc leaders will meet CJI Surya Kant on Monday to submit a memorandum. Indian Express (9:41 PM): Monday's march starts at 1:30 PM from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba junction. Kharge says he and Rahul were given 4 PM to 5 PM on Monday to meet Chief Justice Surya Kant (PTI via ThePrint). That slot is Kharge's account. PTI (9:47 PM): he and Kharge have written to the Chief Justice seeking a 4–5 PM meeting on Monday. Demands they describe include a return to paper ballots. News9 (11:09 PM), citing people aware of the matter, says Chief Justice Surya Kant declined that 4–5 PM slot. K.C. Venugopal says the march is still on (ANI, via webindia123). On 12 Oct he left his residence around 11:49 AM for a press conference at Indira Bhawan (ANI; IANS, 12:03 PM). The press conference was not yet reported. The march is still set for 1:30 PM. At the Indira Bhawan press conference (about 12:17–1:30 PM) he said the bloc will file a Supreme Court petition rather than submit a memorandum. As of 3:06 PM the filing was not confirmed. The march toward the court was underway. Update, evening of 12 Oct: his lawyer, Advocate S. Prasanna, filed the Supreme Court petition on his behalf after he could not reach the court by the 4:30 PM filing cut-off (Economic Times, updated 4:56 PM; The Hindu, about 5:07 PM). India Today says the petition is registered on the Supreme Court website. No hearing date was confirmed. Police stopped the march at Bhagwan Dass Road. Evening of 12 Oct: after that filing he and other INDIA bloc leaders entered the Supreme Court from Gate B (Supreme Court Observer, 6:30 PM; Bar & Bench, about 7:08–7:55 PM). Diary No. 64196/2026. The Hindu (updated 8:52 PM) published the full co-petitioner and respondent lists. India Today (updated 8:29 PM) published ten prayers. They do not include removal of the Chief Election Commissioner. NDTV (updated 6:06 PM) reports registry processing aimed at a Tuesday hearing. That is not a cause-list confirmation. On a CJP question (Indian Express, about 8:21 PM) he said: "All protests are one, to remove Gyanesh Kumar." His words. Update, overnight: IANS, News18, India TV and DNA report 14 registry defects in Diary No. 64196/2026, including a Rs 220 fee shortfall and missing vakalatnamas for nine petitioners. Bar & Bench (11:43 PM) says the petition is not on the 13 Oct supplementary cause list. NDTV's likely-Tuesday report stays NDTV's report. PTI (12:41 AM, citing sources) says he will host a high tea for INDIA bloc MPs at his residence on Tuesday. BJP leaders allege he pushed a woman journalist on Monday evening. Supporters dispute that. No Congress response was found. PTI (8:26 AM, 13 Oct), citing sources, says INDIA bloc leaders will hold a joint press conference and that the tea at his residence now also includes civil society and student groups.
