joined.name: V.D. Satheesan (Kerala CM, Congress)
joined.role: Condemned Pinarayi Vijayan's detention and said state officials are coordinating his release. Via UNI (~5:27 PM) he said Vijayan is held at Mandir Marg police station. Indian Express (5:55 AM, 12 Oct): the Assembly bulletin lists him to move a resolution on Monday urging the Union government to remove Gyanesh Kumar as Chief Election Commissioner. Indian Express says Kerala will be the first Assembly to seek the CEC's removal. Times of India, the Economic Times and Indian Express (12 Oct): he is to move the resolution under Rule 118 on the opening day of the Assembly's second session. Besides the Chief Election Commissioner's removal it seeks reinstatement of eligible voters struck off during the Special Intensive Revision and changes to the selection panel for Election Commissioners. The Economic Times says the LDF will back it and that a state resolution is not binding. It was not reported as passed as of 12:10 PM. The Hindu (updated 2:14 PM), Hindustan Times and ThePrint: the Assembly passed the resolution around 12:52–1:29 PM. UDF and LDF supported it. The BJP objected and its amendments were rejected. He accepted Pinarayi Vijayan's amendment changing "lakhs" of excluded voters to "crores". PTI (about 2:49 PM): he denied political vendetta in a Vigilance probe linked to a road project involving Gyanesh Kumar when Kumar was Kerala PWD secretary, saying "It is not political. There is no political vendetta." His words. The resolution is not binding.

allegations.by: Menaka Guruswamy, to Bar & Bench (7:53 PM)

allegations.claim: Delhi Police behaviour was 'unbecoming of a police force'. On X, via NDTV, he said police drove elected representatives 'around in circles for an hour just to keep them quiet'.
allegations.by: Pinarayi Vijayan (PTI video after release, ~7:10 PM; NDTV)

allegations.claim: The metro and train closures violate the Supreme Court's 9 Oct order.
allegations.by: Advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi (contempt plea, listed for 11 Oct)

allegations.claim: Concerned by reports of mass detentions of demonstrators, protest leaders, members of civil society organisations, lawyers and journalists, and called for the right to peaceful assembly to be fully respected.
allegations.by: UN Human Rights (via The Hindu, 8:41 PM)

allegations.claim: 'Illegal detention' of several advocates and 'disproportionate' force against lawyers, including senior advocates. Calls for an impartial inquiry and accountability.
allegations.by: Delhi High Court Bar Association (Bar & Bench, LiveLaw, 8:11–8:24 PM)

allegations.claim: Police did not let Dipke speak to his lawyer or family after news of his grandmother's death, and 'stopped everything within their control except air and water'.
allegations.by: Ajinkya Shinde (CJP), at the joint press conference (~8:55–9:04 PM)

allegations.claim: 'I am still detained. Since 9AM. There are 30 police official for one woman.' On the court order: 'Judge Serving Master.'
allegations.by: Ratna Singh (her 7:13 PM post, via The Hindu; The Wire, 8:54 PM)

allegations.claim: Delhi Police 'beat a student activist black and blue' (AISA activist Saurabh) and deny he is detained, and snatched the phones of everyone detained at Sanjay Colony / Maidangarhi police station. Unverified claim.
allegations.by: Neha Bora (AISA), own post (9:55 PM)

allegations.claim: Preventive detention of potential demonstrators is 'extremely unlawful', and law enforcement was selective.
allegations.by: Raviesha Pradeep, CJP national spokesperson (India Today, 9:30 PM)

allegations.claim: 'Upar se' orders to detain everyone in Delhi.
allegations.by: Ratna Singh, own post (9:10 PM)

allegations.claim: 'Everyone is being forcibly detained... black emergency.'
allegations.by: Gopal Rai (AAP), PTI video (9:12 PM)

allegations.claim: Supreme Court advocate Fidal Tom was assaulted by police and is illegally detained at Sanjay Colony police station. The association seeks his release and medical treatment.
allegations.by: Lawyers' Association for Constitution (via LiveLaw and Bar & Bench)

allegations.claim: Four colleagues at Sanjay Colony police post were "brutally beaten", including an 18-year-old and a lawyer, and lawyers were not allowed to meet them.
allegations.by: Yogendra Yadav (his own posts)

allegations.claim: The Section 163 BNSS order for Parliament Street cannot justify detentions at the airport and in Gurugram. The petition, filed by Gaurav Bharti on his own and not by CJP, sought production and release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, disclosure of whereabouts and legal grounds, and preservation of CCTV footage, police diaries and movement registers. It said it does not seek immunity from lawful action for any separate offence. LawBeat says the plea also names Dhruv Rathee; Bar & Bench's report does not (single source). CJP says it did not file or approve the plea. Bharti has sought to withdraw it.
allegations.by: Gaurav Bharti, in his individual capacity, in a Supreme Court habeas corpus plea he has sought to withdraw (Bar & Bench, LiveLaw, LawBeat). CJP says it did not file or approve the plea.

allegations.claim: Advocate Fidal Tom was taken to a washroom at Sanjay Colony police post and beaten by several police personnel, including a plain-clothes man. AISA activist Abhigyan said Tom and students Saurabh, Nikhil and Harsh were all beaten badly. A medico-legal examination was conducted before they were released shortly after midnight.
allegations.by: An account shared with The Wire and student activists; AISA activist Abhigyan, via The Wire

allegations.claim: AISA's Jamia Millia Islamia secretary Saurabh was beaten so badly at Sanjay Colony police post that he could not walk.
allegations.by: AISA, via Maktoob (12:22 AM)

allegations.claim: Journalists covering the Delhi protests were detained and harassed. The organisations demanded an apology and an inquiry.
allegations.by: Press Club of India, the Indian Women's Press Corps and two other journalists' organisations, via PTI (1:04 AM)

allegations.claim: Police used indiscriminate violence on 10 Oct: protesters near Jantar Mantar, INA and Dilli Haat were assaulted; a protester near INA was lifted, thrown down and beaten; a young advocate who intervened when police allegedly pulled at a woman's trousers was beaten and suffered head injuries; women were manhandled by male officers; Scroll's Ayush Tiwari was detained despite a press pass; officers had no name tags.
allegations.by: Advocate Aman Prasad, in a Supreme Court contempt petition against Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar (via LiveLaw and Bar & Bench)

allegations.claim: Delhi Police illegally detained, "abducted" or put under house arrest unarmed protesters, student leaders, advocates, politicians and civilians, used disproportionate force, and sexually harassed women protesters. The metro shutdown violated court directions.
allegations.by: RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha, in a Supreme Court plea (via LiveLaw)

allegations.claim: Some AISA workers were "brutally beaten in detention" and had not been released as of Saturday night.
allegations.by: AISA's N Sai Balaji, via The Indian Express (AISA claim)

allegations.claim: Journalists from The Quint, The Wire, Scroll, Reporter TV, Navbharat Times and Newslaundry, and senior journalist Paranjoy Guha Thakurta, were detained despite showing press cards. Some had phones and equipment seized. The organisations called it "reminiscent of a fascist state" and demanded a public apology from Delhi Police. Hindustan Times also reports that men claiming to be from Bajrang Dal threatened journalists near Palika Bazaar at 2:30 PM on Saturday; police chased them away and detained some.
allegations.by: Press Club of India, Indian Women's Press Corps, Delhi Union of Journalists and Kerala Union of Working Journalists (Delhi unit), via Hindustan Times citing PTI (9:35 AM)

allegations.claim: Lawyers protesting near the Supreme Court, including women, were illegally detained and manhandled. The internet was shut for 4 km, virtual courts were inaccessible, and lawyers were "lifted."
allegations.by: SCAORA, argued by president Devvrat (via Bar & Bench)

allegations.claim: What is at stake is "the suspension of citizens' peacefully exercised constitutional rights." "The last time this Court had to consider such... challenges, was at the time of the Emergency." She also told the court that GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya Metro stations, and others, were completely shut, which she called a deliberate and wilful violation of the 9 Oct order.
allegations.by: Dr Menaka Guruswamy, in the Supreme Court (via Bar & Bench)

allegations.claim: Trains were supposed to be allowed from their origin and "That didn't happen." He sought an interim order that there be no Section 163 order, detentions or barricades outside the 4 km zone. People were picked up from trains and from outside the 4 km radius, and the internet was suspended. "Journalists are being impeded inside and outside."
allegations.by: Kapil Sibal, in the Supreme Court (via LiveLaw)

allegations.claim: A former junior of his "was lifted and taken away in a police van, taken nine kilometres away and dropped 11 kilometres away" and could not reach the Supreme Court. Police were without badges.
allegations.by: K.K. Venugopal, in the Supreme Court (via LiveLaw and Bar & Bench)

allegations.claim: Delhi Police did not release Abhijeet Dipke in time, so he missed his grandmother Savitribai Shankarrao Dipke's funeral on Sunday morning in Hingoli. His uncle Vilas Dipke disputed the police account that Dipke was informed and offered help to travel home.
allegations.by: Dipke's family, via PTI (12:40 PM) and Indian Express (1:02 PM). Delhi Police dispute the delay claim.

allegations.claim: Police are continuing to brutalise hundreds of SFI student activists who were detained in Connaught Place.
allegations.by: SFI, via The Wire (2:00 PM) and The Hindu (1:32 PM and 1:51 PM). The Hindu's 1:51 PM item is the students' own video claim that they were being taken to an unknown location.

allegations.claim: CJP leaders Ankit Bharadwaj, Anam, Mukesh all-rounder, Balakrishna and Sudhir Sangwan were detained on 11 Oct while protesting peacefully, and CJP South India lead Vijay Mallangi was unlawfully detained.
allegations.by: CJP (@Cockroachisback, 1:55 PM) and CJP via The Wire (2:00 PM). Not independently verified.

allegations.claim: Delhi Police brutally attacked CPI(M) MP John Brittas and later dropped him by the roadside, visibly injured. In an unverified video he says four CRPF personnel pinned him down in a vehicle until he struggled to breathe. He later told Indian Express, in an account posted at 3:00 AM on 12 Oct: "CRPF men forcefully detained me and threw me in a bus. They pinned me to a seat after grabbing me by the neck and choked me. It was only after a Delhi Police DCP's intervention that I was allowed to go." Indian Express says RAF and Delhi Police detained him at Connaught Place while he spoke to the media, and that he was taken to RML Hospital for treatment. His account.
allegations.by: CPI(M), via ThePrint (2:48 PM), repeated by India Today (3:46 PM). The video account is Brittas's, shared on X at 3:12 PM, and no outlet has verified it. Indian Express (posted 3:00 AM, 12 Oct) carries his later account.

allegations.claim: Three Indian Express Hindi reporters, Shashwat, Siya and Vijay, were put on a police bus at Connaught Place despite saying they were on duty, and the phones of Shashwat and Siya were seized and not returned. This was after the Supreme Court recorded an assurance that journalists would not be obstructed.
allegations.by: Indian Express, 3:57 PM.

allegations.claim: Delhi Police forcefully entered the airplane and kidnapped Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Abhijeet Dipke; there was no detention notice; phones were seized with no seizure memo; they were not allowed a lawyer; Das suspects the phones were hacked or cloned.
allegations.by: Saurav Das, at the Press Club press conference (PTI, about 2:50–3:02 PM; Hindustan Times). His allegation.

allegations.claim: Police used brute force on the march Neha Bora was leading, and protesters were badly beaten.
allegations.by: Protesters, via ThePrint and Scroll; the "badly beaten" wording is AISA's claim.

allegations.claim: Police visited volunteers' homes and intimidated parents from Friday night into Saturday, and Ratna Singh was followed by the Intelligence Bureau after she landed in Delhi. CJP also says police entered Gurdwara Bangla Sahib "with shoes, weapons."
allegations.by: Ratna Singh, via Hindustan Times, on the home visits and the IB claim. The gurdwara claim is CJP's, via Hindustan Times.

allegations.claim: Abhijeet Dipke was denied permission to speak to his cousin after news of his grandmother's death. Police released a video and say he declined offers of help, including a call to his parents.
allegations.by: CJP's Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, via Hindustan Times. Delhi Police, via ANI and the clip HT describes, dispute that account.

allegations.claim: Buses were turned into lockups, with cage-like doors and no air. Protesters were beaten in their private parts and abused with casteist and misogynist slurs. Detainees were taken beyond barricades where journalists were denied access, phones were snatched, and male protesters were beaten.
allegations.by: AISA, via its own posts and The Wire (about 4:49–5:22 PM). AISA's allegation. ThePrint (4:11 PM) carried Neha Bora, from inside a bus: "Are buses the new jails?"

allegations.claim: The Delhi Sikh Gurdwara Management Committee complained to Delhi Police against Arvind Kejriwal and AAP MLAs and workers over the Bangla Sahib incident. CJP's separate claim, that police entered the gurdwara with shoes and weapons, is unchanged. On 12 Oct at 9:41 AM, PTI via The Hindu, citing police sources, reported that Delhi Police filed an FIR against Arvind Kejriwal and other AAP leaders on that complaint, over the alleged ruckus at Gurdwara Bangla Sahib on 11 Oct. The committee alleges AAP workers protested inside and misused the gurdwara for politics, and that AAP leaders circulated a distorted version on social media. Police say footage is being examined. That is the police and committee account. No AAP response was found in this report.
allegations.by: DSGMC, via PTI and Indian Express (5:30 PM); FIR via PTI and The Hindu (9:41 AM, 12 Oct).

allegations.claim: Delhi Police deleted the parts of the Dipke video in which he asked for his phone to get his cousin's number and asked to speak to his lawyers. He also says both requests were refused, and that at 3:30 AM police told him to call his father and say he was going to jail for a long time. On 12 Oct in Hingoli he said (PTI video, 10:16 AM; IANS, 10:29–10:32 AM): "Delhi Police, if you have the courage, release the entire video in which I repeatedly asked them to let me speak to my cousin, give me my phone for two minutes and allow me to speak to my lawyer." He also said police may have felt ashamed of alleged molestation by male officers and so used female officers. That is his allegation. On X, via PTI and The Hindu (11:13 AM): "Youth are being assaulted, journalists are being assaulted, even MPs are being assaulted by Delhi Police. What makes Gyanesh Kumar so indispensable to Modi that he is willing to wage war against everyone just to protect him?" His words. The police position already on his card is that he was offered help and declined.
allegations.by: Abhijeet Dipke, on X (6:31 PM and 7:24 PM) and via State Mirror quoting Neha Bora's team account. His claim. PTI (7:52 PM) describes the released video as a woman officer offering transport and Dipke repeatedly saying he would stay. Delhi Police deny they delayed his release.

allegations.claim: Young protesters on Saturday were beaten both by police and by BJP workers.
allegations.by: Rahul Gandhi, in the post announcing Monday's march to the Supreme Court (Indian Express, 6:59 PM; PTI, 7:07 PM). His allegation.

allegations.claim: Female detainees are refusing to leave detention centres until all male protesters are released.
allegations.by: AISA (7:49 PM). AISA's claim. Not independently verified.

allegations.claim: Unbelievable stories of police brutality are coming out against CJP leaders. From tomorrow, not a single CJP leader will leave a detention centre without a medico-legal certificate.
allegations.by: Ashutosh Ranka (X, 10:05 PM). His allegation.

allegations.claim: Delhi Police are "collaborating with these sexual assaulters."
allegations.by: Saurav Das (X, 8:51 PM). His claim.

allegations.claim: Officers called him at 3:30 AM and asked him to tell his parents he could be jailed "for a long time." He rejects the police claim that they offered help, and says they "wanted to torment my parents."
allegations.by: Abhijeet Dipke (India Today, 9:16 PM; ThePrint, 8:47 PM). His account.

allegations.claim: About eight men followed and filmed CJP's Jharkhand coordinator on a Ranchi–Delhi train on the night of 8 Oct. A ticket examiner warned her she could be detained once the train entered Uttar Pradesh, and she got off at Bokaro around 3:30 AM. Railway security said they had no information.
allegations.by: Khusboo Choudhary, CJP Jharkhand coordinator, to PTI (Indian Express, 10:01 PM). Her allegation. The railway-security line is Indian Express's.

allegations.claim: CJP national spokesperson Sudhir Sangwan and joint secretary Balakrishnan Shukla were detained from Connaught Place on Sunday evening and their whereabouts remain unknown. They have not been allowed to contact their lawyers.
allegations.by: Ratna Singh (X, 8:43 PM), CJP (10:48 PM) and Saurav Das (1:07 AM). CJP's claims. No police response found.

allegations.claim: Till a few minutes ago, Ratna Singh and Saurav Das were being followed by two goon-looking guys at point-blank range.
allegations.by: Saurav Das (X, 10:10 PM). His claim.

allegations.claim: Journalists he names as detained in Delhi include PeekTV, RedMike, Pragya Mishra, Shyam Meera Singh, Harsh Yadav and Rosy. "We are in a state of emergency."
allegations.by: Ashutosh Ranka (X, 11:10 PM). His claim.

allegations.claim: The Democratic Youth Federation of India will move the Supreme Court over alleged illegal detention and custodial torture of its activists. On 12 Oct at about 1:49 PM, The Hindu's live blog reported that Rajya Sabha MP A.A. Rahim had moved the Supreme Court. The plea alleges illegal detention, "secret transportation" in specialised compartmentalised vehicles, and custodial torture of DYFI office-bearers and activists by police on 11 Oct at Connaught Place. That is DYFI's allegation.
allegations.by: A.A. Rahim MP, DYFI president (The Hindu, 11 Oct; live blog 8:03 AM and 1:49 PM, 12 Oct). DYFI's allegation. The 1:49 PM item says the petition has been moved.

allegations.claim: The CPI(M) Central Committee says it will intensify the struggle against the Special Intensive Revision. It demands that the Chief Election Commissioner resign, that the revision be withdrawn, and that the law on appointing Election Commissioners be repealed. It alleges bulk Form-7 filings by BJP workers to delete genuine voters, and condemns Delhi Police action against the protests.
allegations.by: CPI(M) Central Committee (PTI, about 3:46 PM, via The Hindu). CPI(M)'s demands and allegation.

allegations.claim: About 50 police were stationed outside his residence, three or four cars followed him, and he was threatened with being picked up again if he went near a protest. Asked if this was house arrest, he said: "Unofficially, I would say so." He also said he is an Indian citizen and there is no visa issue for him. No police confirmation was found as of 9:35 PM on 12 Oct.
allegations.by: Dhruv Rathee (to The Lallantop; India Today, updated 12:16 PM)

allegations.claim: BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari (ANI, 2:41 AM; IANS, 3:05 AM, 13 Oct) alleges Rahul Gandhi "grabbed a female journalist, hit her with the elbow and made her fall" near the Supreme Court on Monday evening, and says she is hospitalised. BJP Delhi vice-president Rajesh Bhatia (ANI, 2:43 AM) says her sister told him the journalist, who is pregnant, was pushed by Gandhi and admitted for observation. BJP MLA Umang Bajaj (ANI, 2:47 AM) names her as Richa Parashar. The clips they cite are from about 9 PM on Monday. Gandhi supporters on X, including a post at 12:33 AM, argue the clip shows her own camera person, not Gandhi, pushing her. No official Congress response was found. No police complaint or FIR was reported. This is a BJP allegation, and it is disputed.
allegations.by: BJP spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari, BJP Delhi vice-president Rajesh Bhatia and BJP MLA Umang Bajaj (ANI and IANS, 2:41–3:05 AM, 13 Oct). Their allegation. Disputed on X. No Congress response found.

allegations.claim: The SHO of Jaffarpur Kalan police station refused to let a lawyer meet detained CJP leaders Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka, Ajinkya Shinde and others, and their phones were confiscated. Pushp Sharma says he has not been allowed to meet Das, Ranka and 12 others, that Das's last WhatsApp said phones were being taken, and that the SHO told him the phones are "kept safe." Dipke says the three leaders were held at separate locations and that 11 volunteers were taken elsewhere.
allegations.by: Ratna Singh, CJP legal head, and Pushp Sharma (The Hindu, about 2:20 PM; Hindustan Times, updated about 2:52 PM; her X post about 12:39 PM). Dipke's location claim is his, via ETV Bharat (about 3:08 PM). Police were not quoted in reply.

allegations.claim: Delhi Police are still holding Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde, will not let lawyers meet them, kept the three separately, took 11 volunteers elsewhere, and threatened others with detention. Dipke called the lawyer bar kidnapping. CJP also called the detention illegal and a denial of fundamental rights, and asked for their release.
allegations.by: Abhijeet Dipke, citing Ratna Singh, via ANI (Times of India, about 5:52 PM). CJP's illegal-detention accusation is The Hindu's report (about 4:48 PM). Police were not quoted in reply.

govt_position.point: Permission denied: the application came less than 10 days ahead, and conditions were allegedly breached at the July agitation. Public safety, traffic and law and order cited
BNSS Sec 163 (prohibitory) orders in central Delhi; also in Noida 10–20 Oct
Police say the curbs are 'temporary and precautionary' and for the safety of protesters and others
BJP president Nitin Nabin accuses CJP and the INDIA bloc of trying to 'destabilise' the country. The EC and BJP deny wrongdoing in SIR
Chennai police: protesters 'had not obtained permission'

Delhi Police (via ANI): Dipke was detained because the protest call 'was not permitted'; police say they told him of his grandmother's death with due sensitivity and offered possible help to travel home

BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad: 'CJP is doing shadow boxing for the Aam Aadmi Party'; calls the opposition 'defeated, desperate individuals ... weaponizing street protests'; says SIR is a legal provision conducted 'more than nine times'
Tribune live blog (updated 4:27 PM): about 35,000 Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel deployed; police using drones to monitor movement
BJP: 'India is not a banana republic' (NDTV, attacking Congress and CJP).
Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Dhami says voter-roll revision is not new.
Delhi Police released a video explaining why permission for the CJP protest was denied (NDTV, 5:23 PM).

Police say an officer was injured in stone pelting. The officer says a crowd of 100–150 had gathered near the Hanuman temple and protesters twisted his arm while being detained (ANI, 5:19 PM). Police account.
Police, via ThePrint (5:28 PM): detentions could last up to 24 hours.

Delhi Police: two personnel, including Pink Force member Suman and Dheeraj Yadav, were injured during detentions (The Hindu, 5:33 PM, citing a senior officer). Sub-Inspector Bajrang Yadav says he was injured while stopping people running from the CPM office (ANI, 5:46 PM). Police account.
124 former IAS/IFS officers' open letter defends the Election Commission and SIR (PTI, 5:28 PM).
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta (PTI, 6:15–6:22 PM): 'Delhi will not be held hostage'; calls CJP the 'B-Team' of Rahul Gandhi and Arvind Kejriwal.
Union Minister Piyush Goyal (IANS, 6:23 PM): Rahul Gandhi has no respect for any constitutional authority.
BJP MP Sujeet Kumar (PTI, 6:22 PM): Delhi Police denied CJP permission because of its 'past antecedents'.
Bengaluru Police Commissioner Seemant Singh (The Hindu, 6:00 PM): marchers were detained because permission was for a protest, not a march to the CEO's office.

DMRC: the 45 Metro stations closed since 9 PM Friday stay shut till 10 PM on 10 Oct, then security agencies will review (ANI, PTI, ~6:10–6:12 PM). DMRC (via IANS, ~10:36 PM; Delhi Police reposted DMRC at 11:09 PM): all Delhi Metro station gates reopened and interchanges were restored. 45 stations had been closed.
A senior Delhi Police officer (The Hindu, 6:53 PM): the process to release protesters detained across Delhi has begun. No count given, and no named leader's release was confirmed.
Union Minister Ramdas Athawale (ANI, 6:49 PM): police did not oppose an earlier CJP protest while it was peaceful, but violence and stone-pelting followed.
Tapas Roy and Bishal Lama, described by ANI as West Bengal ministers (6:58–7:00 PM): Roy called protesters 'traitors' and 'anti-national'; Lama said grievances should go to court.
Delhi Police (via IANS, 7:12 PM): Dipke was promptly told of his grandmother's death with due sensitivity, told the funeral time, and offered all possible assistance to travel home.
Delhi Police sources (The Hindu, 7:38 PM): women and senior citizens are being released first; due legal process will be followed for CJP leaders; deployment continues.

BJP spokesperson Ravi Shankar Prasad (NDTV, 7:41 PM): 'India is not a banana republic'; democracy 'thwarted attempts to incite anarchy' and the country 'will be governed by Parliament, not by the streets'.
New Delhi DCP video (The Hindu, 8:27 PM): the Jantar Mantar area was clear of protesters, countering social-media claims of a large gathering.
Goa CM Pramod Sawant (ANI, 9:01 PM): the Election Commission is an independent institution and SIR was carried out under the constitutional mechanism.
BJP's Gourav Vallabh (ANI, 8:36 PM) demanded Rahul Gandhi resign as Leader of the Opposition for 'spreading anarchy, fear, and confusion'.

Delhi CM Rekha Gupta (via PTI, 9:39 PM): what happened on Delhi's streets was 'extremely unfortunate'. She says Congress, AAP, the Left and CJP people 'openly ran riot' in the name of protest and provoked Delhi Police and the security forces. Attributed as her statement.

BJP spokesperson RP Singh (IANS, 9:22 PM): police 'did not have a good experience with CJP last time'. He claims there was stone-pelting and a lathi-charge then, with 60 students and 120 police injured. Attributed as his claim.

Delhi Police (via Hindustan Times, 10:47 PM): Dipke was "immediately" told of his grandmother's death and the funeral time and offered "possible facilitation" to travel home. The same report says police say nearly 4,000 people were detained in Delhi today.

India, in a statement on the India at UN account (11:21 PM to 12:02 AM), called the UN Human Rights Office's concerns "misplaced" and an "unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India". It said, "India is the world's largest democracy, where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by our Constitution," and that the office "would also do well to devote comparable attention to large-scale protests elsewhere" (NDTV, Hindustan Times, IANS).

Delhi Police (Hindustan Times, 11:25 PM) posted a video on X titled "Broken promises, shattered trust", explaining why they denied permission for the Jantar Mantar protest. Police say CJP broke the signed undertaking it gave during the June–July protests against then education minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Attributed as the police's claim.
DCP New Delhi (ANI, 11:19 PM), responding to a video of police wearing shoes inside Gurudwara Bangla Sahib, said the staff were walking in a common passage. Attributed as the police's explanation.

Indian Express (updated 7:19 AM): around 30,000 police personnel and 200 companies of paramilitary forces will remain deployed on Sunday ahead of CJP's 10 AM march. Barricades at Parliament Street and Jantar Mantar stay in place. A police officer said metro and train measures could be taken depending on the situation. Police will review on Sunday evening before deciding Monday's deployment. Police sources told IE that detainees were kept at around 30 detention centres.

The Hindu (Vijaita Singh, ~9:41 AM): the Union Home Ministry ordered mobile internet suspended within 500 metres of eight makeshift detention centres in Delhi from noon to 10 PM on 10 Oct. The order is dated 9 Oct and was issued by the Union Home Secretary under the Telecommunications Act, 2023, citing public safety and public order. Venues: Chhatrasal Stadium (Model Town), Rajiv Gandhi Stadium (Bawana), Yamuna Sports Complex, Jasola Sports Complex, Community Centre Daulatpur, Community Centre Pandwala Khurd, Jangli Ram Stadium (Nizampur, Kanjhawala) and Surajmal Stadium (Nangloi). The Hindu says around 2,500 protesters were sent to these centres and released later in the day.

LiveLaw (9:50 AM): a prohibitory order under Section 163 BNSS is in force on Bhagwan Das Road in front of the Supreme Court. Police barricades warn that force may be used if people do not disperse peacefully. This is ahead of the INDIA bloc's planned Monday march to the Supreme Court.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, in the Supreme Court on 11 Oct (attributed to him): on the habeas pleas, "a statutory regime was followed" and "Most of these people mentioned here were picked up at 2 p.m. and they were released at around 6 o'clock." He said there was "no curtailment of any metro service on the 10th" and "zero reduction in the total volume of metro operations", with 4,157 train trips on 10 Oct across a 303-station network, and that an affidavit would follow. He said 47 stations were closed or restricted, "only 15%" (LiveLaw). Bar & Bench says Justice Bagchi noted that authorities first proposed closing 57 and that 45 were closed after the court's order. LiveLaw quotes 47. Both figures are kept. He said all Metro stations are open today, and that Metro services will remain normal unless a public-order situation arises. On the Section 163 board on Bhagwan Das Road, he said he had "just been informed about this now."

India Today (11:14 AM): Delhi Police filed 20 FIRs over the 10 Oct CJP protest, for obstructing official work and assaulting police. Indian Express (10:54 AM): four right-wing men were arrested over a viral video showing students and women being assaulted. Hindustan Times (12:44 PM): senior officers said more than 20 FIRs were registered over attempts to protest at Jantar Mantar, including over alleged attacks on police. Police cite the July CJP NEET protest, in which they say more than 200 police were injured, Jantar Mantar's safe capacity of about 1,000, and that organisers notified them only on 7 Oct against a 10-day requirement. That is the police account. PTI (2:47 PM; ThePrint, 3:13 PM) says a Kamla Market FIR includes the arrest of four men who claimed links to the Hindu Raksha Dal, for allegedly assaulting students and manhandling women during Saturday's protest. That is further detail on the arrest Indian Express reported at 10:54 AM, not a second set of arrests. Hindustan Times (8:22 AM, 12 Oct) names the four as Raman Saini, 50, and Vivekanand, 32, of Delhi, and Kapil Kumar, 27, and Ravinder Singh, 35, of Ghaziabad, apprehended over an assault on a minor near Civic Centre. Police say the case was registered suo motu and that nobody, including the minor, complained. The accused say protesters had confronted them first. Police say the initial probe found no evidence for that. Hindu Raksha Dal chief Pinky Chaudhary (Bhupender Tomar) posted, "These are my warriors. Wherever cockroaches are found, we will fix their minds." Hindustan Times got no police comment on that post.

Hindustan Times (11:40 AM): police are keeping central Delhi sealed on Sunday. Jantar Mantar is shut, borders are barricaded, and traffic is diverted at 30 points, as CJP says it will march again. Shiv Sena's Shaina NC (ANI, 11:45–11:48 AM) said no arrest has been made and that preventive action was taken, and that removing the Chief Election Commissioner is a matter for Parliament, not the streets. Her statement.

Advocate Barun Kumar Sinha (ANI, 1:31 PM) said the Supreme Court passed only three interim orders, on the Metro, the internet and lawyers, deferred the rest to Tuesday, and did not pass a contempt order beyond seeking a response. His reading of the order.
Union Minister Sukanta Majumdar (ANI, 2:01 PM): "There was no permission for the program." His statement.
BJP MP Tarun Chugh (ANI, 3:39 PM): "The mood of the country is against the protesters." His statement.
Union Minister Pralhad Joshi (ANI, 4:01 PM): "They were detained because there was no permission for where they planned the protests." His statement.

Delhi Police press conference (about 5:29 PM). DCP Neha Yadav (ANI, 5:38 PM) said officers told Abhijeet Dipke of his grandmother's death and offered all possible assistance, including flights and phone calls, and that he declined to speak to his parents. Hindustan Times says the police clip shows him declining an offer to return home. Police account. CJP's Ranka and Das say he was denied a call to his cousin. ANI also listed the briefing as covering alleged attacks on police; no details of that part were reported.

Union Minister Ramdas Athawale (PTI, 4:09 PM) backed the Chief Election Commissioner, said there is no need for him to resign, and accused CJP of inviting chaos. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh (NDTV) said dissent is a right but "spreading anarchy is not anyone's right." Their statements.

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, as recorded in the Supreme Court's written order: no violation of the 9 Oct order; 45 of 303 Metro stations were closed for law and order; nobody was illegally detained; the habeas plea is infructuous because detainees were released. His submission.
Delhi Police, via The Wire live blog (6:30 PM): permission to CJP was denied because of a failure to follow procedures and a history of non-compliance with the laws. Police account.

DCP Neha Yadav (Indian Express, 9:19 PM) shared the police video of officers speaking to Abhijeet Dipke and reiterated that permission for the protest was denied because of past non-compliance. Police account. Dipke rejects the claim that police offered help.
BJP MP Hemang Joshi (PTI, 9:36 PM): the so-called "Protest 2.0" "failed miserably." BJP view. IANS (10:20 PM): he alleged CJP is a "subsidiary of the Aam Aadmi Party." His allegation.

Senior Advocate Adish C. Aggarwala, chairman of the All India Bar Association, urged Rahul Gandhi to reconsider the 12 Oct visit of opposition leaders to the Supreme Court (ANI, via webindia123, 11 Oct).
Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta accused Congress, AAP, Left parties and CJP of creating chaos in the city (News9). Her accusation.
BJP MP Manoj Tiwari (IANS, 10:29 PM): "Gen Z no longer supports the protests organized by these people." His words.
Rajasthan minister Madan Dilawar (IANS, 11:00 PM) appealed to youth and said the BJP government and Prime Minister Modi are taking care of everyone's needs. His words.
Shiv Sena's Shaina NC (ANI, 10:54 AM, 12 Oct): "The Chief Justice of India, Surya Kant has already said that the matter is sub judice, so Rahul Gandhi, stop your drama." Her words.
BJP's Ram Kadam (PTI, 11:06 AM, 12 Oct) said opposition leaders "do not understand the difference between the judiciary and the executive." His words.
Bihar BJP chief Sanjay Saraogi (IANS, 10:01 AM, 12 Oct) called the protest a "cheap spectacle of creating chaos on the streets and putting pressure on the Election Commission." His words.
West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh (Mint, 12 Oct): "Are they now going to try to intimidate the Supreme Court too? No one is above the law." His words.

Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar's order, dated 11 Oct 2026 and made public on 12 Oct between about 1:47 and 2:01 PM, partially modifies Standing Order No. L&O/48/22 of 28 Apr 2022. The police and Home Ministry account, via PTI, Indian Express, India Today, The Hindu and News On AIR: a Home Ministry committee examined alternative venues for protests, and on its recommendation Jantar Mantar has been de-notified as a designated protest site. Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground, East Delhi are designated instead. A revised standard operating procedure is to be issued separately.

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis (PTI, about 1:42 PM, via The Hindu): the Opposition is trying to "demonise" judicial institutions after the Chief Justice declined a meeting, and the march is "anti-constitutional." His words.

Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan (PTI, about 3:00 PM, via The Hindu): Rahul Gandhi's march to the Supreme Court is "drama", and Congress is trying to create anarchy by spreading falsehoods. His words.
Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi (PTI, about 1:51 PM, via The Hindu) defended the Special Intensive Revision as necessary to uphold electoral integrity and clean rolls. His words.

Delhi Police (about 4:46 PM) posted a video captioned "Beyond the chaos & hate you see online, the reality speaks for itself." India.com describes the clip as officers distributing food and water and assisting detained demonstrators, prompting "Delhi Police Zindabad" chants. That is the account attached to the police video.

Delhi Police (about 5:05 PM) issued a "FACT CHECK" calling a viral claim that police fired on Rahul Gandhi's rally and killed five workers a rumour and fake news, and warned of legal action. No news outlet reported any firing. The police account is that the claim is false.

BJP spokesperson Harsh Singh Dahiya (News18, about 6:15 PM), on the de-notification of Jantar Mantar: "The venue has changed but the right to protest remains - the new sites will be convenient for protestors as well." His words.
Union Minister Pralhad Joshi (PTI video, about 9:20 PM on 12 Oct), as captioned by PTI: "Cong protest against EC, SIR conspiracy funded by foreign organisations." His allegation.
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma (ANI, about 8:39 PM on 12 Oct): "Ask your Govts to resign first." His challenge to Rahul Gandhi over the Chief Election Commissioner and the electoral roll.
Union Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia (ANI, about 9:12 PM on 12 Oct): "Decisions are made in court of people, not on streets." His words, hitting the Opposition protest.

Khan Market Traders Association president Sanjiv Mehra (PTI video, 11:25 PM, 12 Oct) said "CJP indulging in vandalism and spreading anarchy", that road closures caused "huge business losses", and that the association will move the Supreme Court "seeking a ban on protests here." His claims. ANI (8:04 AM, 13 Oct) spells the president Sanjeev Mehra and quotes him saying business has been hit and that the police perimeter starts 1 km out. PTI's video spelled the name Sanjiv. Both spellings are kept. His claims.

NDMC vice-chairman Kuljeet Singh Chahal (PTI, 8:51 AM; IANS, 9:03 AM, 13 Oct), at a cleanliness drive near Mandi House after Monday's march: "The Aam Aadmi Party, Rahul Gandhi and the CJP have made it a daily agenda to harass New Delhi and its people. This is not a case of vote theft." His words.

BJP MP Jagdambika Pal (IANS, 9:07 AM, 13 Oct) said the INDIA bloc has every right to petition the Supreme Court, and asked whether any Leader of the Opposition has ever marched against the judiciary. His words.
Telangana BJP president Ramchandra Rao (IANS, 9:02 AM, 13 Oct) said Rahul Gandhi "is dragging the Supreme Court and the judiciary into a political controversy." His words.

Union minister Kiren Rijiju shared a screenshot of a deleted Congress Keralam post that told Chief Justice Surya Kant to resign, and accused Congress of targeting constitutional institutions. BJP spokesperson C.R. Kesavan (PTI video, 7:21 AM, 13 Oct) called the post "uncouth language... to openly threaten and abuse the high office of Chief Justice of India." Their words. KPCC president Sunny Joseph said the person responsible was removed and that the post was made without the leadership's knowledge or consent.

Delhi Police, via PTI and The Hindu (about 9:11 AM, 13 Oct), sought an extension of 273 companies of central armed police in Delhi until 20 Oct, citing possible protests by CJP and others. The deployment had been due to end on Monday. The request went to the Home Ministry. Sources said 301 companies had been approved, 221 on 6 Oct and 80 on 8 Oct, and that 28 of the additional 80 had not reported as of Monday. Police flagged possible demonstrations at Jantar Mantar, the Election Commission, Parliament House and India Gate. That is the police request.

Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma opposed notice on the Indian Youth Congress plea. He said the petition is about demonstrating at Jantar Mantar, that the site was de-notified pursuant to Supreme Court orders, and that the plea cannot stand unless the de-notification itself is challenged. The court still issued notice on three prayers and listed the matter for 17 Nov (LiveLaw, 6:08 PM).

legal_context: Article 22(1): anyone arrested has the right to be told the grounds and to consult a lawyer. Article 22(2): they must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours.
D.K. Basu guidelines (SC, 1997): arrest memo, informing a relative, and the place of custody must be disclosed.
BNSS Sec 163: prohibitory orders (formerly CrPC 144). BNSS Sec 172: police may detain people who resist lawful directions.
Note: these are general legal standards shown for reference. Whether they were broken in any specific case has not been decided by a court.

12 Oct 2026: Delhi Police say Jantar Mantar is no longer a designated protest site. Commissioner Anurag Kumar's order, dated 11 Oct 2026 and made public that afternoon, partially modifies Standing Order No. L&O/48/22 of 28 Apr 2022. On a Home Ministry committee's recommendation, the designated venues are now Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground, East Delhi, with a revised procedure still to be issued. That is the police and ministry position, via PTI, Indian Express, India Today, The Hindu and News On AIR. It is not a court ruling.

courts.court: Supreme Court (CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana)
courts.action: Called the transport notifications 'overreaching' and ruled out complete prohibition of metro and trains ('don't use a hammer to kill a fly'). The SG agreed authorities would reassess. Compliance reports due in 4 days. The court also said that protesting without permission can lead to prosecution.

Refused an urgent hearing on the Youth Congress plea for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar. Listed for Mon 12 Oct. On 12 Oct, Justice Amit Mahajan began the hearing around 11:35–11:39 AM. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, for Delhi Police, sought time until tomorrow for instructions. The plea was adjourned to 13 Oct (Bar & Bench, 11:40–11:41 AM; LiveLaw, 11:40 AM and 11:48 AM). On 13 Oct, Indian Express (about 12:36 PM): before Justice Amit Mahajan, Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma said the Indian Youth Congress plea for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar, filed for president Uday Bhanu Chib, had become "infructuous" after the site was de-notified. Senior advocate Siddharth Luthra, for Chib, said it was not infructuous, alleged "subterfuge", and said notice must issue and that they would amend the plea. The court passed the matter over, to take it up later the same day, with Luthra to appear in person. No final order was reported as of 3:11 PM. Later on 13 Oct, LiveLaw (6:08 PM): Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice on prayers (c), (d) and (f) and listed the matter for 17 Nov. Prayer (c) seeks a declaration that the 2022 standing order cannot impose an automatic ban on a peaceful assembly. Prayer (d) seeks a fresh, reasoned look at the protest request. Prayer (f) seeks a declaration that the 10-day application rule is not an absolute bar. Senior advocate Siddharth Luthra, for Uday Bhanu Chib, said he would amend the prayers after the de-notification and called conditions in the 2022 order bad in law. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma opposed notice. He said the petition is about demonstrating at Jantar Mantar, that the site was de-notified pursuant to Supreme Court orders, and that the petition cannot stand unless the de-notification is challenged. Notice on those three prayers is not an order granting permission to protest.

Contempt petition filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi over the blanket closure of metro stations and train cancellations, alleged to violate the Supreme Court's 9 Oct order. A special Sunday bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana will hear it on 11 Oct. Respondents named by IANS: Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chairperson D. Thara. LiveLaw reported again at 10:02 PM, and The Hindu at 9:17 PM, that the special Sunday sitting on 11 Oct is still listed. 11:08 PM: in a PTI video, petitioner Advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi says the authorities "openly violated" the Supreme Court's 9 Oct order; he filed the contempt petition heard at Sunday's special sitting. Bar & Bench (7:15 AM, 11 Oct) says the special Sunday bench assembles at 10:30 AM.
After SCBA, SCAORA and the SG flagged the detentions, CJI Surya Kant spoke to authorities and the detained lawyers were released.

Saket court dismissed Ratna Singh's application seeking an FIR against police personnel over her detention and a direction for her release (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench, ANI, 5:53 PM). ANI reported she had been released. The Hindu says she posted at 7:13 PM that she was still detained, so the release report conflicts with her own account. Earlier, at about 4:58 PM, the order was under dictation. LiveLaw had reported at about 3:20 PM that staff said the judge was dictating an order in a different case. The Hindu (8:32 PM) and The Wire (8:54 PM) also report that a Delhi court dismissed her wrongful-confinement plea. LiveLaw (9:26 PM): the Delhi court rejected her plea for an FIR against policemen for wrongful confinement and for restraining her from protesting.

courts.court: Supreme Court (special Sunday bench, 10:30 AM: Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana)
courts.action: Menaka Guruswamy's plea is a habeas corpus petition. It challenges the detention of Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan, Manik Sarkar and other political leaders. To be heard on Sunday 11 Oct at the special sitting before Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana (LiveLaw). She told Bar & Bench that preventive detention cannot be used to suppress the right to peaceful protest. Bar & Bench (7:15 AM, 11 Oct): the bench assembles at 10:30 AM. Matters: Shailendra Mani Tripathi's contempt plea against Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chair D. Thara; Menaka Guruswamy's plea against preventive detention of opposition leaders, including four former chief ministers; and detention and alleged police excesses against lawyers, including Senior Advocate Shadan Farasat. Advocate Aman Prasad's contempt petition against the Delhi Police Commissioner is likely to be mentioned (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench). RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha has also moved the court the same morning seeking urgent directions (LiveLaw). At the hearing, which began about 10:32 AM, LiveLaw reported that the court restrained the virtual-hearing facility and then sat in Court No. 5; the virtual-hearing position was also described as a Webex meeting at full capacity, so that point is unclear. Bar & Bench named Kapil Sibal, Gopal Sankaranarayanan, Menaka Guruswamy, Arundhati Katju, Sanjay Hegde and advocate-on-record Anas Tanwir for the petitioners, and Solicitor General Tushar Mehta for the respondents. On K.K. Venugopal's contempt plea, Justice Bagchi said a similar petition was already before the court and proposed posting it to Monday; Venugopal asked for listing and replies, and the court said it would. At about 11:48 AM the bench said it will pass an interim order: the Metro should run normally unless a law-and-order situation arises, the public should have free movement, the internet should be restored, and lawyers should not be obstructed in their professional duties (LiveLaw). Bar & Bench quotes Justice Bagchi that no advocate should be hindered in discharging their professional duties, and that he summarised the Solicitor General as saying Metro services are normalised unless a public-order situation arises and that the internet is already restored. SG Tushar Mehta said all Metro stations are open today. India Today's live headline said barricades should be removed across Delhi and the internet cannot be shut down. LiveLaw's wording is the more precise account. From 12:03 PM Justice Bagchi was dictating the order (Bar & Bench). It records urgent applications alleging violation of the 9 Oct order and illegal detention on 10 Oct, and Dr Menaka Guruswamy's statement that GTB Nagar and Vishwavidyalaya Metro stations, and others, were completely shut, which she called a deliberate and wilful violation (her allegation, as recorded). The state was asked to explain the circumstances, manner and justification of the detentions and to give station-wise Metro details on a map in its affidavit. Interim order passed (Bar & Bench, published 12:51 PM; the court rose about 12:36 PM). Metro and rail are to function normally unless regulation is needed for public order under Article 19(2). People may move freely in the city, subject to traffic regulations, and barricades are to be reviewed forthwith. The internet shall remain undisturbed, as per law; the order does not take away powers under the IT Act. No illegal detention except by procedure established by law. Peaceful assembly is to be permitted, particularly outside the area where Section 163 BNSS is in force. The Section 163 BNSS notice board near the Supreme Court is to be taken down. The court recorded an assurance that lawyers, journalists and other professionals will not be obstructed. A contempt notice was issued. The authorities are to file a short affidavit showing cause why contempt proceedings should not be initiated, plus a compliance report, including Metro restrictions and railway advisories, by Tuesday 13 Oct. Habeas corpus petitions on the mass detentions, and connected matters, are to be heard with the main cases on 13 Oct. The principal contempt petition is by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, against Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and DMRC chair D. Thara (Bar & Bench). Justice V. Mohana asked those present to undertake to protest peacefully and not instigate others. Gopal Sankaranarayanan agreed, and asked for a matching undertaking on how police treat peaceful protesters. The court said the State must explain the circumstances, manner and legal justification of the detentions, and is duty-bound under Article 32. During the hearing the bench had proposed posting K.K. Venugopal's contempt plea to Monday. The reported order sets the next hearing for Tuesday 13 Oct. NDTV posted key takeaways at 1:50 PM. Written order uploaded at about 5:25 PM (LiveLaw PDF; Bar & Bench, 5:10 PM). The court finds a prima facie case of contempt over the alleged Metro and train shutdown, treated as a violation of its 9 Oct order. Notice was issued to the alleged contemnors. LiveLaw names Union Home Secretary Govind Mohan, the Delhi Police Commissioner and the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation. They are to file counter-affidavits, including a compliance report, by 13 Oct. Personal appearance is dispensed with for now. Notice was also issued on the habeas corpus petition. Menaka Guruswamy argued that it covers illegal detention of about 7,000 people, not only named leaders. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta denied any violation. He said 45 of 303 Metro stations had been closed for law and order, denied that anyone was illegally detained, and called the habeas plea infructuous because detainees had been released. That is his submission, as recorded. The order directs that the Metro and trains run normally, subject to Article 19(2); that people move freely, with barricades reviewed forthwith; that the internet not be hindered; that there be no illegal detention of peaceful unarmed assemblies beyond the Section 163 BNSS area; and that the Section 163 notice board at the Supreme Court premises be taken down. Lawyers, journalists and other professionals shall not be hindered in any manner whatsoever. Listed again on 13 Oct with the other tagged petitions.

courts.court: Supreme Court (habeas corpus filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity; withdrawal sought)
courts.action: Correction: this habeas corpus petition was filed under Article 32 by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, between about 11:39 PM and 12:10 AM. It was not filed by CJP, and CJP's legal team did not approve it. It sought production and release of Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and others, disclosure of their whereabouts and the legal grounds for each detention, and preservation of CCTV footage, police diaries and movement registers. It asked whether the Section 163 BNSS order for Parliament Street can justify detentions at the airport and in Gurugram. It referred to the detention of Ratna Singh and other advocates and asked for their custodial status. It said it does not seek immunity from lawful action for any separate offence. Respondents named were the Centre, the Delhi government, Delhi Police, and Haryana, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh. Filed through advocates-on-record Rajesh G. Inamdar and Shashwat Anand. LawBeat says the plea also names Dhruv Rathee. Bar & Bench's report does not mention him (single source). At 12:48 AM Ratna Singh, CJP's legal cell chief, posted: "This petition is not filed by @Cockroachisback. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." CJP reposted that and added "Please note." Bar & Bench (12:46 AM and 12:58 AM) and LiveLaw (12:57 AM) report that Bharti has sought to withdraw the plea. It is not described as listed with Menaka Guruswamy's separate habeas plea. Her plea is unaffected; no new report on it.

A new contempt petition against Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar was filed by advocate Aman Prasad (LiveLaw, 7:28 AM; Bar & Bench, 7:53 AM). He alleges police used "indiscriminate violence" against citizens on 10 Oct, in violation of Supreme Court principles. The petition says protesters near Jantar Mantar, INA and Dilli Haat were assaulted; a protester was lifted, thrown to the ground and beaten near INA; a young advocate who intervened when police allegedly pulled at a woman's trousers near INA was beaten, suffered head injuries and was taken to a hospital in Chhatarpur Enclave; women were manhandled by male officers; videos purportedly show a woman dragged by her hair in a detention bus and a woman journalist dragged across a road; Scroll's Ayush Tiwari was detained despite showing a press pass; officers were without name tags; and 45 of 57 metro stations were shut, with road blocks and a mobile-internet shutdown. It relies on the court's 28 July and 18 August orders and the 9 Oct order. LiveLaw says it is likely to be mentioned today, on Bar & Bench's 10:30 AM mentioning list. All of these are the petitioner's allegations.

courts.court: Supreme Court (RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha)
courts.action: RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha has moved the Supreme Court seeking urgent directions against what he calls illegal detentions, "abduction" and house arrests of "unarmed" protesters, student leaders, advocates, politicians and civilians (LiveLaw, 8:02 AM). He alleges "disproportionate use of police force" and "sexual harassment of women" protesters, and says the metro shutdown violated court directions. Allegations are his. Bar & Bench says the special bench sits at 10:30 AM on the contempt, preventive-detention and lawyers' detention pleas.

courts.court: Special Executive Magistrate, South West District, at Delhi Cantt Police Station
courts.action: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were produced before the Special Executive Magistrate and released at about 10 AM on the magistrate's order (LiveLaw, 9:58 AM, citing CJP legal head Ratna Singh; Bar & Bench, 10:00 AM). Delhi Police had placed them under preventive arrest under BNSS Sections 126 and 170 (LiveLaw, Bar & Bench, PTI, Indian Express). India Today (9:00 AM, police sources) had said that no arrests had been made. LiveLaw (10:20 AM), citing Ratna Singh, says the release was on condition they will not engage in a breach of the peace for one year. PTI (10:54 AM) says they must "maintain peace" for one year. Delhi Police, via ANI (10:56 AM), say a surety bond of Rs 50,000 was taken and that all due legal procedures were followed. Police account.

courts.court: Supreme Court (habeas corpus reported by LiveLaw; not a CJP filing)
courts.action: LiveLaw (8:46 AM) says a CJP member filed a habeas corpus petition seeking production and release of Dipke, Das, Ranka and others. At 8:13 AM the account @CJP_for_India, which is not the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, posted a statement attributed to Ratna Singh: "This petition is not filed by @CJP_for_India. We are not approaching the Supreme Court, and no habeas corpus petition has been approved by the CJP's legal team." That post is unverified as a CJP statement because it is not from the official account.

The Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association moved the Supreme Court under Article 32 against the 10 Oct police action on protesting lawyers near the court, alleging illegal detention and manhandling of advocates, including women (Bar & Bench, 10:17 AM). SCAORA president Devvrat argued at the hearing that the internet was shut for 4 km, virtual courts were inaccessible, and lawyers were "lifted." Allegations are SCAORA's.

courts.court: Supreme Court (PIL on the internet shutdown)
courts.action: LiveLaw (11:08 AM): a PIL in the Supreme Court seeks scrutiny of the central Delhi internet shutdown.
LiveLaw (4:22 PM): the lawyers' body Lawyers' Voice moved the Supreme Court to intervene in the contempt case. It says CJP protests paralyse Delhi and hurt lawyers' livelihoods.

12 Oct: the INDIA bloc march will start at 1:30 PM from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba junction and go to the Supreme Court (Indian Express, 9:41 PM). Rahul Gandhi confirmed that time and place. At 9:32 PM he posted that students, civil-society groups and opposition parties should join a peaceful march to the Supreme Court. He and Mallikarjun Kharge are seeking to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice Surya Kant. Kharge told reporters they had written to the Chief Justice and had been given a slot between 4 PM and 5 PM on Monday (PTI via ThePrint). Kharge said, "We cannot demand anything before him (Surya Kant). We will request him with folded hands." That slot is Kharge's account, not a confirmation published by the court. Rahul says the memorandum demands an end to what he calls vote chori, a halt to the Special Intensive Revision, and Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. He alleged that young protesters on Saturday were beaten by police and by BJP workers. That is his allegation. He announced the march earlier on Sunday (Indian Express, 6:59 PM; PTI, 7:07 PM). PTI (9:47 PM): Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge, Leaders of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha, have both written to Chief Justice Surya Kant seeking a meeting between 4 PM and 5 PM on Monday to hand over a memorandum. The demands they describe include an end to what they call vote chori, Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, a halt to the Special Intensive Revision, and a return to paper ballots. Kharge, in Bengaluru, said: "We cannot demand. Only with folded hands, we can request him ... everywhere an undeclared emergency is imposed." His words. An earlier PTI report carried by ThePrint quoted him saying they had been given the 4–5 PM slot. Both wordings are his account. The court has not published a confirmation. News9 (updated 11:09 PM), citing people aware of the matter, says Chief Justice Surya Kant declined the 4–5 PM meeting. In an email reply he reportedly said the issues are already before the court, the court cannot meet political delegations at an administrative level, and they should file a petition. He stressed that the court's doors are open to everyone. That account is sourced to people aware of it, not to an official statement. K.C. Venugopal told ANI, via webindia123: "The CJI has declined to meet us, provided that open avenue for giving a petition to the Supreme Court by hand or a general legal way. We respect that decision, but we are very much for marching to the Supreme Court tomorrow." His words. The 1:30 PM march is still on. Indian Express (12:25 AM), reporting what it learnt, gives four points from the Chief Justice's reply: the SIR and CEC grievances are already pending; the court cannot take cognisance of them on the administrative side; if a petition is filed on Monday, Article 32 judicial review means it will be taken up on Tuesday 13 Oct with the matters already listed; and the court is committed to fundamental rights, with its doors always open. The 1:30 PM march from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba Road junction to the Supreme Court, about 2 km, is still on. The 4–5 PM meeting remains declined. On Monday morning, after the National Human Rights Commission's 33rd Foundation Day, Chief Justice Surya Kant told reporters (New Indian Express; Indian Express, 10:47 AM): "I received a letter yesterday regarding a meeting request, and I responded to it last night, outlining the reasons why I will be unable to meet." He also said: "The Supreme Court's doors are open to everyone. Any petition from any common citizen or member of an elected body is welcome. Every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court, and we will hear their concerns and grant whatever is due under the law." This is his own confirmation. Earlier accounts were from people aware of the matter. In open court, The Hindu's Krishnadas Rajagopal (11:36 AM) reported him saying that democratic and political protests need to take place, but the "Supreme Court should not be dragged into it" and "There should not be any inconvenience caused to litigants, lawyers, court staff." The 4–5 PM slot stays declined. The 1:30 PM march stays on. At the Indira Bhawan press conference (about 12:17–1:30 PM), Rahul Gandhi said the Chief Justice had instructed them to file a petition and that INDIA bloc leaders would go to the Supreme Court to file it, a shift from handing over a memorandum (New Indian Express, NewsDrum, India Today, The Hindu). India Today said the petition was planned for around 3 PM. As of 3:06 PM the filing was not confirmed in the wire copy used here. From about 2:30 PM to 3:05 PM the march was underway. Opposition MPs gathered at the Constitution Club, and a bus carrying Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and others went to the Barakhamba Road junction (PTI video, about 3:03 PM; ANI). The Hindu reported lawyers joining, and police formed a row before Congress protesters at Barakhamba around 2:25 PM. CPI's D. Raja (ANI) said MPs would march, and that inside the Supreme Court 10 leaders would sign the petition and submit it for the INDIA bloc, and that he is a signatory. That is the plan he described, not a report that the petition had been filed. Hindustan Times (about 12:01 PM) quoted CJP co-convener Ashutosh Ranka saying the CJP team "will be there" in solidarity. March coverage as of this check is INDIA-bloc-led. Update, evening of 12 Oct: the petition has been filed. Advocate S. Prasanna, Rahul Gandhi's lawyer, filed it on his behalf because Gandhi could not reach the court by the 4:30 PM physical-filing cut-off (IANS; Prasanna confirmed this to ANI, via the Economic Times, updated 4:56 PM). The legal team had first sought an extension of that 4:30 PM deadline from the Supreme Court registry (India Today, Zee News). India Today's live coverage says the petition is officially registered on the Supreme Court website. The Hindu (Krishnadas Rajagopal, about 5:07 PM) says it seeks an independent committee to inquire into the Special Intensive Revision and the Election Commission's decision-making on it, a re-look at online voter registration and services such as the ECINet portal, and an order calling for the Commission's records and official notings on the revision. The Hindu says the plea is also filed by Mallikarjun Kharge, Trinamool Congress MP Saugata Roy, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and RJD's Tejashwi Prasad Yadav. Earlier, IANS via DNA, citing sources, said the court had agreed to let Gandhi and five to ten leaders, with lawyers, submit the petition at the filing counter outside the high-security area, and that the Chief Justice had agreed to that arrangement. That account is attributed to sources. No hearing date was confirmed in the reports used here. Evening update, as of 9:35 PM: after the 4:37 PM filing, Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders entered the Supreme Court from Gate B. Supreme Court Observer (6:30 PM) reported crowds chanting "Rahul Gandhi Zindabad" as he entered. Bar & Bench (about 7:08 PM, 7:38 PM and 7:55 PM) reported Delhi Police increasing security and trying to stop leaders, a registry that was shut at first, and later a crowd of lawyers and leaders, including Akhilesh Yadav and Supriya Sule, inside the registry. LiveLaw (about 7:24 PM) noted the writ had already been filed. The Hindu (updated 8:52 PM) and Supreme Court Observer: Diary No. 64196/2026, shown as filed at 4:37 p.m. through Advocate Prasanna S. Petitioners: Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Saugata Roy (TMC), Akhilesh Yadav (SP), Tejashwi Prasad Yadav (RJD), Supriya Sule (NCP-SP), Sanjay Raut (Shiv Sena UBT), D. Raja (CPI), Mahua Majhi (JMM), M.A. Baby (CPI-M) and E.T. Mohammed Basheer (IUML). Respondents: the Election Commission of India, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. India Today (updated 8:29 PM) published ten prayers: production of Commission files, notings, objections, ECINET/ERONET logs and the 24 June 2025 nationwide-SIR file; examination under Article 324, Section 18 of the 2023 Act and T.N. Seshan, and quashing of decisions taken without lawful authority; action including under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950; minuting under Section 18 while the case is pending; Form 6 to match the 1960 Rules unless those Rules are amended; an independent committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge to audit deletions and database access and to review EVM practice; booth-wise publication of deletions with reasons and a gender and age breakdown; no deletion without notice and a hearing, with inclusion applications in Punjab and other poll-bound States until the last lawful date; interim suspension of the ongoing SIR; and other consequential orders. That prayer block does not ask for removal of the Chief Election Commissioner. The petition says it does not reopen the validity of SIR after ADR v ECI (27 May 2026). It challenges implementation and collective decision-making. It cites an Indian Express report of 23 September 2026 on objections inside the Commission, and notes the Commission's position that differences are normal and decisions were unanimous. NDTV (updated 6:06 PM) reports that the registry was directed to process the petition and rectify defects so it can be listed on Tuesday, and that a Chief Justice-led bench will likely hear it. NDTV does not name who gave that direction. It is not a published cause-list confirmation. Update, overnight into 13 Oct: IANS (about 11:04 PM), News18 and India TV (11:07 PM; India TV updated 11:47 PM) and DNA report that the registry notified 14 defects in Diary No. 64196/2026 on 12 Oct. The named defects include private individuals listed as respondents without explanation and discrepancies in respondent names; no copy of an earlier judgment annexed; vakalatnamas missing for nine petitioners, all except Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge; an illegible copy of Kharge's identity card; a Rs 220 shortfall in the court fee; and small-font, legibility and printing issues. DNA says the registry also asked for clear copies of the Election Commission's 24 June 2025 Special Intensive Revision decision and related records, and for digital copies on a pen drive. Under the Supreme Court Rules 2013 the defects must be cured before the matter can be listed. India TV says curing them all on Monday is likely to be difficult. Bar & Bench (11:43 PM) says Rahul Gandhi's petition does not figure in the Supreme Court's supplementary cause list for 13 Oct, released at 11:25 PM. Bar & Bench says the bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana is listed that day for CPI(M)'s M.A. Baby PIL, with a tagged contempt plea by Shailendra Mani Tripathi against Govind Mohan and Apoorvanand's plea; Menaka Guruswamy; RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha; the Association for Democratic Reforms; the Supreme Court Bar Association; SCAORA; the Youth Bar Association of India; and pleas by Priya Mishra, Samriddhi Das, who has sought an ex-parte stay, Bhanu Sanoriya, Mukesh Kumar Pandey, Aman Prasad and Anand Kumar Pandey. No report yet says the Gandhi petition's defects have been cured, or that it was mentioned or added to a later list. It could still be mentioned later. NDTV's earlier report that a Tuesday hearing was likely stays NDTV's report. Update, morning of 13 Oct: LiveLaw (8:01 AM and 9:05 AM) says the court will hear today the petitions challenging police and paramilitary action against the Delhi protesters, including allegations of mass illegal detention, assault and arbitrary metro shutdowns, before Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana. LiveLaw lists M.A. Baby of the CPI(M), Professor Apoorvanand, RJD MP Manoj Kumar Jha, Senior Advocate Menaka Guruswamy, the Supreme Court Bar Association, SCAORA and others. That matches the Bar & Bench supplementary list. No outcome yet. The Gandhi petition's absence from that list is unchanged. PTI (7:50 AM) says the registry flagged more than 10 defects in the Gandhi petition. IANS, News18 and India TV said 14. Both counts are kept. Update, by about 12:05 PM: there was no full hearing on the merits, and no order disposing of the protest pleas. Indian Express (about 10:56–10:59 AM) reported that senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan mentioned a journalist's contempt plea, which these reports tie to Amaan Rastogi and the 11 Oct order. Chief Justice Surya Kant said matters can be listed once defects are cured, and "We will take up the matter tomorrow." The bench was the Chief Justice and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana. PTI and The Hindu (about 11:51 AM) and New Indian Express: the Chief Justice assured petitioners that all pleas related to the Delhi protests will be listed, and that they may be listed on Wednesday or Thursday. He said, "Make sure that the defects are cured." Indian Express (about 12:04–12:05 PM): the hearing was adjourned. The Chief Justice said Justice V. Mohana is unwell. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta said the affidavit and compliance report on the contempt notice are ready and that he wants them to be more comprehensive. The court extended the time to file the reply to the contempt notice. The Chief Justice also said listing will happen and that he would like some senior officer to remain present. BJP leader and senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia mentioned the previous day's incident at the Supreme Court, when opposition leaders were at the court. The court asked him to mention it tomorrow. Update, afternoon of 13 Oct: The Hindu and PTI (about 12:48 PM) and ETV Bharat report that the hearing on the Delhi-protest pleas, including detentions and the metro and train curbs, was deferred to Thursday 15 Oct 2026 because Justice V. Mohana was indisposed. The Hindu (about 1:36 PM): the Centre told the court its response on the alleged illegal detentions and the transport shutdown is ready but needs fine-tuning. The bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant extended the time to file that reply to Thursday 15 Oct. ETV Bharat paraphrased the Chief Justice as saying democratic activities must go on smoothly, but without obstructing the court's work or the movement of lawyers, staff and litigants. This Thursday date is for that protest-curbs and detention cluster. It is not a report that Rahul Gandhi's Special Intensive Revision petition was listed for 15 Oct. The defects in that petition still have to be cured.
12 Oct: the BJP Mahila Morcha announced a protest march against the Congress. It says the opposition is giving the protests political patronage (The Hindu, 7:25 PM).

A division bench of Chief Justice Alpesh Kogje and Justice Vivek Jain told the Narmadapuram Superintendent of Police to release or produce 18 people from Goa who were taken off a train at Itarsi. Next hearing Monday 12 Oct (Business Upturn, published 10 Oct, 8:13 AM).

courts.court: Bombay High Court, Goa bench (Azad Maidan detentions)
courts.action: 12 Oct, noon: the Goa bench continues the hearing. The Panaji and Pernem police station in-charges are to file affidavits on the reasons for the detention and on why the peaceful protest was not allowed (The Goan). On Sunday night the bench ordered the activists released. The Goan says they left Panaji police station around 9:40 PM.

courts.court: Supreme Court (SCBA plea on lawyer detentions)
courts.action: Tuesday 13 Oct: the Supreme Court is to hear the Supreme Court Bar Association's petition on detention of lawyers and the internet suspension, and related pleas. Around 11:01 AM the Bar Association mentioned the petition before Chief Justice Surya Kant's bench (LiveLaw). Senior Advocate Nadkarni said a lawyer he represents has also filed (LiveLaw). IANS (11:18 AM): the Bar Association filed the petition and the hearing is tomorrow. PTI, via The Hindu (11:52 AM): a bench of Chief Justice Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana agreed to hear the petitions tomorrow, after Bar Association president Senior Advocate Pradeep Rai raised issues including internet restrictions. The Chief Justice said: "Democratic activities must take place smoothly, but there should be no obstruction to the functioning of the Supreme Court or movement of lawyers, court staff and litigants." PTI, via The Hindu (about 1:54 PM): the Chief Justice also said every lawyer has the right to participate in peaceful protests at designated locations, and the bench agreed to hear pleas against alleged police excesses tomorrow.

Three matters were listed for Tuesday 13 Oct. Justice Amit Mahajan's hearing of the Youth Congress plea for permission to protest at Jantar Mantar began around 11:35–11:39 AM. Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, for Delhi Police, sought time until tomorrow, and the plea was adjourned to 13 Oct (Bar & Bench, 11:40–11:41 AM; LiveLaw, 11:40 AM and 11:48 AM). A plea challenging the closure of Jantar Mantar, saying no alternative site has been earmarked, was mentioned before the Acting Chief Justice's bench around 11:03 AM and listed for 13 Oct (LiveLaw, 11:03 AM; PTI, 11:21 AM; ANI, 11:35 AM). The Hindu (11:19 AM) says the High Court declined to hear it today because the Supreme Court is already seized of the matter. A separate plea alleging harassment of protesters by outsiders on 10 and 11 Oct will also be heard tomorrow (The Hindu). Acting Chief Justice Nitin Sambre agreed to list tomorrow an NSUI plea seeking a special investigation team into violence against protesters on 10 Oct (Bar & Bench, 11:12 AM).

courts.court: Delhi High Court (Mohammad Wasiq Nadeem Khan)
courts.action: About 2:50 PM: PTI, via The Hindu, reported that the Delhi High Court asked city police to file a status report on civil rights activist Mohammad Wasiq Nadeem Khan's allegation that he was illegally detained to stop him attending a peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar. He also alleged constant surveillance and phone calls. A bench of Acting Chief Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Sanjay Sharma issued notice. Orally, the court acknowledged the police power to deny permission for a protest, and questioned entering his house and confining him: "How can you enter the house of this man? ... Where is your cause to confine him?" That is the allegation and the court's question. The status report is still to be filed.

courts.court: Supreme Court (Network of Women in Media, India)
courts.action: Bar & Bench (9:57 PM, 12 Oct): the Network of Women in Media, India has petitioned the Supreme Court over the alleged detention, dragging and manhandling of journalists, including women reporters, covering the anti-CEC protests. The petitioners say police action continued despite the court's direction that journalists not be hindered. They seek binding safeguards and an independent inquiry. That is the petitioners' allegation. No police response was found in this check. No hearing date was reported.

LiveLaw (published 7:40 AM) and Bar & Bench (9:04 AM): the Lawyers' Association for Constitution, convenor Senior Advocate Anjana Prakash, and advocates Fidel Tom, Sumita Hazarika, Anna Oommen and Anne Mathew have moved the Supreme Court under Article 32, through advocate-on-record Pyoli. LiveLaw spells the name Fidel Tom. Earlier cards on this page use Fidal Tom. They allege they were manhandled and illegally detained by Delhi Police on 10 and 11 Oct, and that Fidel Tom was assaulted in custody at Sanjay Colony police station and denied timely legal and medical help. They seek an independent, time-bound, court-monitored inquiry, which Bar & Bench says would be headed by a retired judge, plus preservation of CCTV, disclosure of detention records, mandatory name tags for police, compensation, rulings on the internet suspension, protection of journalists, and binding guidelines for policing peaceful assemblies. They invoke Articles 14, 15, 19, 21 and 22 and the D.K. Basu safeguards. Those are the petitioners' allegations. No police response was found. No hearing date for this petition, separate from today's already listed matters, was reported.

LiveLaw (8:36 AM): journalist Amaan Rastogi, of Moliticis India, has moved the Supreme Court in contempt. He alleges repeated detention by Delhi Police on 10 and 11 Oct despite the court's order protecting journalists, and alleges manhandling, damage to his phone and destruction of his press identity card. Those are his allegations. No police response was found. No separate hearing date was reported. Update, morning of 13 Oct: Indian Express reported that senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan mentioned a journalist's contempt plea before the Chief Justice's bench. These reports tie that mention to this plea and to the 11 Oct order. The Chief Justice said it can be listed once defects are cured, and "We will take up the matter tomorrow."
