By about 12:05 PM the morning hearing had been adjourned, with Justice V. Mohana reported unwell, and the time to reply to the contempt notice was extended (Indian Express). No merits order was reported. Afternoon update: the protest-related sitting was later deferred to Thursday 15 Oct because Justice V. Mohana was indisposed (The Hindu / PTI, about 12:48 PM). These reports do not separately say Rastogi's contempt plea was given its own listing that day, beyond the morning remark that a journalist's contempt plea could be taken up once defects are cured.

courts.court: Delhi High Court (protest SOPs and traders' losses)
courts.action: The Hindu (Soibam Rocky Singh, about 11:10 AM): the Delhi High Court is to hear petitions seeking standard procedures to regulate protests and to limit disruption to businesses and lawyers. Senior Advocate Sachin Puri said recent protests caused losses exceeding Rs 2,000 crore to traders. That is his claim. The court was to hear the matter at the end of the board and was awaiting the Supreme Court's directions on related issues. No order was reported as of 12:15 PM.

caveats: Correction: an earlier update wrongly described Gaurav Bharti as a CJP coverage coordinator and wrongly called his Supreme Court habeas plea a CJP filing. He filed it in his individual capacity. CJP legal cell chief Ratna Singh posted at 12:48 AM that the petition was not filed by CJP, that CJP is not approaching the Supreme Court, and that no habeas corpus petition was approved by CJP's legal team. CJP reposted her post and added "Please note." Bar & Bench and LiveLaw report that Bharti has sought to withdraw the plea. Menaka Guruswamy's separate habeas plea is unaffected.
Detention counts differ a lot by source and time. Official police figures are lower than media and CJP figures. CJP's 10,000+ is unverified.

Most detentions are preventive, not formal arrests. NDTV (~10 PM) says Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Dhruv Rathee were still in custody. Delhi Police sources (ANI, 9:38 PM) said everyone else had been released from detention centres and that CJP leaders would face due legal process. Pinarayi Vijayan, John Brittas and K.N. Balagopal (IANS, 9:20 PM), Mamata Banerjee (ANI, ~8:09 PM), Arvind Kejriwal (PTI, ~8:13 PM), Neha Bora and the women with her (India Today, ~8:30 PM) and Yogendra Yadav (his own post, 9:35 PM) were released. Ratna Singh's status is conflicting reports. No overall release count was given. As of about 10:05 PM IST. As of 11:10 PM IST, CJP says it still has no information on Dipke, Das and Ranka after 12 hours, and they remain detained. Dhruv Rathee remains detained per NDTV (~10 PM); social claims of a release are unverified. Adv Fidal Tom is alleged held at Sanjay Colony police station (Lawyers' Association for Constitution via LiveLaw and Bar & Bench). Senior Advocate Dinesh Dwivedi is detained (LiveLaw; release not reported). Yogendra Yadav says four people at Sanjay Colony police post were beaten and remain held (his claim). Delhi Metro station gates reopened around 10:36 PM (DMRC via IANS). HT (10:47 PM): police say nearly 4,000 people were detained in Delhi. As of 12:15 AM IST, NDTV says Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remained in custody, and that all other detainees among at least 3,000 were released. HT (11:25 PM) says the same four are still held. Social claims that Dhruv Rathee has been released are unverified. Ratna Singh remains conflicting reports. Dinesh Dwivedi has no new report. A Supreme Court habeas plea seeking production of Dipke, Das and Ranka was filed by Gaurav Bharti in his individual capacity, not by CJP. LawBeat alone says it also names Rathee. As of 8:15 AM IST, Dipke, Das, Ranka and Dhruv Rathee remain detained. Ratna Singh says Dipke, Ranka and Das will be produced before an Executive Magistrate at Delhi Cantt Police Station at 9 AM; she cites a police official, and no outlet has confirmed it yet. Police sources via DNA and ET Now say over 7,000 detainees were released. CJP's claim of more than 15,000 is CJP's figure. As of 10:05 AM IST, Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka had been released at about 10 AM on an Executive Magistrate's order, and Dhruv Rathee had been released at about 3 AM. That corrects the 8:15 AM still-in-custody lines and the morning reports from ETV Bharat, ET Now and DNA. The account @CJP_for_India is not the official CJP handle. The official handle is @Cockroachisback. Statements from @CJP_for_India are unverified as CJP statements. As of 12:05 PM IST, the Supreme Court special bench had said it will pass an interim order on the Metro, free movement, the internet and lawyers, and Justice Bagchi was dictating it. The full text was not out. No CJP march or new detentions had been reported. Dipke's mother says he did not attend his grandmother's funeral. As of 2:05 PM IST, Bar & Bench had reported the written interim order: no illegal detention, Metro and rail to run normally, barricades to be reviewed forthwith, internet to stay on as per law, and peaceful assembly allowed outside the Section 163 zone. A contempt notice was issued. The affidavit and compliance report are due Tuesday 13 Oct, when the habeas pleas are also to be heard. After that order, Indian Express reported about 60–70 people detained near Connaught Place and CPI(M) MP John Brittas detained again at about 1 PM. Barricades outside the Supreme Court were being removed at about 1:07 PM. Dipke missed his grandmother's funeral and is travelling home. Das and Ranka were due at a 2 PM press conference. CJP's claims that five more leaders and Vijay Mallangi were detained are unverified. As of 4:05 PM IST, Neha Bora was detained again at about 3:50 PM while leading a march to Connaught Place (ThePrint, Scroll). John Brittas was released after his afternoon detention; CPI(M) alleges police assaulted him and left him injured (ThePrint, India Today). Indian Express reported three of its Hindi reporters detained at Connaught Place, with two phones seized. Police sources, via The Hindu, say over 7,000 people were detained on Saturday. Das, Ranka and Ratna Singh spoke at the Press Club; Ratna Singh is now confirmed released. ThePrint reported police at the Press Club door. PTI later reported that the Press Club notice was in an old case about allegedly morphed photos, following Delhi High Court directions. CJP says it will contest. No fresh detention of Das, Ranka or Singh has been reported. As of 6:10 PM IST, the Supreme Court's written order finds a prima facie case of contempt over the Metro and train shutdown. Notice went to the Home Secretary, the Delhi Police Commissioner and DMRC, per LiveLaw, with replies and a compliance report due on 13 Oct. The order says lawyers and journalists shall not be hindered in any manner whatsoever. Anjali Damania and dozens of others were detained at Shivaji Park in Mumbai, and Scroll reported pickups at Dadar station. The three Indian Express Hindi reporters were released after about 45 minutes. Neha Bora was still reported detained. Delhi Police say a video shows Dipke declining help after his grandmother's death; CJP says he was denied a call. As of 8:10 PM IST, Rahul Gandhi announced that opposition parties, youth and civil-society groups will march to the Supreme Court on Monday 12 Oct and give the Chief Justice a memorandum. Indian Express reported a second evening of detentions at Connaught Place, including many women near Rajiv Chowk Metro Gate 7. AISA's claim that women are sitting in until the men are released is unverified. Dipke missed the funeral. His uncle blames the timing of the release, and police deny a delay. He accuses police of editing their video. Neha Bora and Anjali Damania were still reported detained. As of 10:10 PM IST, Indian Express reported that Monday's INDIA bloc march will start at 1:30 PM from the Connaught Place–Barakhamba junction and go to the Supreme Court. Kharge told reporters, in a PTI report carried by ThePrint, that he and Rahul Gandhi had been given 4 PM to 5 PM to meet Chief Justice Surya Kant and submit a memorandum. That is his account, not a confirmation published by the court. Goa Police stopped a CJP protest at Azad Maidan and detained dozens, including Amreen Shaikh. The Bombay High Court (Goa bench) later confirmed the release of the Panaji detainees, around 9:40 PM. Neha Bora and Anjali Damania were still reported detained. CJP Jharkhand coordinator Khusboo Choudhary told PTI she got off a Ranchi–Delhi train at Bokaro after she says she was followed. Tejashwi Yadav left Patna for Delhi to join the protest (Navbharat Times). Inshorts reported Shyam Meera Singh detained; a release claimed by Neha Bora's team is unverified. The Tribune (updated 9:57 PM) reported Dipke at Nagpur saying he signed no bond against protesting again. That remains in conflict with Ratna Singh's one-year no-breach account. PTI (9:47 PM) says Rahul Gandhi and Kharge have written to the Chief Justice seeking a 4–5 PM meeting on Monday. Ashutosh Ranka said at 10:05 PM that from tomorrow no CJP leader will leave detention without a medico-legal certificate, alleging police brutality. Saurav Das's accusation that police collaborated with sexual assaulters is his claim. DCP Neha Yadav restated the police account that help was offered and that permission was refused over past non-compliance. Bindiya Chari's 9:09 PM post of that Bombay High Court (Goa bench) order was later confirmed by PTI, India Today, Times of India and The Goan. Shyam Meera Singh's release and Neha Bora's lookalike account are from her team and are unverified. Neha Bora's release is unconfirmed. ANI reported Tejashwi Yadav's arrival in Delhi. As of 6:00 AM on 12 Oct, News9, citing people aware of the matter, says Chief Justice Surya Kant declined the 4–5 PM meeting with Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge. K.C. Venugopal says the march to the Supreme Court is still on. CJP says its leaders will go to Parliament Street police station at 10 AM for a Jantar Mantar date, and that Delhi Police have 24 hours to give one. Amreen Shaikh and the Goa group were released around 9:40 PM. Sudhir Sangwan and Balakrishnan Shukla: whereabouts unknown per CJP. No police response found. Neha Bora's release is still unconfirmed. Dipke is in Hingoli. Today: Parliament Street at 10 AM, Bombay High Court (Goa bench) at noon, and the INDIA bloc march at 1:30 PM from Connaught Place–Barakhamba. As of 9:00 AM on 12 Oct, Hindustan Times named four Hindu Raksha Dal associates apprehended over an assault on a minor near Civic Centre. Their account and the police account are both kept. Sudhir Sangwan and Balakrishnan Shukla still have no update since CJP's SOS. John Brittas's account of being choked on a bus is his, via Indian Express. As of 12:10 PM on 12 Oct, Chief Justice Surya Kant confirmed on record that he declined the meeting. Ranka and Das were at Parliament Street police station with a 24-hour ultimatum and no police outcome yet. The Kerala resolution is pending and not reported as passed. Neha Bora's release is still unconfirmed. Sangwan and Shukla still have no update since the SOS. As of 3:06 PM on 12 Oct, Delhi Police had de-notified Jantar Mantar and named three other grounds. The Keralam Assembly resolution has passed and is not binding. The INDIA bloc march toward the Supreme Court was underway. A petition filing was not confirmed in the wire copy used here. Neha Bora's release is still unconfirmed. Sangwan and Shukla still have no update since the SOS. As of 6:15 PM on 12 Oct, the petition had been filed and the march had been stopped at Bhagwan Dass Road. Delhi Police called a viral claim that police fired on the rally and killed five workers a rumour. No outlet reported any firing. Neha Bora was seen on the march. Her exact release time was not reported. Sangwan and Shukla still have no update. Delhi Metro said all stations had reopened at 5:04 PM. The CJP ultimatum still had no police response. As of 9:35 PM on 12 Oct, Rahul Gandhi and other INDIA bloc leaders had entered the Supreme Court from Gate B after the 4:37 PM filing. Diary No. 64196/2026 names eleven petitioners, including Mahua Majhi, and respondents the Election Commission, Gyanesh Kumar, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. Ten published prayers include an interim SIR suspension and a retired-judge audit. They do not ask for the Chief Election Commissioner's removal. NDTV's report of registry processing for a Tuesday listing is not a cause-list confirmation. Dhruv Rathee's "unofficial house arrest" remark is his claim. CJP's 24-hour ultimatum still had no reported police grant of a Jantar Mantar date. As of 6:10 AM on 13 Oct, the registry had flagged 14 defects in Diary No. 64196/2026, and Bar & Bench said the petition was not on the 13 Oct supplementary cause list. NDTV's likely-Tuesday report stays NDTV's report. The BJP allegation that Rahul Gandhi pushed a woman journalist is disputed, and no Congress response was found. A fraud warning posted by @CJP_for_India is not from the official CJP handle @Cockroachisback, and that post is unverified. As of 9:15 AM on 13 Oct, LiveLaw said the Chief Justice-led bench would hear the police-action petitions today. No outcome yet. PTI's "more than 10" defects and the earlier count of 14 are both kept. The Lawyers' Association for Constitution plea and Amaan Rastogi's contempt plea are the petitioners' allegations. Multiple FIRs over Monday's march are attributed to Delhi Police sources. Sri Ganganagar police had said Rajasthan workers were counselled, not detained. As of 12:15 PM on 13 Oct, Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka and Ajinkya Shinde were detained again at Jantar Mantar. No release was reported. Police say entry was through eateries at a de-notified site. CJP says they were inside protesting. The morning Supreme Court hearing was adjourned, with Justice V. Mohana reported unwell. Listing was put at Wednesday or Thursday after defects are cured. That is not a merits order. As of 3:11 PM on 13 Oct, Das, Ranka and Shinde were still detained. The lawyer-denial and phone-confiscation accounts are CJP's. Police were not quoted in reply. Dipke's claim that the three were held separately is his. The Thursday 15 Oct listing is for the protest-curbs and detention cluster, not a report that the Gandhi Special Intensive Revision petition was listed that day. As of 6:10 PM on 13 Oct, Das, Ranka and Shinde were still detained. The kidnapping and lawyer-denial account at 5:52 PM is Dipke's, and he attributes the separate-locations detail to Ratna Singh. Police were not quoted in reply. The Delhi High Court notice is on three prayers in the Youth Congress plea, listed for 17 Nov, not an order granting protest permission. The Thursday 15 Oct Supreme Court date remains the protest-curbs and detention cluster, not a report that the Gandhi Special Intensive Revision petition was listed that day.
Times marked '~' are approximate and come from live-blog timestamps or post times converted to IST.
Dhruv Rathee's housing society is named differently by different outlets.
